areas.area: Home timeline, feed, posts and discovery
areas.summary: This area is the front door. A visitor sees the welcome. A new account gets a short "Get started" list. Home is one timeline (Everyone, Following, Boards, Updates) with votes, a composer that posts to General or a board, live "new posts" handling, notifications and search. Discover and Portfolio ("Your work") are where you find projects and see what you earned. The Home timeline, its new-posts bar and the moderation and error handling are solid and well tested, and most error messages already say what happened and keep the draft. The weak spots are the composer and the suite. The composer puts protocol strings into the text box: picking a mention writes "nostr:npub1…" and adding a picture writes the raw URL. A sticky "share with other apps" switch also copies votes and replies to public servers. On the suite side, the mocked suite runs the build with raises turned on, so the Discover, Start and Portfolio tests mostly check raise-era screens (bids, ETH prices, "Raise money" steps) and leave the contributor-only MVP screens untested. A few labels also clash across screens ("Project board", "communities", "Portfolio"/"Your work").

findings.spec: social-mention.spec.ts › typing straight after choosing a mention goes right behind it
findings.what: Picking "Alice Archer" from the @-list puts `nostr:npub1…` (about 70 characters of code) into the post box. The test locks this in: `toHaveValue(/^hello nostr:npub1\w+ welcome to the room$/)`. The person sees an unreadable key where they picked a name, and every mention uses about 70 of the post's character budget.
findings.why: This shows protocol internals in the main writing surface, which the copy standard rules out. A non-technical person will think something broke, or delete the gibberish and lose the mention. The desktop mention editor already inserts the plain label (docs/mention-editor.md).
findings.suggestion: Show "@Alice Archer" in the box. Keep a map from label to key and turn it into `nostr:npub…` only when the post is published, following the desktop mention contract. Count the label against the character limit, not the URI. Change the spec to expect `hello @Alice Archer welcome to the room` in the box, and `nostr:npub1…` plus a `p` tag in the published event.
findings.verifier: PostComposer.tsx insertMention (around line 213) splices `${mentionUri(pubkey)} ` straight into the text, and social-mention.spec.ts:55 locks in `/^hello nostr:npub1\w+ welcome to the room$/`. `remaining` counts every character of `text`, so each mention uses about 70 characters of the limit. The suggestion is sound. When building it, follow the repo's mention contract in CLAUDE.md: bind each chosen label to its exact key so same-name people don't collide, use the label returned from registration, and make an ambiguous typed name fail visibly instead of fanning out.

findings.spec: feed.spec.ts › posts are only copied to public relays when the author opts in
findings.what: The Home checkbox "Also share with other apps (copies there can't be deleted)" (PostComposer.tsx:521) saves a setting for all future publishes. publishFeedEvent then copies every kind 1, 1111, 6 and 7 event to relay.damus.io and nos.lol. So once someone ticks it for one post, all their later up/down votes, replies and reposts on Home are also copied to public servers for good. Nothing near the vote buttons or reply boxes says so. It also happens on an invite-only server, where short posts have no `h` tag.
findings.why: This is a quiet privacy leak that cannot be undone. The label suggests it affects only this post, while it actually publishes the person's votes and replies permanently on outside servers. Pilot users on a private server would not expect it.
findings.suggestion: For the MVP, hide the checkbox (and the mirror) in the contributor-only build and on invite-only servers. If it stays, make it apply only to the post being written: no saved setting, and never mirror kind 7 or replies made from other boxes. Label it "Also post this publicly outside Creaton (can't be deleted there)". Add a spec that ticks it, then votes on a post, and asserts no public socket opens.
findings.verifier: Confirmed in code. PostComposer.tsx:282 calls writeMirrorSetting(mirror), which saves the choice for every later visit (localStorage `buzz.feed.mirror`). publishFeedEvent (use-feed.ts:285) checks readMirrorSetting() on every feed publish, and isMirrorable (mirror.ts) allows kinds 1, 1111, 6 and 7 when there is no `h` tag. So once the box is ticked, later up/down votes, replies and reposts on Home short posts go to relay.damus.io and nos.lol, and the vote and reply controls say nothing about it. The only spec (feed.spec.ts:414) checks posts only, never votes. The label 'Also share with other apps' is not tied to a single post. The suggestion to scope it to one post (or hide it in the contributor-only build and on invite-only servers) and to add a vote-doesn't-mirror spec holds.

findings.spec: discover.spec.ts (all 5 tests), portfolio.spec.ts, home-checklist.spec.ts › the one door for starting something
findings.what: The mocked smoke suite builds with raises on, so every Discover test checks raise-era UI: "DAOs", "Live launches", "Back this launch", "2 seats · equity map", "Contract · summoner", "Pitch a project". The Start tests check "Raise money" and "Run it together", and the Portfolio tests check bids in ETH. The MVP variants (`raisesOffered()` false) have no mocked test in these files: Discover with "Share an idea" and "Start a project", the Projects/Ideas filters, `discover-start-project`, the idea dialog from `?start=idea`, Start with only "Build with contributors" plus "Other ways to begin", and Portfolio as "Your work" (WaitingOnYou, holdings first, points only when you have them). Only the slower real-server scripts cover them.
findings.why: The screens pilot users will actually see are the least tested, while the suite spends its time on screens the MVP hides. A regression that, for example, shows "Back this launch" or the DAOs section in the hosted build would pass CI.
findings.suggestion: Add a `smoke-mvp` Playwright project built with VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1 (E2E_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY already exists for the screen audit). Add MVP versions of: the Discover directory (Projects/Ideas, the Start a project link, no DAO or launch money words), the Discover empty state ("Start a project"), Start (one contributor card, no numbered steps, no "Raise money") and Portfolio ("Your work" heading, holdings, no backing section). Move the current raise-era Discover, Start and backing tests into a separate `raises` project.
findings.verifier: playwright.config.ts has only the projects smoke, sponsored-op, passkey-wallet and passkey-contributor, all built from one ordinary build. raisesOffered() reads VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY at build time. social-shouldfix-errors.spec.ts:18 says outright that the suite 'cannot switch VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY per test'. The only contributor-only coverage is in tests/e2e-real (screen-audit, social), which needs a real server. So the MVP versions of Discover, Start and Portfolio have no mocked browser test. A second build and project, as suggested, is the right fix.

findings.spec: social-cashtag.spec.ts › a ticker in a post links to the launch that claimed it first
findings.what: useCashtagOwners resolves `$TICKER` against every launch from useLaunches, with no `listedHere`/`raisesOffered` filter (CategoryBrowse.tsx does use listedHere). In the contributor-only build, a `$NEB` in a Home post still becomes a green chip with a price sparkline ("0.5000 ETH") and the label "open for backers. Highest recent bid price 0.5000 ETH per token, not a market trade", linking to a raise this build says it never lists.
findings.why: This breaks the contributor-only promise in contributor-only.ts that the build never describes a project by its money. It puts token prices and a sale invitation on the Home timeline of a no-money pilot.
findings.suggestion: In a contributor-only build, either do not resolve cashtags at all (plain text), or resolve only `listedHere` launches and drop the price, sparkline and stage words about backing. The chip then reads "$NEB: Nebula". Add a spec in the MVP project asserting that `$NEB` has no price text.
findings.verifier: use-cashtags.ts maps tickerOwners over all of useLaunches() with no listedHere/raisesOffered filter. The other surfaces filter (CategoryBrowse, RightRail, PortfolioPage, LaunchesPage). PostContent.tsx:74 renders the chip from this map, and cashtag.ts has the 'open for backers' and '... per token, not a market trade' wording. raises-offered.ts itself notes that a raise published by another build stays readable on the same server, so a contributor-only Home can show a sale price and invitation. Confidence is medium only because it needs such a launch on the server. Filtering with listedHere(record, raisesOffered()) and dropping price words when raises are off is the right fix.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-feed.spec.ts › the Home composer adds a picture, and the post shows it
findings.what:
Adding a picture puts the raw server URL into the text box (the test expects `My new drawing

http://…/media/cdcd…png
`). The person sees a long hash URL instead of their picture. The URL also uses up characters, and deleting part of it breaks the picture without any warning.
findings.why: A non-technical person expects a thumbnail, as in every social app. A wall of hex in the draft looks broken and is easy to damage by accident.
findings.suggestion: For short posts (General), keep attached pictures as separate state shown as thumbnails with a remove button, append the URLs only when publishing, and leave them out of the visible character count. On a board, where the body is Markdown and the picture's position matters, keep the inline insert but show a preview of the picture under the box. Update social-shouldfix-feed.spec.ts to assert the thumbnail is shown and that the published content contains the URL.
findings.verifier: The problem is real. addPicture (PostComposer.tsx:186-200) appends the raw uploaded URL, or `![](url)` on a board, into the text box, and `remaining` counts it. However, the composer serves both short posts and board posts (Markdown, no character limit), and board posts may place a picture inline in the text on purpose.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-feed.spec.ts › a new post waits behind the bar, and Show puts it on top without moving the rest
findings.what: The pill reads "2 new posts. Show" and "Many new posts. Show". A full stop inside a button, with the verb at the end, reads like a sentence fragment.
findings.why: A button should start with what it does. People scan "Show …" faster, and screen readers announce it more naturally.
findings.suggestion: Make the button read "Show 2 new posts", "Show 1 new post", and "Show new posts" when capped (freshLabel plus a "Show " prefix). Keep "2 new posts shown at the top." for the screen-reader note. Update the three spec assertions.

findings.spec: home-timeline.spec.ts › Boards lists every board to join or start; joining writes a join request
findings.what: "Boards are communities for one topic. Their posts show up in Everyone; join the ones you care about." This uses "communities" for boards, while the main nav item "Communities" means servers or workspaces. It also says posts show in Everyone whether or not you join, so it never says what joining does.
findings.why: One word for two different things confuses new people. A Join button with no stated benefit gets ignored, or people assume they must join to see posts.
findings.suggestion: "Boards are places to talk about one topic. Everyone shows posts from every board. Join a board to post there and see what's new on it." Adjust the wording to whatever joining really unlocks (unread counts, posting on private boards).

findings.spec: feed.spec.ts › the founder opens the project's board on its Discussion tab…
findings.what: "Open the project board" means a project's own discussion board here. Discover uses "Project board" for the directory of pitches with open roles (DiscoverPage.tsx:331, the filter label in directory.ts:182, and the header button "Project board" linking to /projects). Same name, two different things.
findings.why: A founder who reads "project board" in both places will look for their discussion in the pitch directory, or the other way round.
findings.suggestion: Call the discussion one "the project's board". Button: "Open a board for {name}". Empty line: "{name} has no board yet. Its founder can open one here. Until then, post about it on Home." Rename the pitch directory "Open roles" (filter, section title and header button).

findings.spec: discover.spec.ts / home-timeline.spec.ts (error paths)
findings.what: The error descriptions sound machine-written or over-explain. Home: "The server did not answer the feed query, so no posts can be shown." Discover (DiscoverPage.tsx:226): "The server didn't answer the directory request. We're not showing an empty list, because that would wrongly suggest there's nothing here." Discover also shows two loading lines at once: "Reading the server…" in the filter row and "Loading the directory…" in the body.
findings.why: "Feed query" and "directory request" are internal terms. The Discover text explains the design decision instead of telling the person what to do. The copy rule says errors should say what happened and what to do next.
findings.suggestion: Home: "Couldn't load posts. Check your connection and try again." Discover: "Couldn't load projects. Check your connection and try again." Keep the server wording under Technical details. Drop "Reading the server…" from the count line and leave it empty while loading.

findings.spec: home-checklist.spec.ts › a new account starts as a helper…
findings.what: The "Look at a project" step counts as done when `signals.lookedAtProject || signals.follows`, and `follows` is true when the person follows anyone. Following one person, with no project page opened, ticks "Look at a project". The module says "a ticked box never lies". Also, "Add your name and a picture" has the hint "The picture is optional.", so the label asks for the picture and the hint takes it back.
findings.why: A wrong tick sends the helper past the one step that shows them what projects need, and it contradicts the checklist's own rule.
findings.suggestion: Split the signal: `look` is done when lookedAtProject is true or followedLaunches is non-empty (this keeps the other-browser reason), not when only people are followed. Update the deliberate unit test at home-steps.test.mjs:72 and add a case where following only a person leaves `look` unticked. Rename the name step to label 'Add your name' with hint 'A picture helps people recognise you.'
findings.verifier: The behaviour is real but deliberate. home-steps.test.mjs:72 has a test named 'following counts as having looked, so the list never asks for a look that obviously happened'. The reason is that lookedAtProject is stored only in this browser, so on a new device someone who follows projects would otherwise be asked to look again. Following only a person, though, does tick 'Look at a project' without any project being seen, which breaks the module's 'a ticked box never lies' rule. The name step's label/hint mismatch is also real.

findings.spec: home-checklist.spec.ts › looking at a project in this browser ticks that box
findings.what: The test pre-seeds `creaton.first-steps` = ["looked-at-project"] in localStorage and checks "2 of 3 done". It never opens a project page, so it does not exercise the code that marks the step (LaunchDiscussion/LaunchDetailPage.tsx:134 `markFirstStep`).
findings.why: Review-proven rule 3: if that markFirstStep call were deleted, the user-facing behaviour would break and this test would still pass.
findings.suggestion: Seed a contributor project, open its page with `page.goto('/launchpad/<id>?author=…')`, go back to Home, and assert "2 of 3 done". Drop the localStorage seed.
findings.verifier: home-checklist.spec.ts:92-100 seeds `creaton.first-steps` = ["looked-at-project"] and only checks the count. No spec opens a project page and checks that the box gets ticked (grep finds the key only in this seed and in start-project.spec's 'project' step). Deleting markFirstStep in LaunchDetailPage.tsx:134 would leave every test green. Note the stale comment there too ('asks a backer'). The suggestion to open a seeded contributor project and then return to Home is right.

findings.spec: feed.spec.ts › votes are trust-weighted: an org admin outweighs a swarm of new keys (on a launch's discussion)
findings.what: The title claims trust weighting, but the test only checks the plain headcount (-4, then -3), and the code comment says trust affects only ranking, which is never checked. Its comment "Posts on Home are liked, not voted; up and down votes live where a team talks about its launch" (line 126) is out of date: Home now has up/down votes on every post (home-timeline.spec.ts:217). The surface it uses, legacy kind-1 "Earlier notes" on a launch's Discussion tab, is read-only history.
findings.why: The test proves less than its name says, the stale comment misleads anyone maintaining it, and it uses a slow raise-era page to test a legacy surface.
findings.suggestion: Rename the test to 'a vote on a project's earlier note counts once and shows at once' and delete the stale comment and the unused org-admin seed. If trust ranking matters, test it at its own seam: a unit test on the ranking code, or a Home Hot-order spec where one trusted up-vote outranks several new-key up-votes.
findings.verifier: The test title claims trust weighting, but the assertions only check the plain headcount (-4, then -3), and the in-test comment admits trust affects only ranking. The comment at feed.spec.ts:126 ('Posts on Home are liked, not voted') is stale: home-timeline.spec.ts:217 votes up/down on Home. One part of the finding is wrong: 'Earlier notes' is not read-only. LaunchDiscussion.tsx says they 'can be read and voted on, but not replied to', so the vote this test makes is a supported action.

findings.spec: home-timeline.spec.ts › Everyone mixes short posts and every board's posts, and New and Top reorder them
findings.what: Hot is Home's default order (`useState<TimelineSort>("hot")`) and the first thing everyone sees, but the test clicks New right away and then checks only the first item under Top/week. Nothing checks that Hot lifts a well-voted post above a newer one, or that it stays newest-first when nothing has votes.
findings.why: A ranking regression in Hot (the default) would ship unnoticed, and it is the most visible behaviour on the product's main page.
findings.suggestion: Before clicking New, assert that the default (Hot) order puts 'Keeping a character steady' first, above the newer, unvoted 'Splitting album royalties'. If the period filter should be covered, first seed a post with created_at older than a day and assert that Top/day leaves it out while Top/week includes it.
findings.verifier: The gap is real: the test clicks New at once, so the default Hot order is never checked in the browser (hotScore is unit-tested in feed.test.mjs, but not the page's default). The first suggestion holds: 'Keeping a character steady' (3h old, 6 up-votes, log10(6)≈0.78) outranks 'Splitting album royalties' (10 min old, 0 votes, a time gap of about 0.23 at HOT_HALF_STEP=45000). The second suggestion is wrong: the seed has no week-old post (the oldest is 3 hours), so 'Top/day leaves out the week-old post' checks nothing.

findings.spec: feed.spec.ts › launches followed in the old browser-only list move into bookmarks once
findings.what: This is a one-time migration from the `buzz.launchpad.followed` localStorage key to a bookmark list, and the test drives it through /launchpad, a raise-era page. The MVP pilot starts fresh, so no pilot browser has the old key.
findings.why: It costs suite time and keeps migration code alive for users who do not exist on the hosted pilot.
findings.suggestion: Remove the LEGACY_KEY migration and this test, or move them to the raises project. Keep "following a launch publishes a bookmark list", but drive it from a Discover contributor-project card instead of /launchpad.
findings.verifier: use-launch-follows.ts carries a one-time migration from the browser-only `buzz.launchpad.followed` list. The hook is still needed (DiscoverCards, LaunchDetailPage, LaunchesPage and use-portfolio import it), but only the LEGACY_KEY/readLegacy/clearLegacy/withMigratedLaunches part is migration. DEPRECATION-2026-10-31.md says nothing about it. A fresh hosted pilot has no such key. Remove the migration and its test together, since keeping the code without its test would break review rule 3, and keep the publish-a-bookmark-list follow test, driven from a Discover card. Impact is low.

findings.spec: home-checklist.spec.ts › the Start button opens the steps in order… / an idea that was published…
findings.what: In the raises build, the Start page's first step is "Set up a place to work": "Channels, AI helpers and pages are set up for you.", with the button "Set up your community" and the note "Create one of your own, or open one you are in. Then press Start a project in its sidebar." The last step's button is "Try it with pretend money". The step titles say "place to work", the button says "community", and the note refers to a sidebar the person cannot see yet.
findings.why: These are the tests the suite spends time on, and their copy mixes three names for one thing and gives directions to UI that is not on screen. If raises come back, this is the first screen a founder reads.
findings.suggestion: Title "Set up a place to work". Body: "Pick a creative or technical project and we set up its channels and pages." Button: "Set up a workspace". Note: "Then choose Start a project." Rename "Try it with pretend money" to "Try a practice project". Since this is raise-era, move these four tests into the raises project (see the MVP test-gap finding).

findings.spec: home-timeline.spec.ts (Home tabs)
findings.what: Home stacks HomeYours (waiting on you), the Get started list or welcome, a composer with "Post to", a "Team update" checkbox and the share-outside checkbox, a Hot/New/Top bar with a period picker, and four tabs (Everyone, Following, Boards, Updates). Boards duplicates what the "Post to" picker and the board pages already offer. The Updates tab's test id is still `social-tab-projects`, and these specs never test that tab. The composer placeholder "What's happening?" is the Twitter prompt, not one for a project community.
findings.why: For people without business experience, the first screen has too many controls before the first post. Each extra tab and checkbox is one more thing to understand.
findings.suggestion: Keep all four tabs. Change the default composer placeholder to something like 'Share an update or ask a question'. Rename the test id to `social-tab-updates` and update dao-os.spec.ts. Remove or scope the share-outside checkbox as in finding 1. If the first screen still feels crowded, hide the Hot/New/Top bar and period picker on the Boards and Updates tabs, where they do nothing, instead of removing a tab.
findings.verifier: Several premises are wrong. Updates is not just posts: ProjectProgressFeed shows the projects' progress reports (kind 47003 with evidence and 'N new to you'), which do not appear in Everyone. It is also tested: dao-os.spec.ts:174, 212 and 264 click `social-tab-projects` and check its content. The old `?tab=projects` links are handled by the TAB_ALIASES in routes/index.tsx. Boards is the only place on Home to browse, join and start boards (home-timeline.spec.ts:411 and 430), so it does not just duplicate the 'Post to' picker, and the finding itself goes on to keep it. What holds: the placeholder "What's happening?" (PostComposer.tsx:81) is generic, the stale test id is confusing, and the share-outside checkbox adds clutter (see finding 1).

areas.area: Boards: posts, ideas, moderation and reports
areas.summary: This area covers what people do on a board: read and sort posts, write posts and nested replies, vote, report someone else's words, and, for owners and moderators, lock, pin, remove, mute, write rules, appoint moderators and handle reports. It also covers the Tasks-page flow that turns a board post into a task and gives its author points once the task is done. Most of it works, the copy is mostly plain, and the specs check what the app sends to the server, not just that a screen loaded. The weak spots: one assertion is silenced and can never fail; an already-claimed credit keeps offering "Claim"; a closed report shows two near-identical buttons; the starter boards still use fundraising words; and notices to people who were moderated don't say which board or post. For a pilot of a few people, appointed-moderator terms plus two-moderator longer mutes are more machinery than anyone needs. Some moderator paths (Lift mute, Remove as moderator, Step down) are shown but never driven by a test.

findings.spec: board.spec.ts › proposal posts have no vote arrows and are not ranked by votes
findings.what: The "Votes never rank a proposal under Top" check is `await expectRows(page, ["Loved proposal", "Ordinary post", "Newest proposal"]).catch(() => undefined);`. The expected order is wrong: board-model.ts:341 scores proposals as 0, so under Top it is Ordinary post, Newest proposal, Loved proposal. The `.catch` hides that failure. The check can never fail, and it costs a full poll timeout (about 5s) on every run.
findings.why: The claim in the test's title, that votes never rank a proposal, is not tested. A regression that let votes rank proposals would pass, and the suite is slower for nothing.
findings.suggestion: Remove the `.catch` and assert the real order: `await expectRows(page, ["Ordinary post", "Newest proposal", "Loved proposal"]);`. That fails if the 4 votes on "Loved proposal" ever move it ahead.
findings.verifier: board-model.ts:341 scores a proposal as 0 under Top, so the order is Ordinary post (score 1 from BOB's vote), then Newest proposal, then Loved proposal. The spec at board.spec.ts:1219 expects [Loved, Ordinary, Newest], which can never match, and `.catch(() => undefined)` swallows the failure after the poll times out. The check is dead weight, and a regression that let votes rank proposals would pass. The suggested order is correct.

findings.spec: board-ideas.spec.ts › a finished task lets its post's author claim, and a second claim is refused
findings.what: After a claim, "Claimed. A reviewer will look at it." is kept only in component state (`filed`). After a reload or on another device, the row shows "Claim 5 points" again, and pressing it gives "This credit has already been claimed." The spec writes this behaviour into the test as expected ("After a reload the button is back, and the server's answer is no").
findings.why: Someone who already claimed sees a button inviting them to claim again, presses it and gets an error. It looks as if their first claim was lost. That is the opposite of reassuring at the moment they are waiting for a reviewer.
findings.suggestion: When Your suggestions loads, read the person's existing finder records (kind 37013, `#d: finderCreditKey(doneRowId)`, which the claim already queries) and show "Claimed · waiting for a reviewer", "Accepted" or "Not accepted" in place of the button. Change the spec so that after a reload it expects the claimed state, not an error.
findings.verifier: BoardIdeas.tsx keeps `filed` only in useState. After a reload the Claim button comes back, and use-task-planning.ts:200-204 already queries 37013 by `#d: finderCreditKey(doneRowId)` and throws "This credit has already been claimed.". The spec (board-ideas.spec.ts:298-305) treats that as the expected result. Reusing the same query on load to show the claimed state is cheap and correct. At minimum show "Claimed, waiting for a reviewer". Accepted or Not accepted only if the review result can be read from the same record's reviewStatus.

findings.spec: board-reports.spec.ts › a moderator is told who decides a report about an equal, and can close one about words already gone
findings.what: For a report about words that are already gone, the row offers both "Close the report" and "Dismiss" (`{ remove: false, close: true, dismiss: true }`). The two buttons sit side by side and do almost the same thing: both close the report and remove nothing. The only difference is the internal action recorded (delete or dismiss).
findings.why: A new moderator can't tell them apart and will hesitate, or guess. The difference only matters to the community's moderators' records, which board moderators never see.
findings.suggestion: Offer one button for gone words, labelled "Close (already removed)", sending action delete. Keep Dismiss only where Remove is also offered. Add a check to the spec that board-report-dismiss is absent on the gone row.
findings.verifier: board-reports.ts:115 returns close and dismiss both true for gone words. BoardReports.tsx shows "Close the report" and "Dismiss" side by side. Both resolve the report and remove nothing, and differ only in the recorded action (delete or dismiss, use-board-reports.ts:215-216). One button for gone words is clearer. A label like "Close (it's already gone)" sending delete is fine, and the spec should assert board-report-dismiss is absent on that row.

findings.spec: board-reports.spec.ts › a moderator is told who decides a report about an equal, and can close one about words already gone
findings.what: "It is about someone of the same or higher standing, so someone above them decides it." The neighbouring sentences have the same tone: "It is about your own words, so someone else decides it." and "It is about a person, not a post: the community's moderators decide it."
findings.why: "Standing" and "someone above them" sound like a rank system the reader never saw, and the sentence doesn't say who to go to. "Your own words" reads oddly next to "post or reply" everywhere else.
findings.suggestion: "Written by another moderator, owner or admin. The board's owner decides this one." / "This is about your own post, so another moderator decides it." / "This is about a person, not a post. The community's moderators decide it."

findings.spec: board-reports.spec.ts › a board's owner sees its open reports, removes a reported post with a reason, and dismisses another
findings.what: The Reports intro reads: "Open reports about posts and replies here. Board moderators don't see who reported. The community's moderators do, and they decide anything more than a removal, such as a ban." The first sentence has no verb. The two kinds of moderator (board and community) arrive with no explanation. Separately, the read error "Couldn't read the reports. Check your connection, then refresh." (use-board-reports.ts:133) sits next to a "Try again" button, not a refresh, and the other read error (use-board-reports.ts:80) shows a status code: "The server didn't send the reports (500)."
findings.why: This is the first thing a newly appointed moderator reads. A status code means nothing to them, and "refresh" sends them to reload the whole page when a button is right there.
findings.suggestion: Intro: "Reports people sent about this board. You won't see who sent them. For anything beyond removing a post, such as a ban, the community's moderators decide." Errors: "Couldn't load the reports. Check your connection and press Try again." and "The server didn't send the reports. Try again in a minute."

findings.spec: board.spec.ts › a community with no boards can add the supporters and founders boards in one click
findings.what: The starter boards come from the raise era: a "supporters" board "for everyone who follows or backs this project", the line "decisions that need a vote are made by the DAO", and a "founders" board whose first post asks "What we can show supporters". The pilot runbook relies on these boards ("starter boards help").
findings.why: The MVP is contributor projects with no raise, so there are no backers. People are contributing work. "Backs this project" and "supporters" suggest money is involved, and "founders" sets a small owner group against everyone else when the pitch is that anyone can contribute.
findings.suggestion: Rename the pair to "community" (open) and "team" (private), or "ideas" and "team". Open-board purpose: "Questions, ideas and updates for everyone following this project. Vote posts up to show what matters." Replace "follows or backs" with "follows or helps with", and "What we can show supporters" with "What we can show everyone else". Update the board.spec.ts assertions at :947 and :962 to match.

findings.spec: board-reports.spec.ts › the author of removed words is told in the notifications, with the reason
findings.what: Notifications say "A moderator removed your post" and "You were muted on a board", with the reason. Neither names the board or the post, and neither says what the person can do if they disagree.
findings.why: The runbook's success test is "whether a moderator's action reads as fair to the person it was taken against". A notice that doesn't say where it happened, or how to object, will read as arbitrary, especially to people who are in several projects.
findings.suggestion: Name the board from the entry's h tag ("A moderator removed your reply in #ideas", "You were muted on #ideas until 8 Nov."). Don't promise a post title the entry doesn't carry. Add a 'think it was a mistake' line only once there is a real place to send it, such as the board owner's profile. Extend moderation-items.test.mjs and the spec to assert the board name.
findings.verifier: The notice does lack the board name. But the post title is not reliably available: the log entry carries only the reason, h, p and thread, and notifications.ts says "A removed post has nothing left to open". There is also no appeal or contact-owner flow to point to. Clicking a board notice already opens the board (boardId is passed), so 'where' is partly covered.

findings.spec: board-moderation.spec.ts › an appointed moderator is told a long mute needs a second moderator, and cannot appoint others
findings.what: An appointed moderator who picks 14 or 30 days sees "Starts as 7 days. Becomes 30 days if another moderator, owner or admin agrees within a day." Another moderator then has to notice the request in the log and press "Confirm until <date>". Moderators also have 30-day terms, 20 actions an hour, and "never act against each other" rules.
findings.why: The pilot is a handful of people on a few boards. A second-moderator confirmation that has to arrive within a day will almost never be met, so the longer options promise something that quietly won't happen. All of it is extra to learn for people new to moderation.
findings.suggestion: For the pilot, filter needsSecond choices out of muteChoices(STANDING.moderator) in the dialog only, keeping the server and log handling so existing entries still render. Update board-moderation.test.mjs:287 and the spec that asserts board-mute-second-*. If the owner wants to keep the feature, show waiting requests at the top of the moderation panel rather than only in the log. Medium-to-low impact.
findings.verifier: The claim that the long options "promise something that quietly won't happen" doesn't hold: MuteDialog.tsx:82-89 says plainly "Starts as 7 days. Becomes 30 days if another moderator… agrees within a day", and the notice is suppressed while it waits. What holds is that the confirm-from-log flow is extra to learn and is rarely met in a small pilot. DEPRECATION-2026-10-31.md makes no decision on it.

findings.spec: board-moderation.spec.ts › a second moderator confirms a longer mute from the log, and the log names and opens the thread
findings.what: A waiting longer mute reads "Ann (moderator) muted Bob on this board until 8 Nov. A longer mute waits for a second moderator. Reason: Insults." The button next to it says "Confirm until 21 Nov" (BoardModerationPanel.tsx:408).
findings.why: The entry never says how long the requested mute is or what confirming does. "Confirm until 21 Nov" without the word mute is ambiguous in a list that also holds locks and removals.
findings.suggestion: "Ann (moderator) muted Bob until 8 Nov and asked for 21 Nov. Another moderator can agree to the longer mute. Reason: Insults." Button: "Agree: mute until 21 Nov".

findings.spec: board-moderation.spec.ts › an appointed moderator is told a long mute needs a second moderator, and cannot appoint others
findings.what: "Step down" ends the reader's own moderator appointment in one click, with no confirmation. Removing someone else as moderator goes through a ConfirmDialog. The reader can't undo stepping down; only an owner can appoint them again.
findings.why: The button sits on the same line as their name in a list of small underlined links. One accidental click silently removes their powers and writes "stepped down" into the public log.
findings.suggestion: Reuse the ConfirmDialog: title "Step down as a moderator?", body "You will no longer be able to lock, pin or remove posts or mute people on this board. Only an owner can appoint you again.", button "Step down".
findings.verifier: BoardModerationPanel.tsx:230-243: Step down calls actions.dismiss(me) directly, while Remove as moderator goes through setRemoving and a confirm. One click is irreversible for the reader, though a toast does show, so it is not silent. Reusing the confirm dialog with the proposed wording is right.

findings.spec: board-ideas.spec.ts › the team turns a board post into a task, with a credit for whoever wrote it
findings.what: Several strings in this flow are awkward. The note posted under the author's post says "If it gets done, you can claim 5 points as its finder." The row button says "Make a task" but the submit button says "Make task" (BoardIdeas.tsx:199). The help text reads "They can claim the credit once the task is done, and a reviewer accepts it. Leave it empty for the usual tenth of the reward." (BoardIdeas.tsx:202).
findings.why: "Finder" is internal vocabulary; the author doesn't think of themselves as a finder. The help text's grammar suggests the reviewer accepts it at the same time as the claim. "Usual" implies a norm nobody told them about. Two labels for one action looks careless.
findings.suggestion: Note: "The team turned this into a task. When it's done, you can claim 5 points for suggesting it." Submit button: "Make a task". Help: "Once the task is done, they can claim these points and a reviewer checks the claim. Leave it empty to give them a tenth of the reward." Update the expected string in the spec.

findings.spec: board-ideas.spec.ts › the team turns a board post into a task, with a credit for whoever wrote it
findings.what: `points()` returns null for anything that is not a positive whole number. Typing "50.5", "fifty" or "-5" in Reward silently creates a task with no reward and no credit for the author, and the success toast still says "Made into a task".
findings.why: A team member believes they offered 50 points. The post's author is told nothing about points, and the task is out there with no reward. Nothing tells them it went wrong.
findings.suggestion: Validate before sending. If Reward or Credit is not empty and `points()` returns null, show "Use a whole number of points, like 50." under the field and don't submit. Add a spec step that types "fifty", expects that message and expects no kind 44011 event.
findings.verifier: points() (BoardIdeas.tsx:41-46) returns null for "50.5", "fifty", "-5" and "0", and submit sends reward null and finderReward null (defaultFinderReward(null) is null) with the success toast "Made into a task". The input has inputMode numeric but no validation. The suggested inline message, with no submit, is right.

findings.spec: board-ideas.spec.ts › the team turns a board post into a task, with a credit for whoever wrote it
findings.what: The spec and UI say "the team turns a board post into a task", but `canEscalatePost` only checks that the viewer isn't the post's author. Any signed-in community member who opens Tasks can turn anyone's post into a task with any point reward and author credit.
findings.why: Two friends can turn each other's posts into tasks with large credits. A reviewer is the only safeguard. And ordinary readers see a "Make a task" button they probably shouldn't be using, which is confusing on a page meant for the project team.
findings.suggestion: Don't invent a team gate just for escalation. Either decide one rule for who may create rewarded tasks (both the Create form and Make a task) and apply it in both places, or keep both open and make the self-dealing risk visible to the reviewer: show who turned the post into a task and the credit size on the finder claim the reviewer accepts. Lower the impact to low or medium.
findings.verifier: canEscalatePost does only check viewer is not the author. But the suggestion's premise, "whatever already gates task creation on the Work board", does not exist: WorkBoard.tsx's Create form is open to any signed-in member, with any reward. Gating escalation alone would be inconsistent, and the reviewer's acceptance of the finder claim is the same safeguard as for any task reward.

findings.spec: board.spec.ts › someone without an account is told to make one, and nothing is written
findings.what: Signed-out readers who press New post, a vote arrow or Report get a toast: "Create your account (top right) to post." On the same board, the thread's reply area instead shows a button that opens sign-up (PostThread.tsx:470).
findings.why: "Top right" is a direction to go and find something. On a 390px screen the account control may not be there, and the toast disappears. The same app already has a one-tap way to open sign-up.
findings.suggestion: Give the toast an action that dispatches SIGN_UP_EVENT: `toast("Make an account to post.", { action: { label: "Create your account", onClick: ... } })`, and drop "(top right)". Update the specs that match the old string.
findings.verifier: needAccountTo() in account-copy.ts:16-18 says "(top right)", but AppNav.tsx:240 mounts ProfileMenu in the bottom tab bar on small screens, so the direction is wrong on mobile, not just vague. SIGN_UP_EVENT already exists and ProfileMenu listens for it in both placements. Note the helper is shared by about 16 call sites (some render it inline, not as a toast), so change the helper's wording and add the action at the toast call sites.

findings.spec: board-moderation.spec.ts › the moderation log reads in plain words, a muted reader is told, and a removed reply is counted in its thread
findings.what: The muted note says "You are muted on this board until {toLocaleString()}. You can still read it, and post everywhere else." toLocaleString includes seconds ("11/5/2026, 3:14:07 PM"). The disabled New post button's tooltip on the same screen uses `whenText` (BoardList.tsx:128), and the log uses "5 Nov 2026". The note gives neither the reason nor anyone to ask. PostThread.tsx:442 repeats the same text.
findings.why: Three date formats for one mute looks machine-made. A muted person's first question is "why, and who do I talk to", and the note answers neither, even though the log has the reason.
findings.suggestion: Use one date format (dateWords or whenText) everywhere: "You're muted on this board until 5 Nov, 3:14 PM. Reason: Repeated insults. You can still read it and post elsewhere. Ask the board's owner if you think this is a mistake."

findings.spec: board.spec.ts › a signed-out reader who presses Report is told to make an account, and nothing is sent
findings.what: The title says the reader "is told to make an account", but the test only checks that the report form did not open and no kind 1984 event was sent. It never checks that a prompt appears. The same gap applies to the report flow at :1333: the two reports are sent, but the success toast "Thanks. The moderators have been told." is never checked.
findings.why: If the prompt broke, the button would do nothing visible and the test would still pass. That silent dead click is exactly the input-path regression the repo's review rules warn about.
findings.suggestion: Add `await expect(page.getByText("Create your account (top right) to report.")).toBeVisible();` (or the new wording) after the click. In the report test, assert the toast once.
findings.verifier: board.spec.ts:1368-1379 only asserts report-form count 0 and no 1984 events, never that a prompt appears. The report test at :1333 never checks the ReportDialog.tsx:66 toast "Thanks. The moderators have been told.". Also the 'nothing sent' check runs immediately after the click, so it doesn't prove much without the visible prompt. Adding both assertions is right, matched to whatever wording finding 13 produces.

findings.spec: board-moderation.spec.ts (missing)
findings.what: No spec presses "Lift mute" (board-log-unmute), "Remove as moderator…" (board-moderator-dismiss plus its confirm), or "Step down". The specs only check that these buttons are absent or visible. There is also no spec for a refused moderation action showing its reason in the panel's role=alert, for example a moderator over the 20-an-hour limit.
findings.why: Undoing a mute and taking powers back are the recovery paths for a moderation mistake. The runbook asks pilot owners to appoint a moderator, and lifting a wrong mute is the first thing they'll need. Repo rule 6 treats a broken recovery path as a functional failure.
findings.suggestion: Add one spec: the owner opens the log, presses Lift mute on an active mute and expects kind 9050 with h and p tags and the toast "Mute lifted."; then removes an appointed moderator through the confirm and expects the kind 9053 event and the row gone; then the server refuses with "rate-limited: …" and the panel shows the plain sentence.
findings.verifier: grep finds board-log-unmute, board-moderator-dismiss and board-moderator-step-down in board-moderation.spec.ts only as toHaveCount(0) or toBeVisible checks (lines 242 and 287). None is ever clicked, and no spec covers a refused action's role=alert text. These are the recovery paths. Check the exact kinds (9050 and 9053) against board-moderation.ts when writing the spec.

findings.spec: board.spec.ts › a reader's own post goes to the top at once and is written the way the desktop reads it / a post made without a heading, as the desktop can, still has a title
findings.what: Two test titles justify their behaviour by the desktop app ("the way the desktop reads it", "as the desktop can"), which is out of the MVP. Separately, board-moderation.spec.ts:300 appoints by pasting a raw 64-hex key into a field whose placeholder says "Their profile link", and :556 asserts only `.toMatch(/^(a1|b2)+$/)`, so it would pass whichever candidate was appointed.
findings.why: Test names are the spec's documentation; tying them to a surface that has been dropped misleads the next reader. The appoint tests don't exercise the path a real owner takes (pasting a profile URL) and don't pin down who got appointed.
findings.suggestion: Rename the two tests as proposed. In the appoint test, fill `https://<host>/u/${BOB}` and keep the exact tags assertion. In the candidate test, either seed a profile and click the chip by its visible name, or keep first() and assert the p tag equals the specific expected key (ANN or BOB per the candidate order) instead of /^(a1|b2)+$/.
findings.verifier: The renames are reasonable: the desktop is out of the MVP, and the real point is a shared title format. parsePersonOrLink accepts `…/u/<key>`, so pasting a profile URL in the appoint test works and better matches the placeholder. But clicking a chip by name ("Appoint Ann") depends on seeded profiles. Chips render `Appoint {nameOf(pubkey)}`, which without a profile falls back to a short key, so that exact locator may not exist.

areas.area: Communities, access, invites, rooms and unread
areas.summary: This area covers how someone joins a community from an invite link, starts a community of their own, and how owners and admins run it: who can join, invite links, roles, removing, banning, muting, editing rooms and boards, what a person is told when they lose access, and unread counts. The flows are well built, and the tests are strong at what they target: signed requests, role gating and server refusals are checked against the real seams, and the error paths keep the server's own words under Technical details. The weak spots are product and copy. The same thing is called "channel" in the sidebar and "room" in the header. The ban form promises "They are told the reason you give", but a banned person cannot read that reason. Bans default to "For good". The fallback errors tell the owner to "ask the community's owner". The create dialog asks "What is it called?" when it is really asking for a web address. On tests, a few specs lock in doubtful behavior (the For good default, a retry button on an expired invite), live-scope.spec.ts tests an AI-helpers view that is outside the MVP, and two unread-queue specs repeat unit tests at the localStorage level.

findings.spec: community-access.spec.ts › the owner can ban a person for a week with a reason, after being told what it means, and the ban is listed
findings.what: The ban form says "{name} will be signed out right away and cannot get back in ... They are told the reason you give." The server sends the reason only as a moderation message inside the same community, and every login by a banned person is refused, so they can never open that message. All they see is "You are banned from this community." (refusal-text.ts:47), with no reason and no end date. The notice also always sends timeout_until: None, so even a 7-day ban never tells them it ends.
findings.why: This is a promise the product does not keep. An owner bans someone for 7 days believing they explained why. The person sees a bare, permanent-sounding ban and has no way to learn why or when it ends. That is exactly the case in which people give up on a community or argue in public.
findings.suggestion: Either deliver the reason and end time where a banned person can read them (include them in the refusal the server already sends, e.g. "blocked: you are banned from this community until <ts>: <reason>", and render that in liveRefusalText), or change the form copy to the truth: "{name} will be signed out right away and can't come back, even with an invite link, until the ban ends or you lift it." Then label the reason field "Reason (only moderators see it)".
findings.verifier: BanPanel.tsx:60-63 promises 'They are told the reason you give.' The relay (moderation_commands.rs:207-220) only sends the reason as a DM opened in the same community (moderation_notices.rs open_dm(tenant.community(), ...)), and with timeout_until: None even when expires_at is set. A banned person can never sign in to read it: auth.rs:109 and api/mod.rs:332 refuse with 'blocked: you are banned from this community', which refusal-text.ts:47 shows as a bare 'You are banned from this community.' with no reason or end. The copy makes a promise the product does not keep.

findings.spec: community-shouldfix.spec.ts › a room shows only its own notes; channel-edit.spec.ts › a chat room's owner edits it from the room's header
findings.what: One thing has two names. The header and cards say "Edit room", "Share this room" and "Link to this room copied", and the refusals say "this room or board". The sidebar says "Channels", "New channel", "Load more channels", "{n} channels · {n} boards" and "Private channel. A member with admin rights has to add you." The timeline notes say "You created this channel" and "archived this channel", the dialogs say "for everyone in this channel", and the create form's placeholder is "What this channel is about".
findings.why: A newcomer meets "channel" in the sidebar and "room" in the header of the same screen and cannot tell whether these are two different things. This is the most visible inconsistency in the area.
findings.suggestion: Use "room" everywhere users can see it: "Rooms", "New room", "Load more rooms", "3 rooms · 2 boards", "Private room. Its owner or an admin has to add you.", "{actor} created this room", "What this room is about", "...for everyone in this room". Update the shouldfix spec's /created this channel/ match to /created this room/.
findings.verifier: The mismatch is real. The header and cards say 'Edit room' (EditChannelDialog.tsx:259) and 'Share this room' (RoomInviteCards.tsx:51), and the refusals say 'this room or board'. The sidebar says 'Channels', 'New channel', 'Load more channels' and 'Private channel. A member with admin rights has to add you.' (ChannelSidebar.tsx:85, 248-252, 302-303). system-notes.ts:127-180 says 'created this channel', 'archived this channel' and so on. ChannelTimeline.tsx:873/963/976 and the CreateChannelDialog placeholder 'What this channel is about' use 'channel' too. The DEPRECATION doc already talks about 'rooms'. Changing only the strings users see, and leaving testids and identifiers alone, is low risk.

findings.spec: community-access.spec.ts › when the server refuses the change / when the server will not change a role / ... will not ban / will not lift a ban / will not end a mute
findings.what: The fallback errors end with "Try again, or ask the community's owner." AccessControl and role changes are offered only to the owner, so the owner is told to ask themselves. The whole family also sounds machine-made: "The server did not change who can join, so it is as it was.", "The server did not remove them, so they are still here.", "The server did not lift the ban, so it is still in place."
findings.why: Telling the owner to ask the owner is a dead end. The "The server did not X, so Y" pattern is the machine-sounding voice the copy standard rules out.
findings.suggestion: Plain words, with no "ask the owner" on owner-only actions: "Couldn't change who can join. Nothing changed. Try again in a moment." / "Couldn't change their role. Try again in a moment." / "Couldn't remove {name}. They're still here. Try again in a moment." / "Couldn't ban {name}. Try again in a moment." / "Couldn't lift the ban. It's still in place. Try again in a moment." / "Couldn't end the mute. Try again in a moment." Keep "or ask the community's owner" only when myRole is admin. Update the exact-text assertions in community-access.spec.ts.

findings.spec: community-access.spec.ts › a ban that is for good sends no end time, and can be lifted
findings.what: The ban length defaults to index 0, "For good". The harshest option is what one press of "Ban {name}" does, and the spec locks this in by pressing ban-yes with no choice made.
findings.why: Most bans by first-time community owners should be cool-downs. A permanent default turns a hasty click into a permanent exclusion, and the banned person cannot even see why (see the ban-reason finding).
findings.suggestion: Make no length preselected: show a 'Choose how long' placeholder and keep 'Ban {name}' disabled until a length is picked. Order the lengths 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, For good. Change the For-good spec to selectOption({ label: 'For good' }) explicitly, and add a check that the button stays disabled until a length is chosen.
findings.verifier: Real: useState(0) together with BAN_LENGTHS[0] = 'For good' means one press of ban-yes bans for good, and the spec at community-access.spec.ts:761-783 relies on that. Two things argue against making 7 days the default. Bans are often for spammers, where 'for good' is right. And a person can already be muted everywhere with an end time (the timeouts/MutedList), so that is the cool-down tool. Forcing a choice avoids both a harsh default and one that is too soft.

findings.spec: invite-join.spec.ts › an invite that cannot be used says why in words, and the person stays on the page with an account to try again
findings.what: After "This invite has expired. Ask for a new invite." (also for invite_exhausted and invite_invalid), the page offers an enabled "Join in browser" button, and the spec asserts that it is enabled. Pressing it can only fail again. Meanwhile the person has just been given a nameless account, and the name they typed was never saved.
findings.why: A retry button on a dead link wastes the person's next click. They now hold an account but have no place to go and no next step apart from asking.
findings.suggestion: For the three terminal invite codes, mark the problem as terminal in inviteProblem (for example a `final: true` flag). Hide the join button and show 'Ask whoever sent it for a new link' plus a 'Go to Creaton' link to Home. Keep retry for network, timeout and terms problems. Do not try to publish the name before a successful join. Change the spec to expect no join button and a Home link after invite_expired.
findings.verifier: The dead retry is real. After invite_expired, invite_exhausted or invite_invalid the code is fixed in the URL, so 'Join in browser' can only fail again, and the spec asserts that it is enabled. But 'the name they typed was never saved' is not a loss: newName stays in state, and joinInBrowser passes it to claimAndJoin. Saving it 'right away' would also be refused, because claimAndJoin saves the profile after the claim on purpose ('a private community would refuse a profile from a stranger'). So the fix is about the next step, not about the name.

findings.spec: invite-join.spec.ts › someone with an account sees the usual button and is not asked to make another
findings.what: The button says "Join in browser". This build is the web app only (DESKTOP_APP is off), so "in browser" points to an alternative that doesn't exist. The no-account label reads "No account yet? Pick a name and we will make one in this browser."
findings.why: "in browser" is left over from the desktop era and makes people wonder whether there is another way they should join.
findings.suggestion: "Join" (or "Join {community}") when DESKTOP_APP is off. Label: "New here? Pick a name and we'll make your account." Update the spec's getByRole name.

findings.spec: community-create.spec.ts › a server that offers it shows the button, tidies the name and previews the address
findings.what: The field is labelled "What is it called?", but whatever is typed is rewritten as it is typed ("My Film Crew!" becomes "my-film-crew") because it is really the web address. The hint says "Its address will be your name followed by example.test, like my-film.example.test." Here "your name" reads as the person's own name.
findings.why: Someone without technical experience who names their community "My Film Crew" watches their typing change under them, and their community ends up shown as "my-film-crew". It is confusing in the moment, and the result looks unfinished.
findings.suggestion: Either ask for a display name and derive the address from it (shown and editable underneath), or be honest in one field: label "Pick its web address", hint "It will live at {name}.{domain}" (empty state: "Letters, numbers and hyphens, like my-film.{domain}").
findings.verifier: CreateCommunityDialog.tsx:86-108 labels the field 'What is it called?', but onChange runs tidyName, which lowercases, turns spaces into hyphens and drops other characters as the person types. The empty hint reads 'Its address will be your name followed by {domain}', where 'your name' sounds like the person's own name. Both problems are real. The single honest-field option ('Pick its web address' plus a hint showing the full address) is the smaller change.

findings.spec: community-create.spec.ts › a new community is open by default; community-access.spec.ts › closing a community warns that strangers are signed out
findings.what: The open choice is titled "Anyone with the address", but its own detail says the community can show up in the public list, so you don't need the address to find it. The closing warning, "People who are not on the list will be signed out right away. Members stay.", refers to a "list" the owner has never seen.
findings.why: The title understates how public an open community is. "The list" is internal vocabulary.
findings.suggestion: Title: "Open to anyone". Detail: "Anyone can find it, read it and join. Good for a public community." Invite-only detail: "Only people you send an invite link can come in or read anything. Good for a team." Closing warning: "People who haven't joined will lose access right away. Members keep theirs."

findings.spec: community-access.spec.ts › the owner can make a member an admin and an admin a member
findings.what: "Make admin" takes effect on one click, with no confirmation and no note on what an admin can do (remove and ban members, make invite links). The reverse button reads "Make member".
findings.why: Remove and Ban get warnings, but the action that hands out those same powers does not. A misclick on a crowded row (Make admin, Remove and Ban side by side) gives a stranger moderation powers. "Make member" reads as if they were not a member before.
findings.suggestion: Rename the reverse action to 'Remove admin'. After 'Make admin', show a toast like '{name} is now an admin: they can invite, remove and ban people.' with an Undo action, or add that sentence as the button's title. Add an inline confirmation only if the owner wants one.
findings.verifier: Real: 'Make admin' (PeopleSection.tsx:429-438) runs giveRole on one click and sits beside Remove and Ban, and 'Make member' is unclear. But the change undoes itself with one click, and the role badge updates on the row, so a full confirmation step adds friction to a reversible action where Remove and Ban are not reversible. A short explanation solves the problem more cheaply.

findings.spec: community-access.spec.ts › the owner sees the current setting, and everyone in the community
findings.what: When the member list is empty or cannot be read, the page shows "The list of people is not available here."
findings.why: This doesn't say what happened or what to do, and "here" suggests the list exists somewhere else.
findings.suggestion: "Couldn't load who's in this community. Try again in a moment." Offer a retry, and add a spec for the empty or failed list.

findings.spec: access-refused.spec.ts › a ban arriving while a chat room is open says so under the room's header
findings.what: The tooltip on the Reconnecting chip reads "Live updates from the server have stopped; the client keeps retrying." The removed-from-board message reads "You no longer have access to this room or board." with no next step.
findings.why: "the client" is developer vocabulary. The removal message breaks the house rule that a refusal says what to do next. NO_ACCESS_TEXT right below it already does: "Its owner can add you."
findings.suggestion: Tooltip: "Lost touch with the server. Trying again…". Removal: "You no longer have access to this room or board. Ask its owner if you think this is a mistake."

findings.spec: live-scope.spec.ts › a task tied to a room arrives live in the agents view
findings.what: The only test in this file opens fleet-toggle ("AI helpers"). That view exists only when beyondContributorProjects() is true, so it is out of the MVP and absent from the VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY pilot build.
findings.why: The rule it guards (a view that follows records which may or may not be tied to a room needs both kinds of subscription) still matters for the MVP. Here it is proven only on a screen the pilot never shows, so the MVP path is unguarded and the suite pays to keep a raise-era screen working.
findings.suggestion: Retarget the test to the Tasks view (work-toggle), which ships in the contributor-only build: deliver the room-tied task and assert that it appears there. Then drop the fleet version, or move it to a raise-build-only project.
findings.verifier: fleet-toggle is rendered only when helpers = beyondContributorProjects() (CommunityShell.tsx:192, 466-482), so the contributor-only pilot never shows it. The Tasks view (work-toggle, outside that gate) renders WorkBoard, whose useWorkBoard (use-work-board.ts:306-320) uses the same liveFiltersFor({kinds:[KIND_AGENT_TASK]}, channelIds) per-room subscription rule. Pointing the test at work-toggle guards the same rule on a screen the MVP actually shows.

findings.spec: community-access.spec.ts › the owner sees the current setting / a ban that is for good ...; invite-join.spec.ts › a name is optional
findings.what: Several "nothing happened" assertions rest on fixed waits (waitForTimeout(300) and (500)) before checking that a list is empty, so they pass whenever the request is merely slower than the wait. The For-good ban spec presses ban-yes without choosing a length, so it pins the default rather than the For-good behavior its title names.
findings.why: These tests cannot catch a late request, so they only look falsifiable. The ban spec would block the safer default proposed above for the wrong reason.
findings.suggestion: In the For-good ban spec, selectOption({ label: 'For good' }) explicitly. Remove the needless waitForTimeout(300) in invite-join (the URL wait already orders it). Leave the member-no-invites-request check as it is.
findings.verifier: Only the ban part holds: the For-good spec (community-access.spec.ts:761-783) presses ban-yes without choosing a length, so it pins the default. The fixed-wait claims are weaker than stated. In invite-join.spec.ts:121-130, claimAndJoin awaits saveNewProfile before window.location.assign, so any profile publish would happen before waitForURL resolves, and the 300ms wait is extra rather than load-bearing. community-access.spec.ts:529 already waits for a positive signal (three person rows) before its 500ms negative check, which is a normal way to assert that something did not happen.

findings.spec: (none) invite-join.spec.ts / community-access.spec.ts
findings.what: Several real paths have no mocked spec: joining through the server's terms (loading, failure with "Try again", the tick-boxes, and the TERMS_CHANGED retry); the invite-page path "Create with a passkey" ending in the recovery-key dialog; and the full owner loop of making a link, copying it and opening it as a new person (the copy toast "Link copied." and the fallback "Could not copy..." are untested).
findings.why: These are the first-minute paths for every pilot participant. Terms changing between page load and join already has dedicated error code (reloadTerms) that no browser test exercises.
findings.suggestion: Add one community-access spec: the owner makes a link and copies it, with clipboard permission granted, and sees 'Link copied.'. Then a second browser context opens the copied URL and joins (the claim reaches the mock). Optionally, deny clipboard access and assert the 'Could not copy' fallback that shows the link. Do not duplicate the terms and passkey specs.
findings.verifier: Most of the named gaps are already covered in social-shouldfix-signup.spec.ts. Line 85 makes a passkey account on the invite page, joins and is offered the recovery key. Line 259 covers terms that could not be loaded, with Try again, and terms that changed and need a new tick. The PeopleSection invite maker's copy feedback ('Link copied.' or 'Could not copy...') and the full owner-makes-link, newcomer-opens-it loop do lack a spec.

findings.spec: community-create.spec.ts › the two choices sit side by side on a desktop
findings.what: A test whose only job is a bounding-box check that two radio cards share a row at desktop width.
findings.why: It pins a layout choice, not behavior, and costs a full page boot. The phone test next to it already covers the layout case that can actually break (stacking, no sideways scroll, submit reachable).
findings.suggestion: Delete it, or fold the one assertion into the phone-fit test as a desktop or phone pair in a single page load.
findings.verifier: community-create.spec.ts:148-156 only compares the bounding boxes of the two access cards, which pins the sm:grid-cols-2 layout, and it boots a whole page to do so. Folding it into the phone-fit test as one desktop-then-phone viewport check, or deleting it, loses nothing behavioral.

findings.spec: community-shouldfix.spec.ts › community search finds a board post and opens it
findings.what: The search box placeholder says "Search messages…", but it also finds board posts, which the spec checks. Separately, nameProblem has a branch that can never run, with copy no one can read: "Pick a name that does not have hyphens as its third and fourth characters." tidyName already collapses "--" to "-", so a name can never reach it.
findings.why: The placeholder undersells what search finds. The dead branch is unreachable copy that a later change could resurface as nonsense.
findings.suggestion: Placeholder: "Search this community…". Delete the unreachable hyphen branch, or, if the server's rule must be mirrored, word it as "Names can't start with two letters followed by two hyphens."

areas.area: Messages, safety, muting, removal and reports
areas.summary: This area covers private messages (Home's Messages, plus the community panel, which is "Private chats" in the full build and "Notices" in the pilot), personal mute, reporting messages, posts and people, the moderators' report queue, ban and time-out, removing messages in rooms and on boards, and the server's notes in rooms. The basics are solid and well tested: reports always need a reason, server words go under Technical details, nothing is sent on Cancel, and mute is applied on boards, in rooms and in notifications. The biggest problems are about trust. The mute list is public, so the person you muted can see it. "Escalate" promises a hand-off that nobody receives. A ban from the queue skips the length and reason that a ban from a message asks for. And a ban that worked can be reported as a failure. On copy, the word "mute" means two different things, room notes say "channel" where the rest of the app says "room", and the queue uses different reason names than the report dialog. The suite runs only the full build, so the pilot's Notices panel is never exercised. Removing a report and dismissing one have no browser test, and neither does muting on the Home timeline. A few steps are slow or prove nothing (one swallowed 20-second assertion, fixed sleeps), and the "shouldfix" files are grab-bags.

findings.spec: social-safety.spec.ts: a conversation can be reported, and muting it takes it out of the inbox until they are unmuted
findings.what: Muting writes the muted person's key as a plain, public tag in your mute list. The file's own comment calls it a "public NIP-51 list", and the test checks for that public tag. Bookmarks in the same file are stored privately (NIP-44 in the content), but mutes are not. Nothing on screen tells the user. A person who mutes a harasser is publicly showing that they did, and the harasser can see it.
findings.why: People mute in order to quietly step away from someone. A public mute list can provoke the very person they are avoiding, and on a small pilot server everyone can read it. This is a safety and privacy problem, not a style issue.
findings.suggestion: Store muted people privately, the same way readBookmarkState and the bookmark writer store bookmarks: tags encrypted with NIP-44 in the content, and still read any old public tags so existing mutes keep working. Then change the test to check that the published event has no public p tag for ALICE and that the encrypted content contains her. Until that ships, add one line under the Mute button: "Others can see who you muted."
findings.verifier: use-social-actions.ts writes the kind 10000 mute list through withMuted() as public p tags (the section header even says "public NIP-51 list"), while bookmarks below are NIP-44 private. On the relay, 10000 is not in AUTHOR_ONLY_KINDS (buzz-core kind.rs:184) and is not otherwise gated, so any member can read someone's mute list, including by #p. Nothing on screen says so. The suggested fix (private tags in NIP-44 content, still reading old public tags, and a test that the published event has no public p tag) holds. Note that e2e-real/social.spec.ts:581-596 also reads the public tag and would need updating.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-moderation.spec.ts: an escalated report stays in view with its status, the Escalated filter reads escalated ones, and Show older reads further back
findings.what: "Escalate" marks a report and then shows "Passed on to the people who run this server." Nothing reads escalated reports except this same queue's Escalated filter (grep finds them only in web/src/features/moderation and fleet/BoardIdeas). buzz-admin has no escalation view, and the pilot runbook never mentions escalation.
findings.why: The app promises a hand-off that nobody receives. A moderator who escalates a threat or something illegal believes someone else now owns it, so the report is effectively dropped, which is the swallowed-failure pattern from rule 1. Small teams without moderation experience will take that line literally.
findings.suggestion: Keep the relay backstop. For the pilot, either hide Escalate and the Escalated filter behind the non-contributor-only build, or give the operator a real receiver before the pilot: a `buzz-admin reports --escalated` command that calls the existing admin listing, plus a runbook line saying who checks it and how often. Until one of those exists, change the status line to say plainly that no one has picked it up yet (for example "Marked for the server's owner. Nobody has picked it up yet.") instead of "Passed on to the people who run this server."
findings.verifier: "Nothing reads escalated reports" overstates it. The relay's operator API, GET /api/admin/v1/reports (crates/buzz-relay/src/api/admin/mod.rs:216-223), shows escalated reports by default, as the moderation vision intends. The only client for it is the desktop admin console (desktop/src/features/admin-console/api.ts), and the desktop app is out of MVP scope. buzz-admin has no command for it and PILOT-RUNBOOK never mentions escalation. So in the pilot the hand-off really does land with nobody unless the operator curls a NIP-98 API, and the copy promises more than the pilot delivers.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-review.spec.ts: a queue action the server could not apply says so plainly, never its internal error
findings.what: Ban, time-out and remove are published first, and the report resolution is published separately afterwards. If the ban is accepted but the resolution is refused or times out, the row says "Couldn’t apply the action. Try again. The report stays open. Use the buttons above to try again." The ban has actually taken effect.
findings.why: Two writes for one user action leave a torn state (rule 5), and the message is wrong. The moderator believes the person is not banned and bans them again, or goes to the server owner about a failure that never happened.
findings.suggestion: Catch a failure of the resolution step on its own, after the enforcement has succeeded, and say what happened: "Carol Ng is banned, but the report couldn't be closed. Close it with Dismiss." Add a test with a mock that accepts kind 9040 and refuses 9044, and check that wording.
findings.verifier: use-moderation-queue.ts:310-354 publishes the enforcement (ban, timeout or delete) and then, separately, buildResolveReport. Any refusal of the resolve step, other than the Home-delete "report is not open" case, is rethrown into the generic FAILED message even though the ban or timeout already took effect. That is the torn two-write state rule 5 describes, and the wording is false. The suggested fix (catch the resolve failure separately, name what did apply and how to close the report, and add a mock that accepts 9040 and refuses 9044) is right.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-moderation.spec.ts: a ban from the queue names the person, and a timeout says whom it is for
findings.what: There are two bans that work differently. A ban from a message (BanForm) asks "How long" and for a reason the person will see, and says "{name} will be signed out right away and cannot get back in, even with an invite link". A ban from the queue is a plain confirm, always permanent and never with a reason (buildBan({ pubkey: person })), and it says "Carol Ng can no longer post in this community. You can lift the ban later."
findings.why: The queue is where moderators handle bad actors, but from there they can only ban for good and without a reason. The two screens also describe what a ban does differently ("can no longer post" against "signed out and cannot get back in"), so moderators can't tell which is true.
findings.suggestion: Use BanForm (length plus reason) inside the queue row instead of ConfirmDialog, and pass expiresAt and reason through perform(). Keep one description of a ban everywhere: "{name} is signed out and can't come back, even with an invite link, until the ban ends or you lift it. They see your reason."
findings.verifier: In ModerationQueuePanel.tsx:272-284 the queue ban is a ConfirmDialog with "can no longer post in this community", and perform() calls buildBan({ pubkey: person }) with no expiresAt or reason, even though buildBan (moderationEvents.ts:66) supports both. BanForm (communities/ui/BanPanel.tsx:24) has length and reason and says the person is signed out and can't come back. Two inconsistent descriptions of one action, and the queue can only ban permanently with no reason. Reusing BanForm and passing options through perform() is straightforward.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-moderation.spec.ts: a ban from the queue names the person, and a timeout says whom it is for; social-shouldfix-review.spec.ts: a wiki rename that saved the new page but could not delete the old one
findings.what: "Mute" means two opposite things. A personal mute ("You muted Bob", "Hidden: 1 conversation with people you muted") hides someone from me. A moderator sanction is also called mute: "Mute everywhere…", "Mute Alice Reyes everywhere in this community for". The person sanctioned is told "You are muted everywhere in this community until …", and BanPanel says "End mute".
findings.why: Someone who was put in a moderator time-out reads "you are muted" and may think another user just muted them. A moderator can't tell whether "Mute everywhere" only hides the person or stops them posting.
findings.suggestion: Keep "mute" for the personal action only. Call the sanction a pause on posting: the action "Pause posting…", the legend "Pause Alice Reyes's posting in this community for", the refusal "A moderator paused your posting here until {when}. You can still read.", and in BanPanel "Paused" / "End pause".

findings.spec: report.spec.ts: when the server will not take the report, its words are shown and the form stays open
findings.what: Any "invalid:" refusal is shown as main copy. The test expects "Report target event not found.", and the same rule would show "Report must include exactly one p tag." or "Unsupported report type: phishing." (crates/buzz-relay/src/handlers/report.rs:59-207).
findings.why: This is protocol language in the main copy ("target event", "p tag"), and it doesn't say what to do next, which goes against both copy rules. The test locks in the bad wording.
findings.suggestion: Map report refusals in refusal-text.ts. For "report target event not found": "That message is no longer here, so it can't be reported.
