If it's still a problem, report the person instead." Everything else: "Your report was not sent. Your note is still here. Try again." (the dialog's own fallback). Update the test.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-moderation.spec.ts: each queue row shows the reported words or person…
findings.what: Reasons are named differently on each side. The reporter picks "Abuse or hateful language", "Spam or a scam", "A harmful link or file", "Sexual content", "Pretending to be someone else" (lib/report.ts:32-66). The moderator sees "Profanity", "Spam", "Malware", "Nudity", "Impersonation".
findings.why: A threat reported as "Abuse or hateful language" shows up as "Profanity" and looks minor. The queue also uses jargon ("Malware") that the reporter never saw.
findings.suggestion: Make REPORT_TYPE_LABEL use REPORT_REASONS[].label so both sides share one list: "Abuse or hateful language", "Spam or a scam", "A harmful link or file", "Sexual content", "Pretending to be someone else", "Something illegal", "Something else".

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-moderation.spec.ts: appointing a board moderator from the buttons asks first, naming them; the box takes a profile link
findings.what: A moderator appointed with a candidate button gets a confirm that names them ("Make Alice Reyes a moderator of this board?"). One appointed by pasting a link into "Their profile link" is appointed at once, without ever being named on screen. The test checks that this path sends kind 9052 with no confirm.
findings.why: The pointer and paste paths behave differently (rule 8). A wrong or old link gives moderator powers to a stranger for 30 days, and the owner never sees who it was. Pasting links is also a technical step that newcomers struggle with.
findings.suggestion: Send the link path through AppointDialog as well (setConfirming(pubkey) after parsing). Better still, replace the link box with the same "Search by name" PersonSearch that New chat uses. Extend the test so the link path also opens "Make Carol Ng a moderator of this board?" and sends nothing on Cancel.
findings.verifier: BoardModerationPanel.tsx:158-166: appoint() parses the pasted link and calls actions.appoint immediately, never naming the person, while the candidate buttons go through a named confirm. This is a real modality divergence (rule 8) on a 30-day power grant. Sending the parsed pubkey through the same confirm (setConfirming) is the minimal fix. Replacing the box with name search is a good optional follow-up.

findings.spec: room-notes.spec.ts: a new private room's notes read as sentences with names; chat-removal.spec.ts: removing asks first…
findings.what: Room notes and dialogs say "channel" ("Board Tester created this channel", "joined the channel", "It is taken away for everyone in this channel.", "The message is replaced with a deletion marker for everyone in this channel."). Everywhere else people see "room" ("in any room or board here", "You don't have access to this room or board"). The removed marker is lowercase "message removed by a moderator", while boards say "A moderator removed this post."
findings.why: Two names for the same place, and "deletion marker" and "taken away" sound like a machine wrote them.
findings.suggestion: Replace "channel" with "room" in system-notes.ts ("created this room", "joined the room", "left the room"). Delete confirm: "It will show as 'Message deleted' for everyone in this room." Remove confirm: "It disappears for everyone in this room. The person can still post. To keep them out, use Ban." Markers: "Removed by a moderator." / "Message deleted."

findings.spec: room-notes.spec.ts: a thread the server opened itself (its moderation notices) is listed under Messages too
findings.what: Moderation notices come from a sender named after the server's host: "localhost:3001 Moderation" (in production something like "alpha.example.com Moderation"). The thread then says "Only the people who run this community write here. To answer, use Messages on Home." It doesn't say who to message.
findings.why: A hostname isn't a name people recognise. Someone whose post was removed wants to reply or appeal, and is sent to an inbox with nobody named to write to.
findings.suggestion: Name the sender after the community: "{community name} moderators". Change the footer to "Only this community's moderators write here. To ask about a notice, message the owner, {owner name}." and link to the owner's conversation.

findings.spec: chat-removal.spec.ts: removing asks first, sends one removal for that message…
findings.what: Removing a room message is a bare confirm with no reason. Removing from a board or from the queue uses ReasonDialog, and the author is told the reason ("Its author is told, with your reason").
findings.why: The same moderator action behaves differently by place. In rooms the author's message vanishes with no explanation, which reads as arbitrary and pushes newcomers away.
findings.suggestion: Use ReasonDialog for room removal too, with an optional public reason sent on the 9005. The "message_deleted" note in system-notes.ts already shows "Removed by community moderators: {reason}" when one is given.
findings.verifier: ChannelTimeline.tsx:970-985 uses a bare ConfirmDialog, and removeMessage calls moderation.remove(eventId) with no reason, while board and queue removal use ReasonDialog. system-notes.ts:170-175 already renders "Removed by community moderators: {reason}" when a public reason is present, so the display side is ready. The fix needs moderation.remove to accept and send the reason. Low impact as stated.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-messages.spec.ts: Messages does not offer other apps a way in on an invite-only server
findings.what: On an open server, the Messages page shows a banner: "Let people using other apps message you here. This posts a public note saying where to reach you." [Turn on]. The signed-out empty state says "Messages are end-to-end encrypted with your key."
findings.why: Pilot users don't know what "other apps" means. The banner asks them to publish something public on the first screen of their inbox, and "with your key" is jargon. The MVP is about contributors talking to each other, not Nostr interop.
findings.suggestion: Keep the banner, which is already off on the invite-only pilot. Change the signed-out empty state to "Only you and the person you write to can read your messages." Optionally reword the banner for open servers to drop "other apps" vagueness, for example "Let people on other Nostr apps write to you here. This shares, publicly, where to reach you." Keep the invite-only negative test as is.
findings.verifier: The pilot server is invite-only (PILOT-RUNBOOK.md:12, 90: BUZZ_REQUIRE_RELAY_MEMBERSHIP=true), and ReceiveFromOtherAppsBanner already returns null on invite-only servers (MessagesPage.tsx:58-60). Pilot users never see the banner, so removing it buys nothing for the MVP and loses a working open-server feature plus its test. The signed-out empty-state copy "end-to-end encrypted with your key" is real jargon and is shown in the pilot.

findings.spec: social-safety.spec.ts: a conversation can be reported, and muting it takes it out of the inbox until they are unmuted
findings.what: Muting is an icon-only button with the label "Mute" (no name) and the toast "Muted", and it says nothing about what muting does. Afterwards the inbox only says "Hidden: 1 conversation with people you muted. Unmute someone from their profile to see their messages again." There are no names, no links and no Show, while boards offer "Show" in place.
findings.why: Without names, people can't find out who they muted, so the way back is effectively hidden (rule 6).
findings.suggestion: Toast: "You muted {name}. You won't see their posts or messages. They aren't told." (Drop "aren't told" if the list stays public.) Set aria-label to "Mute {name}". In the inbox, list the hidden conversations by name behind a "Show" button, the same way BoardList does.
findings.verifier: PersonSafety.tsx:30-60 is an icon button with aria-label/title "Mute" and toasts "Muted"/"Unmuted". There is no name and no word on what muting does. MessagesPage.tsx:196-206 only gives a count and sends people to profiles they can't identify, while BoardList offers a Show for muted posts. The suggestion holds, including the caveat to say "They aren't told" only once finding 0 makes the list private.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-review.spec.ts: a queue action the server could not apply says so plainly, never its internal error
findings.what: The error reads "Couldn’t apply the action. Try again. The report stays open. Use the buttons above to try again.", which says to try again twice. The internal messages "Couldn’t resolve who to time out." and "Couldn’t resolve who to ban." can also show up there.
findings.why: It's repetitive, and "resolve" is developer language.
findings.suggestion: Name the action: "Couldn’t ban Carol Ng. The report is still open, so you can try again." For an unknown author: "Couldn’t tell who wrote this, so they can't be banned from here. Ban them from their profile."

findings.spec: chat-removal.spec.ts: removing asks first, sends one removal for that message, and the message reads as removed by a moderator
findings.what: `await expect(theirRow(page)).toHaveCount(0, { timeout: 20_000 }).catch(() => {})` is an assertion that swallows its own failure. The row stays with its marker, so the step usually waits the full 20 s and then proves nothing.
findings.why: It adds about 20 s to every run, and a step that can never fail reads as if it checks something.
findings.suggestion: Remove the .catch(() => {}) and its misleading comment, and keep the assertion as a real check that the removed text is gone from the open page (`await expect(theirRow(page)).toHaveCount(0)`). It is cheap and falsifiable. Keep the marker and reload checks that follow.
findings.verifier: The swallowed assertion is real, but the "waits the full 20 s" claim is wrong. theirRow filters message-row by hasText "Buy my coin". Once removed, the row renders "message removed by a moderator" instead of its content (ChannelTimeline.tsx:379-384), so the filter matches nothing almost at once. The step passes fast and proves nothing only because of the .catch.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-moderation.spec.ts / report.spec.ts
findings.what: No browser spec clicks moderation-delete ("Remove message…" with its reason dialog, including the Home-post path where the server closes the report itself) or moderation-dismiss. Only ban, timeout and escalate are covered.
findings.why: Removing is the moderator's most common action. The Home path has special handling for "report is not open" (use-moderation-queue.ts:345-352) that only a run through the real flow would catch if it broke.
findings.suggestion: Add one mocked queue test for the paths the real-server suite doesn't cover: remove a reported room message with a reason (one 9005 with the reason, then one 9044, and the row reads Resolved), and dismiss another report (one 9044 with action=dismiss and no 9005, and the row reads Dismissed). Optionally add a mocked case where 9044 answers "report is not open" after a Home removal, to pin the special-case branch without the real server.
findings.verifier: Removal and dismissal from ModerationQueuePanel are indeed untested in the mocked suite: no spec there clicks moderation-delete or moderation-dismiss. But the Home-post removal path, including the server closing the report itself, is covered against the real server in tests/e2e-real/home-moderation.spec.ts:157-159. Board-level remove and dismiss are covered in board-reports.spec.ts:190-216, although that is a different component.

findings.spec: mute-everywhere.spec.ts
findings.what: Muting is tested on boards, rooms and notifications, but not on the Home timeline, which is the product's main feed (D71). Separately, the suite runs only the full build. The pilot build's community panel ("Notices from this community", no New chat, "Only you can see these. To write to someone, use Messages on Home") is never exercised, while three tests cover the non-pilot "Private chats" path.
findings.why: The two surfaces pilot users actually see are the ones without coverage.
findings.suggestion: Optionally add a fast mocked Home check that a muted author's existing post is left out of the list. The main ask should be pilot-build coverage of DmView, either as a node test of its gated text or by asserting that copy in the SOCIAL_HOSTED (contributor-only) branch of tests/e2e-real/social.spec.ts, which already runs against the VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1 build.
findings.verifier: Home muting is covered: tests/e2e-real/social.spec.ts:568-606 mutes Carol and checks her post is gone from /social, and the mocked social-shouldfix-feed.spec.ts:140 checks a muted person's new post isn't counted. Also, Home leaves muted posts out with no Show (PostList.tsx:89-97), so asking to check "with Show" would test behaviour that doesn't exist. The pilot-build gap is real: DmView's contributor-only copy ("Notices from this community", "Only you can see these…", DmView.tsx:140, 161) is never asserted by any spec.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-review.spec.ts (all); report.spec.ts: a member's sidebar is rooms, boards and messages…; report.spec.ts: every signed read carries its own nonce…
findings.what: social-shouldfix-review.spec.ts is a grab-bag named after a review round: profile picture upload, wiki rename, passkey unlock, board access, older history. report.spec.ts also holds the sidebar role-gating test and a NIP-98 nonce test that checks only headers.
findings.why: Nobody looking for wiki or profile tests will find them here, the file names say nothing about the feature, and the nonce check is a protocol detail that a fast unit test of makeNip98AuthHeader would cover in milliseconds.
findings.suggestion: Move the off-topic tests into feature specs (profile-edit, wiki, sidebar-roles), which is low priority. Add a unit test for src/shared/lib/nip98.ts that checks two calls in the same second get distinct nonces and ids, but keep the browser nonce test, perhaps moved to a spec about signed reads, since it guards the caller-level behaviour.
findings.verifier: Moving the misplaced tests (picture upload, wiki rename, passkey profile, sidebar roles) to feature-named specs is fair housekeeping. The nonce test should not simply become a node test, though. It checks that two different in-app callers (the moderator check and the queue read) send distinct signed requests at runtime. A unit test of the nip98.ts header builder would not catch a caller reusing or caching one header, which is the failure the comment describes (the server refuses a replayed authorization).

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-messages.spec.ts: a first visit starts the record on Home…; a message newer than the reader last saw…; report.spec.ts: a member is offered no Ban; chat-removal.spec.ts tests 1, 3, 4
findings.what: Fixed sleeps (500 ms to 1.5 s) stand in for "nothing happened" checks, so the absence checks pass whenever the app is simply slow.
findings.why: A false pass on a slow machine and wasted time on a fast one. A missing Ban or a missing dot proves nothing if the roster hasn't been applied yet.
findings.suggestion: Replace the absence-check sleeps (messages spec 522 and 549, chat-removal 152, 208 and 254, report 544) with a positive readiness signal, such as a data attribute set once the roster or messages-seen record has been applied, or a Ban visible on another row. Keep the 1.1 s wait at line 553, or swap it for a seeded created_at, because it exists for seconds-granular timestamps and not as an absence check.
findings.verifier: Several cited sleeps are absence checks after a fixed wait, which is the real problem. But social-shouldfix-messages.spec.ts:553 (waitForTimeout(1_100)) is not one: it moves the clock past a whole second so the next message's created_at is newer than the seen record's seconds-granular "since". Removing it would make that test flaky. report.spec.ts:422 already waits for a positive signal (relay.requestsFor(13534) > 0) before its short settle.

areas.area: Sign-up, identity, passkeys, wallets, recovery and first run
areas.summary: This area covers how a new person gets an account (the sign-up dialog, the invite page, passkey or browser key, wallet sign-in), how they get back in (recovery key, passkey unlock), their profile and name, linking a payment wallet, and the first-run guidance on Home. The copy is mostly plain and careful, and errors keep server wording under "Technical details". The biggest risks are in recovery. "Remove passkey sign-in" can delete a passkey-only account in one click with no warning. The unlock overlay has no way out and re-prompts in a loop. The invite page, which is how pilot users arrive, puts the no-passkey account first, even though that account can't be paid, and it has no "I already have an account" option. Several specs drive raise-era or prototype screens (/launchpad, /identity-demo, org setup, the tour) rather than the pilot path, so the MVP's own locked-passkey and first-run journeys are thinly covered.

findings.spec: passkey.spec.ts "removing the passkey clears the stored record" (only the prototype page is covered)
findings.what: "Remove passkey sign-in" in the account menu runs removePasskeyIdentity() and reloads at once, with no confirmation. For a passkey (PRF) account there is no browser key (the specs assert buzz.identity.nsec is null), and the random salt (passkey-identity.ts:228) is stored only in localStorage, so deleting it means the key can never be derived again.
findings.why: A pilot user who signed up with a passkey and has not saved their recovery key loses the account permanently, along with its Shares and claims, with one misclick. Sign out has a guard ("You have not saved your recovery key...") but this path, which does more damage, has none (Review-Proven Rule 6).
findings.suggestion: Send Remove through the same ConfirmDialog as Sign out. When !hasBackedUp(), show "You haven't saved your recovery key. Without it this account is gone for good." with "Save recovery key" as the main button and "Remove anyway" as the secondary one. Better still, in the MVP drop the menu item for PRF accounts, since Sign out already covers leaving. Add a spec in the real app: passkey sign-up, then Remove, and expect the warning.
findings.verifier: ProfileMenu.tsx:660-667 calls removePasskeyIdentity() then window.location.reload() with no dialog. removePasskeyIdentity (passkey-identity.ts:334-347) deletes CRED/SALT/PUBKEY/MODE/R1 from localStorage, and setupPasskey makes the salt with crypto.getRandomValues (line 228). In PRF mode there is no other copy of the key, so one click loses the account unless the recovery key was saved. Sign out has a guard and this path has none. One detail to add: in unlock mode the browser key survives Remove, so the hard warning only needs to show for PRF accounts that have no backup (!hasBackedUp()).

findings.spec: (none: PasskeyUnlockGate has no spec)
findings.what: The auto-prompt effect lists `unlock` in its deps, and `unlock` is a new function on every render (the project has no React Compiler). setUnlocking(true) or setError(...) re-renders, the effect fires again and starts another passkey ceremony. If someone cancels the system prompt they get it again straight away, over and over. The overlay also has only one button, "Unlock", with no Sign out or "Use my recovery key".
findings.why: An unlock-mode user whose passkey was deleted from their keychain, or who keeps cancelling, is trapped behind a modal that re-prompts forever and gives no way back (Review-Proven Rules 4 and 6).
findings.suggestion: Run the auto-prompt once with a ref guard (useRef(false)) and leave `unlock` out of the deps. Add a secondary "Sign in with my recovery key instead" link (open OnboardingDialog with startOn="signin") and a "Sign out" link. Copy: change the heading "Sign in with passkey" to "Unlock your account", and change "Touch is required to unlock your account for this session." to "Use your fingerprint, face or device PIN to open your account."
findings.verifier: PasskeyUnlockGate.tsx:46-51 lists `unlock` in the deps, and `unlock` is a new closure on every render; the biome-ignore comment only silences the lint. setUnlocking(true) re-renders while `needed` is still true, so the effect fires again and starts a second ceremony while the first is pending. That rejects, setError re-renders, and the cycle repeats. The overlay renders only the Unlock button. One adjustment: in unlock mode the browser key is still stored, so the main way out should be a "Sign out" link. "Use my recovery key" is a secondary option. The ref-guard fix and the copy change are good.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-signup.spec.ts "someone with no account can make a passkey account on the invite page..."
findings.what: For a newcomer the invite page makes "Create an account and join" (a browser key, no passkey) the black primary button and "Create with a passkey" the outlined secondary. The sign-up dialog does the opposite in the pilot build (passkeyFirst, OnboardingDialog.tsx:289) and warns "You'll need a passkey to be paid for work." The invite page gives no such warning, offers no recovery key after the plain path, and lets either button go ahead with an empty name, so the passkey path falls back to "Creaton user".
findings.why: The pilot is invite-only, so most pilot users arrive through this page. They will take the big black button and end up with an account that can't be paid and has no saved key. That is exactly what the dialog was redesigned to prevent.
findings.suggestion: Mirror the dialog. Make "Create with a passkey" the primary button and "Create without a passkey" a quiet link with "You'll need a passkey to be paid for work." Require a name before either button is enabled. Change "No account yet? Pick a name and we will make one in this browser." to "New here? Pick the name people will see." Add a spec asserting which button is primary in the contributor-only build.
findings.verifier: InvitePage.tsx:519-528 makes "Create an account and join" (getOrCreateIdentity, a plain browser key) the black primary button. "Create with a passkey" is the outlined secondary (530-545). `disabled` (339-348) does not check the name, and the passkey path falls back to "Creaton user" (line 310). The plain path goes straight to window.location.assign("/") without offering a recovery key, while the passkey path does offer one (RecoveryKeyDialog at 704). This is the opposite of OnboardingDialog's passkeyFirst (line 289). The runbook sends every pilot user in through their own invite link.

findings.spec: (none)
findings.what: The invite page offers sign-in only when this browser already holds an account. Someone who already has an account but opens their invite on a new phone or browser sees only "Create an account and join" and "Create with a passkey". There is no "I already have an account" option to sign in with a recovery key, as the sign-up dialog has.
findings.why: An existing contributor who opens an invite elsewhere makes a second identity and splits their Shares, reviews and name across two accounts. Nothing on the page says this is happening.
findings.suggestion: Under the create buttons, add "Already have an account? Sign in with your recovery key". Open the existing SignInView and, after import, come back to this invite instead of reloading to /. Add a spec: a fresh browser imports a key on the invite page, and the claim is signed by that key.
findings.verifier: The invite page has two branches. When browserSigningAvailable is true (NIP-07, stored identity or passkey record) it shows join or unlock. Otherwise it shows invite-new-account with only the two create buttons, and nothing on the page imports a recovery key. An existing user opening the invite on a new browser can only make a second account.

findings.spec: passkey.spec.ts "reload → Continue with Touch ID re-derives the registered identity"
findings.what: The PRF salt is random per registration and kept only in localStorage. Because of that, a synced passkey (iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager) can't sign in on the person's other devices, and signing out on the same device also needs the recovery key. That is why the copy has to say "On another device you need your recovery key" everywhere.
findings.why: People without technical experience lose 64-character hex keys. Synced passkeys would cover most "new phone" cases with no key at all and remove the biggest recovery burden in the product.
findings.suggestion: Apply this to new registrations only. Put the salt (or a fixed app-wide salt, which is safe because PRF output is secret per credential) into user.id, which today is randomBytes(16) at passkey.ts:616. Then a discoverable get() with no allowCredentials returns it through userHandle, and the key can be re-derived on any device the passkey syncs to. Existing accounts keep their localStorage salt. Add "Sign in with a passkey" to SignInView for accounts made this way. Unlock-mode accounts still need the recovery key, so keep it as the backup and say so.
findings.verifier: The diagnosis holds: the salt is random per registration (passkey-identity.ts:228) and lives only in localStorage, and passkey.ts uses allowCredentials with the stored credentialId (696-697). A synced passkey therefore can't re-derive the key on another device, yet the runbook asks people to "confirm the passkey is synced". The suggestion needs a migration caveat, though. Changing how the salt is derived changes the derived key, so every existing PRF account must keep its stored salt.

findings.spec: passkey.spec.ts "signing out of a passkey account ... counts it saved only after the export"
findings.what: copyRecoveryKey() calls markBackedUp(account) as soon as the clipboard write resolves. A single click on "Copy recovery key" in the account menu therefore removes the amber "Save a recovery key. Your account only exists in this browser." warning and the Sign out guard, even though the key only sits in the clipboard. The spec's stated contract, "counts it saved only after the export", tests Download only.
findings.why: Clipboards get overwritten. The person then believes their key is saved, signs out with no warning, and is locked out.
findings.suggestion: Keep Copy, but after it succeeds show a small check, "I've pasted it somewhere safe" (a password manager or notes), and call markBackedUp only when that is ticked. Download keeps counting on its own. Add a spec step: Copy without ticking, reopen the menu, and the warning and the Sign out guard are still there.
findings.verifier: Confirmed: copyRecoveryKey (RecoveryKeyDialog.tsx:80-99) calls markBackedUp as soon as the clipboard write resolves, and ProfileMenu's "Copy recovery key" calls it directly. That clears the amber warning and the Sign out guard. Counting only Download would be worse, though. Pasting the key into a password manager is the safest way to store it, and many phone browsers handle downloads badly.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-signup.spec.ts "Get started does not tick the name step for a profile that has no name"
findings.what: The Get started checklist has "Add your name and a picture" plus project steps, but no "Save your recovery key" step and no "Set up passkey sign-in" step for an account made without a passkey. The only reminder is a small amber line inside the account menu.
findings.why: For a new account, the most important first-hour action is making sure it can't be lost and can be paid. The checklist is the one place a newcomer reliably looks.
findings.suggestion: Add a step {label: "Save your recovery key", hint: "You need it to sign in on another device.", done: hasBackedUp()} that opens RecoveryKeyDialog in place. For an account without a passkey, also add "Set up passkey sign-in" with the hint "You need it to be paid for work."
findings.verifier: stepsFor in home-steps.ts:59-98 returns only name, look/follow or publish steps. There is no recovery or passkey step. RecoveryOfferHost does offer the key once, right after passkey sign-up, but if the person presses Done the only reminder left is the amber line inside the account menu. The plain-key path from the invite page never gets even that offer. Show the steps only when they apply: the recovery step when !hasBackedUp(), and the passkey step in the contributor-only build for accounts that have no passkey.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-signup.spec.ts "Edit profile in the account menu uploads a picture..." and "Edit profile on the profile page offers the same picture upload..."
findings.what: There are two profile editors. One is an inline form squeezed into the 18rem account popover (placeholder "Display name", aria-label "Name", save id profile-save). The other is the EditProfileDialog opened from the profile page and from Home's name step (label "Name", save id social-edit-profile-save). Each has its own save path, its own error handling and its own spec.
findings.why: Two editors for one thing means double the specs and double the bugs, and the labels already differ. The popover version is cramped on a phone and was already broken once by the menu closing under the pointer (see first-run.spec).
findings.suggestion: Have the account menu's "Edit profile" open EditProfileDialog, as Home does, and delete the inline form along with its state, saveProfile and the profile-menu-picture wiring. The profile-page spec and first-run's Edit profile check (retargeted) then cover it, so the account-menu upload spec can be dropped. The "profile-save-error" spec would move to the dialog's error test id.
findings.verifier: ProfileMenu.tsx:449-498 has its own inline editor (placeholder "Display name", aria-label "Name", profile-save) with its own saveProfile (238-263, publishProfile plus its own error handling). EditProfileDialog takes only open/onClose/profile and is already used by ProfilePage and HomeHero, so AppNav's ProfileMenu can open it in place. Nothing in the inline form is missing from the dialog.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-identity.spec.ts "an account with no passkey is told why..."; passkey-wallet.spec.ts; payment-wallet.spec.ts
findings.what: The wallet card mixes jargon and verbs. "This account linked a smart account, which has to be checked on the network, and that check could not be made just now. Try again in a moment." (no Try again button is shown in this state). "Sign with my passkey account", "Waiting for signatures…", "Retry wallet update", "Link again", "Your payment wallet was not linked" and "Connect payment wallet" all name the same action, sometimes as link and sometimes as connect.
findings.why: "Smart account", "signatures" and "wallet update" are crypto internals, and the connect/link mix makes it unclear these are one action. The unreachable state tells the person to try again but gives them nothing to press.
findings.suggestion: Use "connect" everywhere: "Your payment wallet wasn't connected. Try again.", "Connect again", "Finish connecting" (for Retry wallet update). Change "Sign with my passkey account" to "Use my passkey" and "Waiting for signatures…" to "Waiting for your approval…". Line 270 becomes "We couldn't check this wallet just now. Try again in a moment." with a Try again button that refetches. Change "View on explorer" (line 243) to "See its payment history".

findings.spec: signing-recovery.spec.ts (LOCKED_MESSAGE); payment-wallet.spec.ts "a locked passkey has a recovery action inside wallet linking"
findings.what: The lock message shown on every gated surface is "Unlock your passkey before this browser can sign." The page-level description is "This server requires sign-in to load. Sign in with your passkey below and this page will retry automatically." The same state is also called "Unlock with your passkey" (InvitePage.tsx:491), "Sign in with passkey" (sign-recovery.ts:61) and "Unlock" (RecoveryKeyDialog, PasskeyUnlockGate).
findings.why: "This browser can sign" is machine wording, and three names for one action make people wonder whether these are different steps.
findings.suggestion: Settle on one verb, "Unlock". The message becomes "Your account is locked. Unlock it with your passkey to carry on.", the button "Unlock with passkey" everywhere, and the page line "Unlock your account to see this page. It reloads by itself after." SIGNING_BLOCKED_MESSAGE is matched by isSigningBlockedError, so change the constant and keep matching on the class.

findings.spec: (none directly; OnboardingDialog wallet path)
findings.what: "Use my wallet instead" (wallet sign-in) appears in the sign-up dialog whenever window.ethereum exists, including in the contributor-only pilot build. Unlike the other buttons it is enabled with no name typed, and it makes an account that is neither a passkey account nor offered a recovery key.
findings.why: In the pilot this is a third, crypto-flavoured way in, which contradicts "the passkey is the way in". Accounts made this way can't be paid and may end up nameless.
findings.suggestion: Show it only when raisesOffered() (as was done with passkeyFirst), or move it under the "I already have an account" sign-in. If it stays, require a name like the other buttons. Removing it costs nothing in the pilot, since payouts go to the passkey account.
findings.verifier: OnboardingDialog.tsx:403-415 shows "Use my wallet instead" whenever walletAvailable() is true. That only checks window.ethereum (siwe.ts:110) and has no raisesOffered() gate. The button is disabled={!allowed || saving}, with no name check, unlike `ready`. The dialog's own passkeyFirst comment says the contributor-only build pays work at a passkey account. One small correction: a wallet account doesn't need a Creaton recovery key, because the wallet's own seed covers that, so that part of the 'what' doesn't matter. Gate the button on raisesOffered().

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-errors.spec.ts "Sign up on an invite-only server says so before an account is made"
findings.what: On an invite-only server the dialog warns "An account made here without one can't read or post." but still enables "Create with a passkey" and "Create without a passkey", so the person can still make the useless account the notice warns about.
findings.why: A warning that sits beside an enabled button is easy to skip, and every page then refuses the account that was just made.
findings.suggestion: When access.data === "invite_only", lead with a "Paste your invite link" field that goes to /invite/<code>, keep "I already have an account", and turn the create buttons into one quiet link, "Make an account anyway". Only drop that link if no owner flow can add an existing account by key. Notice copy: "This server is invite-only. Open the invite link you were sent to make your account." The spec asserts the paste field is the primary action.
findings.verifier: Real: InviteOnlySignUpNotice is advice only. Its own comment says "sign-up is not blocked either way", and the create buttons stay enabled. On the pilot server (BUZZ_REQUIRE_RELAY_MEMBERSHIP=true) an account made this way can't read or post. Removing account creation outright is riskier, though. useCommunityAccess may be loading or wrong, and existing members still need a way in.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-signup.spec.ts "terms that could not be loaded..." and "a refusal the page does not know..."
findings.what: The invite page's main button reads "Join in browser". That only meant something next to a desktop app ("Accept invite in Creaton"), and DESKTOP_APP is off in the MVP.
findings.why: "In browser" hints that there is a better place to join, and a newcomer can't find one.
findings.suggestion: "Join this community" (and keep "Join in browser" only when DESKTOP_APP is on). Update the role-name locators in the two specs.

findings.spec: signing-recovery.spec.ts (all five tests)
findings.what: The locked-passkey contract is tested only on /launchpad ("Set up a sale", "Launch id", "Publish launch") and the /projects % board. Both are raise-era surfaces that are gated off in the contributor-only build.
findings.why: The pilot's own gated actions (posting on Home or a board, accepting or finishing work on a contributor project, voting) are where a locked passkey will actually bite, and none of them is covered. If the raise screens are removed, the coverage goes with them.
findings.suggestion: Move the suite onto MVP surfaces. Locked passkey, then post on Home: expect the unlock action inline and the draft kept. Locked passkey, then accept a work item on a contributor project: expect the unlock action in the dialog. Keep one read-side auth-required case on Home's feed. Drop the launch-wizard case.
findings.verifier: All the signing-recovery.spec.ts cases go to /launchpad ("Set up a sale", "Launch id", "Publish launch") or to /projects with its % board. The deprecation note lists both as hidden in the contributor-only build. Posting on Home or a board, contributor-project accept/finish and voting have no locked-passkey coverage.

findings.spec: first-run.spec.ts "a newcomer can sign up, start an organization, and find it again"; tour.spec.ts (whole file)
findings.what: The "first visit" spec signs up with the quiet "Create without a passkey" path and then drives org setup (org-toggle, helpers). Org views are hidden in the pilot build. The tour's page list is /launchpad, /portfolio, /projects plus the sale wizard and raising-project stops, and it ends with the meaningless `expect(ME).toHaveLength(64)`.
findings.why: The pilot's real first hour (invite, then passkey, then save the key, then the Get started steps, then start a contributor project or look at one) has no end-to-end spec. The tour's screenshots describe a product the MVP no longer ships, so anyone reading the product off them is misled.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite first-run step 3 as: the Get started list, then "Start your project" to /start/contributor, then the project page reachable after reload, using the passkey path. Rebuild the tour's PAGES around Home, Start, contributor project, Your work and a board, and delete the sale-wizard, idea and raising stops (or drop the file, since it is opt-in and asserts nothing).
findings.verifier: first-run.spec.ts:31 uses the quiet create path and clicks org-toggle (line 86), and org views are hidden in the pilot build. tour.spec.ts PAGES includes /launchpad and /portfolio and ends with expect(ME).toHaveLength(64), which asserts a constant. The pilot's own first hour (invite, passkey, save the key, Get started, a contributor project) has no end-to-end spec.

findings.spec: passkey.spec.ts tests 1-3 ("one registration derives both identity roots...", "reload → Continue with Touch ID...", "removing the passkey clears the stored record")
findings.what: These drive the /identity-demo prototype, which the hosted build never serves (build-gates.ts:36-48), using its own buttons ("Continue with Touch ID / platform authenticator"). The production sign-up, reload-unlock and Remove paths in the account menu are different code.
findings.why: They keep the prototype route alive and give false confidence. Remove in the real menu (the dangerous one above) and the real reload unlock are untested.
findings.suggestion: Move the storage-posture assertion (only public buzz.passkey.* keys, no nsec) into the production passkey sign-up spec. Replace the reload test with: sign up via the dialog, reload, unlock from the account menu or a gated action, same pubkey. Replace the Remove test with the production menu plus the confirmation it should have. Then delete the demo specs, and consider deleting /identity-demo and UserOpDemoCard from the app.
findings.verifier: passkey.spec.ts tests 1-3 go to /identity-demo (line 47). That page is PasskeyCeremonyPage, which has its own buttons and its own Remove call (line 254), and the deprecation doc lists the passkey demo among the routes gated off. The production Remove in ProfileMenu and the reload unlock through PasskeyUnlockGate have no spec. Note: UserOpDemoCard is also imported by lib/sponsoredSender.ts, so before deleting it check that import (it may only be a type or a shared helper).

findings.spec: usernames.spec.ts (four tests)
findings.what: Four tests cover showing a community username (`tessa@alpha.example.com`), but the web app gives no way to get one: Edit profile deliberately has one "Name" field and no Username (asserted in social-shouldfix-identity.spec.ts:130). The tests mount the community chat view at /c/... rather than Home.
findings.why: Three of the four tests protect display of a value no MVP user can create, and that rendering is unit-level label logic (user-label.ts). The one that matters to the MVP is "no name means Your account, never a key".
findings.suggestion: Keep "an identity with no name is Your account to its owner" and move it to Home. Move the username/no-key rules into user-label unit tests and delete the other three browser tests. If usernames are wanted in the MVP, add them to Edit profile instead.
findings.verifier: usernames.spec.ts mounts /c/alpha.example.com (line 79). Three of its four tests check how a nip05 username is shown, and EditProfileDialog has no username field. The labeling rule already has unit tests in features/profiles/lib/user-label.test.mjs, so the move is cheap. Keep the "no name is Your account" case as a browser test on Home. Low impact, as rated.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-errors.spec.ts "a picture from another site loads under the embedder policy the server sends"
findings.what: Its own comment says the routed picture "skips the browser's check", so this test can't fail when the embedder policy blocks pictures. The next test (line 320), with two real servers, is the falsifiable one.
findings.why: It adds runtime and reads as COEP coverage without being any.
findings.suggestion: Keep it, and rename it to what it proves: "Home runs under the server's isolation headers and shows a profile picture". Keep the real-server test as the one that covers the embedder policy.
findings.verifier: Partly refuted. This test is not a fake COEP check. It serves the app's documents with the server's COOP/COEP headers and asserts window.crossOriginIsolated matches SPA_COEP. It also checks that Home boots and renders a profile picture under those isolation headers. The next test does not check that: it uses a bare page, not the app. The routed picture does skip the embedder check, as its own comment says, and the comment already scopes the test that way.

findings.spec: social-shouldfix-signup.spec.ts "signing up with a passkey says a recovery key is still needed..."
findings.what: "Your recovery key can't be read in this browser, so there is nothing to save here. Stay signed in until you have it." doesn't tell the person why or what to do. "I am 18 years of age or older." is stiff form language.
findings.why: The first leaves someone unsure whether their account is safe, with no next step. The second is a small tone mismatch with the rest of the plain copy.
findings.suggestion: "This account signs in through your wallet, so there's no recovery key to save here. Keep your wallet safe; it's how you get back in." (or the right reason for the account type). "I'm 18 or older."

areas.summary: smoke.spec.ts is a grab-bag of about 45 regression guards. They cover the community directory and community page, the invite consent and join, the server connect form, error panels for failed reads (Tasks, AI helpers, launchpad, search, community), the wiki, the profile menu (wallet, theme, name edit), the document shell and a few accessibility checks. Most tests guard real past bugs and are falsifiable. But the suite only runs against the default (raise-capable) build. About a third of its time goes to screens the contributor-only pilot hides (AI helpers, the tab helper, the sale wizard, Repositories, desktop downloads), while the pilot build gets no broad smoke at all. Reading the screens behind the tests turned up real problems the tests lock in: a directory card stores a ws:// address that an https page cannot open; a malformed directory crashes the whole page instead of showing the directory error; several error panels say the server "did not answer" when it actually refused; and the community page offers a desktop "Open in Creaton" link plus a "Join in browser" button that doesn't join anything. Much of the copy around these tests still uses protocol words ("relay", "query", "client", "local identity", "peer-to-peer room").

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: community page shows metadata and join stores the relay URL
findings.where: web/src/shared/lib/relay-url.ts:36 (used by web/src/features/communities/ui/CommunityHomePage.tsx:181 and CommunityDirectoryPage.tsx:120); asserted at web/tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts:221
findings.what: normalizeRelayWsUrl turns a bare host from a directory card into `ws://host` every time, and the test asserts `ws://alpha.example.com`. On the hosted app, which is served over https, the browser blocks ws:// as mixed content.
findings.why: Someone opens another community from the directory and presses "Join in browser". The override is saved in localStorage and the page reloads onto a server it can never reach, and it stays broken on every reload. The only way back is the /repos connect form, and the pilot build hides /repos.
findings.suggestion: For a bare host, pick the scheme from the page: `wss://` when window.location.protocol is https:, else `ws://`. Do the same in AddCommunityForm. Change the test to assert the scheme-correct URL, and add a case that runs under an https origin (or unit-test normalizeRelayWsUrl with both protocols).
findings.verifier: relay-url.ts:36 returns `ws://${trimmed}` for any bare host, and CommunityHomePage.tsx:181 / CommunityDirectoryPage.tsx:125 pass directory hosts and typed hosts through it, then store the result as the buzz.relayUrl override. relayWsUrl() already picks wss: from window.location.protocol for the same-origin case, so the bare-host branch is the odd one out. On an https page, ws:// is blocked as mixed content, and the override survives reloads. The test at smoke.spec.ts:221 locks in ws://. The suggested fix (scheme from the page protocol, plus a unit test for both protocols) is right.

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: a malformed relay payload shows a recoverable error, not a blank page
findings.what: `(await response.json()) as CommunityDirectory` is cast without any check. If `communities` is not an array, the directory page throws during render and the whole route shows "Something went wrong". The test then locks that crash in as the expected behaviour.
findings.why: The page already has a proper state for a bad directory: the "Couldn't load the community directory" panel with a retry, while the person's own community card stays reachable. A crash hides that card, so one odd field from the server stops people from opening their own community.
findings.suggestion: Validate the shape in fetchCommunityDirectory: throw `new Error("The server sent a community list this app can't read.")` when `!Array.isArray(directory.communities)`, and drop malformed entries. Change the test to expect `community-directory-error` plus the visible `127.0.0.1:4173` card. Keep a route-boundary test that uses a genuine render throw.
findings.verifier: use-communities.ts:38 casts the response without checking it. CommunityDirectoryPage.tsx:165 calls `data?.communities.find(...)` during render, so `communities: "not-an-array"` throws, the route boundary takes over, and the connected-community card disappears. The page already has a `community-directory-error` QueryError with a retry and copy that says the connected community stays reachable, so a shape check in fetchCommunityDirectory is the right fix. The test comment shows it was written to prove the route boundary, so keeping a separate boundary test with a real render throw (as suggested) is needed.

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: the work board reports a refused query instead of an empty board / the fleet view reports a refused roster query / a refused task query is reported on the agents view / a refused search offers a retry
findings.what: These panels pass `message` to QueryError but not `error`, so QueryError cannot tell a refusal from silence. Every one of the tests sends a CLOSED refusal, yet the panel says "The server did not answer the task and issue query, so this board has nothing to show." The tests only check the raw words inside the collapsed Technical details.
findings.why: QueryError's own docs call saying "nobody replied" about a server that replied the exact lie the component exists to prevent. People are told to check their connection when the real problem is a refusal or missing access. The plain-words refusal mapping (bans, invite-only, rate limit) is also skipped on these screens.
findings.suggestion: Pass `error={loadError}` (and `error={error}` in search) to QueryError on all four panels. Rewrite the unanswered descriptions as "The server didn't answer, so the tasks can't be shown." / "The server didn't answer, so search can't run.". Make the tests assert the visible description (`work-load-error-description`) and `data-outcome="answered"`, not just text inside the collapsed details.
findings.verifier: WorkBoard.tsx:342, FleetView.tsx:233 and :366, and SearchResults.tsx:120 pass `message` but not `error`. QueryError computes the outcome only from `error` (query-error.tsx:84), so with `error` undefined these panels always show the caller's "did not answer" description and data-outcome="unanswered", even for a CLOSED refusal. Passing `error` turns on the refusal-aware copy and the plain-words mapping. The rewritten descriptions and the test changes are sound. The two fleet panels only appear in raise builds.

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: community page shows metadata and join stores the relay URL
findings.what: The community card always shows an "Open in Creaton" button that is a desktop deep link (`desktopConnectDeepLink`). Unlike the invite page, it is not gated on DESKTOP_APP.
findings.why: The MVP has no desktop app (D137). In the web-only build this button does nothing, or asks to open an app nobody has installed, and it sits right next to the main action.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the button in `DESKTOP_APP ? … : null`, as InvitePage.tsx does. Nothing in the web flow depends on it.
findings.verifier: CommunityHomePage.tsx:313 always renders `Open in Creaton` (desktopConnectDeepLink). In the web-only MVP (D137, no desktop) it is not gated, unlike InvitePage.tsx:560/597, which use DESKTOP_APP. The only other caller is repos/ConnectButton, which is not affected. Gate it on DESKTOP_APP. Optional follow-up: with the second button gone, "Join in browser" could simply read "Join". The card copy there ("...repositories, and agents") is also stale for the pilot.

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: community page shows metadata and join stores the relay URL
findings.what: Three strings. The button "Join in browser" only points this browser at that server and reloads; it joins nothing. The fallback description "Browse this community in your browser. Join to see channels, messages, repositories, and agents." uses words the pilot doesn't use (the app says rooms and boards; repositories and agents are hidden). The note "Joining doesn't require an account here. Creaton creates a local identity only when you post or join privately." is jargon.
findings.why: A newcomer reads "Join" as membership and "local identity" as nothing. The word "browser" means nothing in a web-only product.
findings.suggestion: Button: "Open this community". Description: "See what people here are talking about and working on." Note: "You can look around without an account. You'll make one when you first post."

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: wrong relay shows connect form and stores the relay URL
findings.what: Main copy uses "relay" throughout: "Couldn't reach the relay", "If that isn't your community's relay, enter its URL to connect.", label "Relay URL", "Enter a relay URL to connect to.", "That doesn't look like a valid relay URL.", and the placeholder "wss://relay.example.com".
findings.why: The copy rule says "server" rather than "relay" in main copy, and the directory's own form already says "Server address" for the same input. Two names for one thing on neighbouring screens.
findings.suggestion: "Couldn't reach the server" / "This app is trying to reach {address}. If that's not your community's server, enter its address." / label "Server address" / "Enter a server address." / "That doesn't look like a server address." / placeholder "community.example.com". Update the test's role and label lookups to match.

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: a malformed relay payload shows a recoverable error, not a blank page
findings.what: "This view stopped responding to its data. Reloading usually clears it." The panel also shows both a "Try again" and a "Reload" button, which look identical to a person.
findings.why: It sounds like a machine wrote it, and two near-duplicate buttons make people guess which one to press.
findings.suggestion: "This page hit a problem. Try again, and if it keeps happening, reload the page." Keep "Try again" as the primary button and rename "Reload" to "Reload page", or drop it.

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: a dropped live connection is shown instead of failing silently
findings.what: Tooltip: "Live updates from the server have stopped; the client keeps retrying."
findings.why: "client" is developer vocabulary. People don't know they are "the client".
findings.suggestion: "New messages aren't arriving right now. Trying to reconnect…"

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: a dropped live connection is shown instead of failing silently
findings.what: The test accepts `/Reconnecting|Connecting/`. The chip already shows "Connecting…" while the first socket opens, so the test can pass without the drop ever being detected.
findings.why: If drop detection broke, this regression guard would not fail (Review-Proven Rule 3).
findings.suggestion: Replace the regex with an exact `toHaveText("Reconnecting…")` (with the usual polling timeout). It only becomes true after a drop and stays true while the mock keeps closing. No open-first step is needed.
findings.verifier: Real: ChannelTimeline.tsx:733-736 shows "Connecting…" while liveStatus is "connecting" (the first attempt, subscribe-channel.ts:85), so `/Reconnecting|Connecting/` passes even if the drop is never detected. But the suggested "wait for the chip to be hidden first" step is racy, because this mock closes the socket as soon as the live REQ arrives. After the first drop, backoff.attempt > 0, so the status stays "reconnecting" (subscribe-channel.ts:85/169/189) through the retries.

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: the wiki says when nobody else is connected, and why live editing is off
findings.what: The wiki toolbar shows a permanent "Live co-editing unavailable" chip. Its details read like "Live co-editing is unavailable: this server publishes no member list, so collaborators cannot be verified.", "the peer-to-peer room could not be opened", "your identity could not sign the update". The other chip states are "Live: verified members only" and "Live: connecting".
findings.why: On the usual server this warning sits on every page someone writes, and it is phrased as a fault in protocol terms. For a small team, "save to share" is all they need to know.
findings.suggestion: When live editing is off, hide the chip and show the editors text as "Editing alone · others see your changes when you save". Keep the reason in a title or Technical details, rewritten plainly, e.g. "Live editing is off on this server. Others see your changes when you save." Chip states: "Live" and "Connecting…".

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: the search shortcut hint is visible on desktop and hidden on a phone / Cmd+K focuses search
findings.what: The hint always shows "⌘K", but the handler also accepts Ctrl+K (line 209). Windows and Linux users see a Mac-only key. The tests only press `Meta+k`, so the Ctrl path, which those users actually take, is untested.
findings.why: Wrong shortcut hints for most non-Mac users, and an input modality with no test (Review-Proven Rule 8).
findings.suggestion: Show "Ctrl K" when the platform isn't Mac (navigator.userAgentData?.platform or navigator.platform). Add `Control+k` to the Cmd+K test.
findings.verifier: CommunityShell.tsx:209 accepts metaKey or ctrlKey, but the hint at :429 is hard-coded "⌘K". The only test presses Meta+k (smoke.spec.ts:964), so the Ctrl path that Windows and Linux users take is untested. Showing a platform-correct hint and adding a Control+k press holds up. Impact is low.

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: invite requires age and legal consent before opening Creaton
findings.what: The test asserts that the Terms of use and Privacy note links have `text-decoration-line: none` until hovered. That locks in an accessibility defect: the links are text-black inside black label text, so nothing marks them as links. The test also mocks a GitHub release list with four Buzz desktop builds that this build never shows.
findings.why: It asserts styling instead of behaviour, and the styling it protects fails the "links distinguishable without colour or hover" rule. Anyone fixing the underline gets a red test. The dead mocks add noise.
findings.suggestion: Underline the Terms of use and Privacy note buttons all the time (`underline underline-offset-4`). Replace the hover CSS checks with a click on "Terms of use" that asserts the document dialog opens and the agreement checkbox stays unchecked. Keep the GitHub releases mock, with a comment saying it is there so the no-download assertion would fail if the desktop gate leaked.
findings.verifier: The underline part holds. The buttons are `text-black no-underline ... hover:underline` inside `text-black/60` label text, so they are barely distinguishable, and the test asserts `none` until hover. It also never checks that pressing Terms opens the document without ticking the box. But the api.github.com mock is not dead: it makes the "no Download it now link / no Accept in Creaton" assertions falsifiable. Without releases available, a broken DESKTOP_APP gate would still show no download link in the test, because the fetch would fail.

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: invite requires age and legal consent before opening Creaton
findings.what: The checkbox reads "I agree to the Creaton Terms of use and Privacy note.", but the documents are this server's (the loading line says "Loading this server's terms…"). The age line reads "I am 18 years of age or older." The button for people who already have an account reads "Join in browser".
findings.why: The terms are attributed to the wrong party, the wording is formal, and "in browser" makes no sense in a web-only app.
findings.suggestion: "I agree to this community's Terms of use and Privacy note." / "I'm 18 or older." / button "Join this community". Update the getByLabel and getByRole strings in the tests.

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts (whole file)
findings.what: The smoke project runs only against the default build. The contributor-only pilot build (VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1) is the one people will use, and it gets no broad smoke run: nothing checks that Repositories, AI helpers, Org and the sale wizard are actually hidden, or that the community, Tasks, wiki and profile paths still work with those flags.
findings.why: A flag regression would leak raise-era or agent screens into the pilot, or break a pilot-only path, and this suite would stay green.
findings.suggestion: Add a small pilot-build spec (or a few @pilot-tagged tests) run against a VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1 dist via E2E_DIST/E2E_PORT, for example from web-social-e2e.sh, which already builds one, or from mvp-gate --pilot. It should assert that fleet-toggle, org-toggle, the Repositories link and the sale wizard are absent, and that community, Tasks, wiki and profile still open. Don't duplicate the whole smoke file.
findings.verifier: Partly covered already. build-gates.test.mjs and the raises-offered, remixes-offered and contributorOnlyGates contract tests unit-test the predicates for VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1. scripts/web-social-e2e.sh builds and runs the real-server social suite on a contributor-only dist, and web-screen-audit.sh runs in mvp mode with E2E_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY. What is missing is a browser check that the shell actually uses those predicates (fleet-toggle, org-toggle, Repositories absent). A full smoke-pilot project is costly, and many specs hard-code :4173. Impact is medium, not high.

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: invite asks Safari users to choose their Mac download; invite download links to the appropriate platform destination
findings.what: About 190 lines of desktop-download routing tests (Mac chip chooser, App Store, Play Store, Fire tablet, ChromeOS). Both are skipped unless VITE_DESKTOP_APP=1, which no MVP build sets.
findings.why: The MVP ships no desktop app (D137). These tests never run, but they keep raise- and desktop-era fixtures (Buzz_0.4.9 assets, block/buzz release URLs) alive in the main smoke file.
findings.suggestion: Move them to a desktop-only spec file (e.g. invite-desktop-download.spec.ts) in a project that runs only for VITE_DESKTOP_APP builds, or delete them together with the download UI if desktop stays out.
findings.verifier: Both tests (smoke.spec.ts:411 and :487) call test.skip unless VITE_DESKTOP_APP=1, which no MVP or default smoke build sets. They carry block/buzz Buzz_0.4.9 fixtures. Moving them to a desktop-only spec keeps them for a future desktop build without cluttering the main smoke file. DEPRECATION keeps code that other builds use, so moving is safer than deleting while buzz-download still exists.

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: home page loads with Creaton branding; empty directory keeps the connected community reachable; an unpublished directory keeps the connected community reachable; invite can enroll the identity this app creates, without an extension
findings.what: Several tests duplicate others. The branding test only checks a top-bar link that every other test renders. The empty (200) and unpublished (404) directory tests repeat the setup and the card assertion of the parametrised `Communities opens launch chats directly with directory status 200/404`. The stored-identity invite join repeats invite-join.spec.ts "someone with an account sees the usual button" plus its claim test.
findings.why: Each costs a browser boot without adding coverage, and duplicates drift apart over time.
findings.suggestion: Delete the branding test. Fold the "No other communities are listed" and "doesn't publish a public community directory" assertions into the parametrised test and rename it (e.g. "the connected community opens with its open and private rooms, directory status 200/404"). Move the stored-identity invite claim test into invite-join.spec.ts next to "someone with an account sees the usual button" rather than deleting it.
findings.verifier: The branding test and the two directory-status tests do overlap with the parametrised 200/404 test, which already uses `communities: []` / 404 but does not check the empty or unpublished text. Folding those in and renaming the raise-era "launch chats" / "Demo · supporters" wording is fine. But the stored-identity invite test (smoke.spec.ts:1989) is not a duplicate. invite-join.spec.ts "someone with an account sees the usual button" only checks that the button is visible. Its claim tests cover a new account. The smoke test is the only one where an existing identity clicks Join in browser and the claim is checked as signed by that identity with the payload tag.

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: a launch can be bound to a discussion channel; the tab agent's key can be rotated; the fleet view reports a refused roster query; a refused task query is reported on the agents view; the launchpad directory reports a refused query; the landing Repositories button opens the repo browser
findings.what: Six tests drive screens the pilot build hides: the "Set up a sale" wizard, AI helpers (fleet) with its tab-helper account, and Repositories. The fleet screen also shows internal names in copy, e.g. "Mention @buzz-tab in a channel" (FleetView.tsx around line 306), and its load-error panels have no Try again (FleetView.tsx:236, :367).
findings.why: The MVP has no raises and no agents. Keeping these in the main smoke suite spends review and fix effort on surfaces no pilot user sees, while pilot paths go unchecked.
findings.suggestion: Keep the tests in the default (raise-capable) smoke run, optionally grouped under a describe block labelled as hidden in the pilot build. Add onRetry to fleet-load-error and fleet-tasks-load-error, replace "@buzz-tab" with the helper's shown name, and put the effort for pilot coverage into the pilot-build check (see finding 13).
findings.verifier: DEPRECATION-2026-10-31.md sets the rule: features still used in raise builds are hidden in the contributor-only build, not deleted. AI helpers (#6), repositories (#4) and the sale wizard stay in raise builds, and the default smoke build is a raise build. So these tests still guard live code, and dropping them would leave it unguarded. The copy and retry points hold. FleetView.tsx:305 shows the internal handle `@buzz-tab`, and fleet-load-error (:233) and fleet-tasks-load-error (:366) have no onRetry.

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: heavy views are split out of the first-load bundle
findings.what: The negative checks `not.toContain("WorkBoard-")` and `not.toContain("FleetView-")` depend on Vite chunk filenames. Rename the component, or let Vite name the chunk differently, and both pass vacuously. Only the wiki side is ever proven positive.
findings.why: A guard that stays green after its subject disappears protects nothing (Review-Proven Rule 3).
findings.suggestion: Prove the positive side for each view too: open Tasks and assert a `WorkBoard-` script loads, the same way the wiki side is checked. Or check the chunk names against dist/.vite/manifest.json so a rename fails the test.
findings.verifier: smoke.spec.ts:1126-1128 asserts the absence of the "WorkBoard-" and "FleetView-" chunk names, but only the WikiView side is ever shown to load. If the lazy import in CommunityShell.tsx:40/74 were renamed, or the chunk named differently, the negative checks would pass without testing anything. Opening Tasks (and helpers in the default build) and asserting the matching chunk loads makes them falsifiable.

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: a bound wallet can be unbound, and the proof names the revoke endpoint
findings.what: Confirm text: "It can no longer act for your account here, and it cannot be connected to this account again." It is unclear what "It" refers to, and the permanence is buried at the end. The test name also states an implementation detail ("names the revoke endpoint"), and the failure path (revoke refused, walletError shown) is untested.
findings.why: This step can't be undone, so the person has to understand that before confirming.
findings.suggestion: "This wallet will stop working with your account, and you can't connect it again later." Confirm label: "Disconnect for good". Rename the test "a connected wallet can be disconnected" and add a case where the revoke returns 500 and the binding is kept with a visible error.

findings.spec: smoke.spec.ts: home page shows the community directory from the relay / Communities opens launch chats directly
findings.what: When the member count is unknown, the card's footer reads "Open community". It sits where "3 members" goes and reads like either a button or "not invite-only". The "This community" section also shows a card whose fallback description is "Rooms, boards and messages on this server."
findings.why: "Open" is ambiguous now that communities can be open or invite-only (D33). The tests even locate the card by this phrase.
findings.suggestion: Footer: "Your community", or leave it empty when the count is unknown. Description: "Where your team talks and works." Locate the card in tests by testid instead of this text.

areas.area: Project pages, lists, presets and sandbox
areas.summary: Almost everything this area's specs exercise belongs to raises: the sale wizard, raise-size presets, the bid composer, funding chips, the raise sandbox, plus the "Technical details" cards. These screens only appear in builds that offer raises. The hosted pilot build (VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1) turns the same /launchpad page into an "Ideas" list, and no mocked spec runs in that mode. So about 45 tests run on every smoke pass and protect screens the MVP never shows, while the pilot's own list, empty state and idea start go untested. Inside the raise screens there are real problems: the raise sandbox claims you can create and bid when it is view-only, and it still shows a retired minted-token raise with six shares. Raw field names and contract jargon ("floorPrice", "milli-bips", "approve", "settled on-chain") reach users, and a test locks the field name in. "Community scores" links from every project page to a URL that any member can set. A few tests are not falsifiable (the sandbox.spec iframe test, the bid "mirror" test), or leak state between tests through a shared `published` array. My recommendation: move the raise specs to a raise-only project in the later gate, add a contributor-only mocked project for the Ideas list and project page, and fix the copy listed below.

findings.spec: launchpad-empty.spec.ts / funding-status.spec.ts (all tests); playwright.config.ts smoke project
findings.what: Every mocked spec in this area runs on the default build, where raisesOffered() is true. In the pilot build (VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1) the same /launchpad route becomes the 'Ideas' page: it opens on the Ideas tab, has no sale tabs or chips, shows 'Open project' buttons on contributor cards, and shows a 'N ideas · M projects' count. None of that has a mocked test. The only coverage is one click in e2e-real/social.spec.ts:965.
findings.why: What pilot users actually see can regress without the smoke suite noticing, while about 45 raise tests guard screens the MVP hides.
findings.suggestion: Keep launchpad-empty.spec.ts as it is. Add a 'pilot' Playwright project, or a separate config, since webServer is per config. It builds and serves a VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1 dist through E2E_DIST/E2E_PORT. Give it a new launchpad-pilot.spec.ts that checks: the page opens on Ideas; the empty state reads 'No ideas yet. Be the first to start one.' with Start an idea; there is no 'Set up a sale', no sandbox-entry and no launch-chips; `?start=sale` opens nothing; starting an idea lands on its page; a contributor card shows 'Open project' and no bid figures. Run it in mvp-gate.sh --pilot.
findings.verifier: The gap is real. raisesOffered() reads VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY at build time, and every smoke spec runs the default build. social-shouldfix-errors.spec.ts:18 says outright that the suite 'cannot switch VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY per test'. Nothing in tests/e2e asserts the Ideas tab default, the 'N ideas · M projects' count (LaunchesPage.tsx:328), the missing chips or sandbox, or 'No ideas yet. Be the first to start one.' Pilot coverage today is e2e-real/social.spec.ts and the screen-audit captures, which run against a real server and are not part of smoke. Moving and rewriting launchpad-empty is the wrong fix: raise builds are still the default build (DEPRECATION #18), and launchpad-empty guards that build's empty state.

findings.spec: launchpad.spec.ts (36 tests), launchpad-presets.spec.ts (2), funding-status.spec.ts (7)
findings.what: launchpad.spec.ts (1,279 lines), launchpad-presets.spec.ts (each test has a 120s timeout) and funding-status.spec.ts all drive raise-only surfaces: Set up a sale, bids, tokenomics, vesting, the auction param grid, funding chips. They sit in the default 'smoke' project, which runs with workers: 1.
findings.why: These tests make every smoke run of the MVP slower and noisier but protect nothing the pilot ships. DEPRECATION-2026-10-31 already moved raise journeys to `mvp-gate.sh --later`, and the mocked raise specs should follow.
findings.suggestion: Create a 'raise' Playwright project run by mvp-gate.sh --later and move the clearly raise-only specs into it as one set: launchpad-presets, funding-status, launchpad-dao-launch, voting-allocation, and the sale and bid parts of launchpad.spec.ts. Before moving launchpad.spec.ts, split out the directory, detail, track-record and verdict-timeline tests into a small spec that stays in smoke, unless a contributor spec already covers them. Keep stack-check in smoke.
findings.verifier: Most of launchpad.spec.ts is raise-only, but not all of it. 'directory renders launches from the relay', 'detail shows overview and updates', 'a production build shows no fabricated funding figures', the track-record tests ('the track record says what was recorded', 'a recorded verdict renders a timeline'), 'milestone claims and verdicts mirror to the feed' and the trust page test cover the shared directory and detail page that pilot projects also use. Moving the whole file drops that coverage. The 120s in launchpad-presets is a test.setTimeout ceiling, not how long the tests take. The finding also names only three files, while launchpad-dao-launch, voting-allocation, launchpad-challenge and launchpad-milestone are just as raise-era. Raise screens are hidden, not deleted (DEPRECATION line 6), so they still need a home that runs somewhere.

findings.spec: launchpad.spec.ts: 'the sandbox walks a full raise, clearly badged as simulated'
findings.what: The sandbox pitch reads "A simulated raise so the launchpad can be walked end to end. Terms are deployable; no chain is touched." The longer pitch reads "The sandbox exists to be played with: create, bid, watch price discovery, graduate." But LaunchDetailPage.tsx:449 (`sandbox || stage === "graduated" ? null`) hides every bid action, and nothing can be created there. The record also uses tokenPlan mode "mint" (line 114) and a six-way split with liquidity: 15 (line 98). Both were retired in D150 and D46: the wizard now shows three shares and no Liquidity, which launchpad.spec.ts:1158 asserts.
findings.why: The one 'try it' path tells people they can bid and create, and then shows a kind of raise the app no longer offers. Its sale page will not match the real sale they would set up.
findings.suggestion: Change the record to tokenPlan mode 'dao' with the three-share split, so it shows the powers card like a real launch. Replace the copy with: pitch "A practice raise with made-up numbers. Watch a sale fill and finish in about two minutes. No real money." longPitch "Nothing here is real: you can look around, but not bid." Or, if the sandbox is meant to teach, let it take a pretend bid.
findings.verifier: Verified in sandbox.ts. The pitch (line 39) promises 'Terms are deployable', and the longPitch says 'create, bid, watch price discovery, graduate'. LaunchDetailPage.tsx:449 renders no actions when `sandbox`, so nothing can be bid on or created. The record also uses tokenPlan mode 'mint', which D150 retired for new web launches ('old minted launches open read-only'), and a six-way allocation with liquidity 15, while the wizard now shows three shares. The copy also breaks the plain-words standard ('deployable', 'price discovery', 'graduate'). The sandbox only appears in raise builds, so this does not affect the pilot, but the bug in raise builds is real. The suggested rewrite is sound.

findings.spec: launchpad.spec.ts: 'the sandbox walks a full raise...'; launchpad-empty.spec.ts
findings.what: The only guided 'try it without risk' entry is 'Try the sandbox: Walk through a full raise, start to finish. No blockchain and no real money.' It only appears in raise builds. The MVP's core loop (take on work, get reviewed, earn Shares by vote) has no equivalent practice project.
findings.why: Pilot users without business experience are the ones who most need a safe walkthrough, and the existing one teaches the part of the product they will not use.
findings.suggestion: Do not build a simulated contributor project now. Point the empty Ideas and Discover states at what exists: one line such as 'Not sure where to start? Start an idea; your project will show you the first steps.' If a read-only example is still wanted after the pilot, model it on docs/v3-review/CREATON-EXAMPLE-PROJECT.md and reuse the D167 NewHereCard, so there is one source of truth. Keep the raise sandbox in raise builds only (it already is).
findings.verifier: The premise partly misses recent work. D167 (commit 420c4098a) added the 'New here?' card on a contributor project's Overview and two worked examples in 'Take this on' for first-time takers. That is the guided first walk through the core loop, done inside a real project. A separate fake example project is a second deterministic record to maintain, and it can drift the way the raise sandbox did (finding 2). The gap that is left is narrower: a brand-new community with no projects has nothing to look at.

findings.spec: launchpad.spec.ts: 'the create form refuses parameters the auction contract would reject'
findings.what: Issues render as `{issue.field}: {issue.message}`, so people see "floorPrice: Floor price must be a multiple of the tick spacing (100); the floor is the first tick." and "steps[0]: A step cannot last zero blocks." Other messages say "Supply is above the auction's ceiling (2^100 units)..." and "the steps sum to N of M milli-bips" (lib/launch-params.ts). The test asserts the text contains "floorPrice", which locks the internal name in.
findings.why: Code identifiers and contract units are protocol internals in main copy, which CLAUDE.md forbids. The messages also do not say what to do next.
findings.suggestion: Drop the `{issue.field}:` prefix and map each field to a label (Floor price, Price step, Sale schedule). Rewrite the messages, e.g. "The starting price must be a whole number of price steps. Press Use recommended terms to fix it." and "The sale schedule must sell the whole supply. Press Use recommended terms." Change the test to assert the label 'Floor price', not 'floorPrice'.

findings.spec: launchpad.spec.ts: 'a published score root is shown as a community data plane'
findings.what: fetchScoreRoots queries kind 37006 with no author filter, and the relay accepts 37006 from any member with MessagesWrite (ingest.rs:616). ScoreRootsCard (OverviewTab.tsx:468) shows the first root it gets as 'Community scores' on every project's Technical details, with a 'View proofs and scores' link to the event's `indexerUrl`.
findings.why: Any member can publish a score root and turn the link on every project page into a link to their own site. That is a ready-made phishing link, and nobody in the MVP publishes real score roots.
findings.suggestion: Remove ScoreRootsCard from OverviewTab and delete the 'community data plane' test. Also limit TrustGateCard's root list to roots authored by the community operator's key, or hide TrustGateCard in the contributor-only build. It fetches an attacker-chosen URL in the same way.
findings.verifier: fetchScoreRoots (use-launches.ts:167) queries kind 37006 with no author filter. The relay requires only MessagesWrite and global scope (ingest.rs tests at line 8020 and following). parseScoreRoot takes indexerUrl with a plain str(), with no allowlist. ScoreRootsCard renders roots.data[0] with an external 'View proofs and scores' link.
