It is also not limited to raise pages: raiseOverview is passed as children to DaoOverview (LaunchDetailPage.tsx:538), so contributor projects show it too, inside 'Technical details and checks'. TrustGateCard.tsx:46 also does fetch(selected.indexerUrl) on whatever URL any member published. The removal suggestion fits the MVP.

findings.spec: launchpad.spec.ts: 'milestone claims and verdicts mirror to the feed...' / 'a recorded verdict renders a timeline...' / 'the track record says what was recorded'
findings.what: The intro reads "What the feed has actually recorded: milestone verdicts and claims (the verdict word is approve or reject), settlement receipts with their tx...". The empty hint reads "Strengthen your proof line: record a milestone claim or a verdict ... The chain remains the ledger. This card only repeats what the feed says." Status words are "settled on-chain" and "No claim mirror for this milestone", and the badge shows the raw word "approve".
findings.why: This text sounds like a machine wrote it and is full of internals (feed, mirror, tx, ledger, code-formatted vocabulary). Even inside a 'Technical details' fold, people read it as the project's record.
findings.suggestion: Intro: "Milestones the team said were done, what reviewers decided, and what was paid." Empty: "Nothing recorded yet. When the team marks a milestone done, it shows here." Statuses: "Paid out" / "Decided, not paid yet" / "Waiting for a decision". Badge: "Approved" / "Rejected". Update the tests that assert 'approve' and 'settled on-chain'.

findings.spec: funding-status.spec.ts: 'a chip filters the list to that stance' (gap)
findings.what: The chip row is hidden whenever the current tab is empty (`filtered.length === 0 && "hidden"`), but stanceFilter and seekingFilter stay set when you change tabs. Scenario: choose 'Raising now' on All, then open Following (or Mine) where nothing matches. The page says "Nothing matches those filters. Try removing one." while the chips needed to remove the filter are hidden, and the Start an idea button is suppressed too.
findings.why: A guard hides the only way out (Review-Proven Rule 6), and the page tells people to remove a filter they cannot see.
findings.suggestion: Hide the chip row only when no stance or seeking filter is active (`filtered.length === 0 && stanceFilter === null && seekingFilter === null`), or clear both filters on tab change. Add a test: pick a chip, switch to an empty tab, and the chip can still be turned off.
findings.verifier: Verified. stanceFilter and seekingFilter are plain useState, and setFilter (line 298) never resets them. The chip row gets 'hidden' when filtered.length === 0 (line 338). filtered is the tab's list before the funding filter, so on an empty Following or Mine tab the chips disappear. The empty state then says 'Nothing matches those filters. Try removing one.' (line 444), and Start an idea is suppressed because a filter is set (line 459). The only way out is reloading or going back to a non-empty tab. The proposed guard and the regression test are right. Of the two fixes, keeping the row visible while a filter is active is better than clearing on tab change, because it keeps the person's choice.

findings.spec: launchpad-empty.spec.ts / funding-status.spec.ts
findings.what: The tab says "Sale completed", its empty state says "No launches have graduated yet." (line 456), and the card target says title="Raise needed to graduate" (LaunchCard.tsx:213). In the pilot's Ideas page, Mine says "You haven't launched anything yet." (452), Following says "Follow a launch to see it in this list." (457), and the card star is labelled "Follow launch" / "Unfollow launch" (LaunchCard.tsx:122).
findings.why: 'Graduate' is jargon, three words name one state, and 'launch' leaks into a build where nothing launches.
findings.suggestion: Use 'finished' throughout: empty "No sales have finished yet.", tooltip "Needed for the sale to go ahead". Mine: "You haven't started an idea or project yet." Following: "Nothing here yet. Follow an idea or project to see it here." Star aria-label: `Follow ${record.name}` / `Unfollow ${record.name}`.

findings.spec: launchpad.spec.ts: 'a production build shows no fabricated funding figures'
findings.what: The progress label reads "No chain data", with tooltip `No chain data: ${reason}` that shows raw reasons like "no auction contract linked". It sits beside OverviewTab.tsx:154, "This launch has no auction contract yet, so there are no live figures to show."
findings.why: 'Chain data' and 'auction contract' are crypto internals in main copy. A reader only needs to know whether the sale has started.
findings.suggestion: Label: "Not started" (or "Can't read right now" when the read failed). Body: "The sale hasn't started yet, so nothing has been raised." Drop the raw reason from the tooltip. Update the asserted strings.

findings.spec: launchpad.spec.ts: 'a project that does not lock the team's Shares...'
findings.what: Cards say "Team tokens unlock with N milestones", while every new launch is the project's own Shares and the powers card says "the team's Shares".
findings.why: Two names for the same holding on neighbouring screens. 'Tokens' is also the crypto word the copy standard avoids.
findings.suggestion: Use the record's own unit: "Team Shares unlock in {n} milestones" for DAO-mode records, and keep 'tokens' only for old minted records shown read-only.

findings.spec: launchpad-presets.spec.ts (both tests)
findings.what: The Standard preset's blurb is "The app's usual starting point." and the Small and Large blurbs only restate the numbers ("A smaller target, over a shorter sale."). The ETH targets (20/120/400 ETH) are fixed numbers that drift away from the dollar sizes as the price moves.
findings.why: "The app's usual starting point" sounds machine-written and doesn't help a first-time founder choose. Blurbs that say what each size suits would.
findings.suggestion: Small: "For a first version or a test run." Standard: "For a small team's first few months." Large: "For a team with a track record and a plan to show." For ETH, consider offering only USDC presets, or say the ETH sizes are rough.

findings.spec: sandbox.spec.ts: 'the preview frame cannot reach the app's origin' and 'an inline script in a srcdoc frame is blocked'
findings.what: Both tests create their own iframe with sandbox="allow-scripts" on '/'. They never render RepoBlobViewer's HtmlRunView (RepoBlobViewer.tsx:157). The origin test checks browser behaviour: if someone added allow-same-origin to RUN_SANDBOX, it would still pass. The file name also suggests the raise sandbox.
findings.why: Rule 3 (bind the production seam): the guard this spec claims to protect can be removed without any test failing.
findings.suggestion: Keep the CSP probe as it is. Replace the origin test with one that renders the real repo HTML preview (mock a repo blob with an .html file) and asserts the rendered iframe's sandbox attribute is exactly 'allow-scripts'. Rename the file repo-preview-sandbox.spec.ts and keep it in smoke.
findings.verifier: Half right. The CSP test does bind a production seam: it runs on the app's own page, so it exercises the app's real document policy and would fail if that policy were relaxed. The origin test only checks browser behaviour on an iframe it builds itself, so removing allow-same-origin protection from RUN_SANDBOX (RepoBlobViewer.tsx:157) would not fail it. Moving the file out of smoke is the wrong call. These are two sub-second tests guarding a security property (pushed code running in the app's origin), and repositories are still live in raise builds. Hidden in the pilot does not mean unreachable.

findings.spec: sandbox.spec.ts (the note it guards)
findings.what: The note reads "Sandboxed preview. The page's own scripts do not run here: the document's Content-Security-Policy applies to this frame, and relaxing it would also relax it for the app. Static content, styles and inlined assets render."
findings.why: This explains how the app is built instead of telling the person what to expect.
findings.suggestion: "Preview only: this page's scripts don't run here, so buttons and animations may not work. Text, styles and images show as they will."

findings.spec: launchpad.spec.ts: all tests (shared `published` array)
findings.what: `published` lives at module level and is never cleared in beforeEach (line 203). The mock relay replays every earlier test's 37001 back into the directory, so later tests see launches made by earlier ones. Three tests clear it by hand (317, 1069, 1083), and the agent test works around it with `[...published].reverse().find`.
findings.why: Tests depend on run order: running one alone or reordering them changes what the directory holds, and the 'directory badges it' assertion (`launch-agent-badge .first()`) could pass on a leftover launch.
findings.suggestion: Add `published.length = 0` to beforeEach next to the other served* resets, and drop the manual clears and the reverse() workaround.
findings.verifier: Verified. `published` (line 113) is module-level. beforeEach (lines 203-218) resets every served* variable but not `published`. The mock relay replays every earlier published 37001 whose d-tag is not 'nebula' into the directory (lines 170-184). Manual clears at 317, 1069 and 1083 and the [...published].reverse() searches at 670 and 772 are workarounds, and the comment at 668 says so. The directory therefore depends on run order. Adding `published.length = 0` to beforeEach is the right fix. The reverse() lookups can stay where one test publishes the same d-tag twice; they are harmless.

findings.spec: launchpad.spec.ts: 'a bid sends onchain before the mirror is allowed' and 'the main button follows the sale: bid while it is open, then claim tokens or a refund'
findings.what: The bid test asserts `bid-record` is disabled before any budget is typed, which is trivially true for an empty form, so it never shows the record step waits for a transaction hash. The 'main button' test's title promises 'bid while it is open', but it only loops over the failed and graduated stages.
findings.why: The titles claim guarantees the assertions do not check.
findings.suggestion: In the bid test, fill a valid bid, make the wallet's eth_sendTransaction reject, and assert no 47002 was published and the error says what to do. Add the 'live' stage to the loop, asserting 'Place bid' is visible, or rename the test.
findings.verifier: Verified. At line 479, bid-record is asserted disabled before any budget is filled, which an empty form gives anyway. The test does check that the published 47002 carries the wallet hash, but it never checks that nothing is mirrored when no hash exists. The 'main button' test (line 1106) loops only over 'failed' and 'graduated', so its 'bid while it is open' claim is unchecked; 'Place bid' is only asserted absent. Both suggestions are right. These are raise-only tests, so if finding 1 moves them out of smoke, this is low priority.

findings.spec: screenshots.spec.ts: 'the channel view renders a conversation'
findings.what: This is a screenshot harness running in smoke. Its one assertion (the first message is visible) is already covered by the channel specs, and it waits a fixed 400 ms then writes a PNG on every run. The seeded messages are raise-era ("the CCA sale parameters are in the launchpad doc", "the vesting table").
findings.why: It adds runtime and test-results noise and checks nothing new. Its sample chat also shows the product the pilot is not.
findings.suggestion: Run it only when E2E_SHOTS is set (test.skip otherwise), use waitForAnimations instead of waitForTimeout, and seed MVP-like messages (e.g. "I picked up the logo work area. Draft by Friday.").
findings.verifier: Verified. screenshots.spec.ts sits in smoke (playwright.config.ts:79), makes one visibility assertion, waits a fixed 400 ms and writes a PNG on every run. Its messages are raise-era ('CCA sale parameters', 'vesting table', 'treasury view'). The stated reason for them, side-by-side comparison with the desktop harness, no longer applies because desktop is outside the MVP. tests/helpers/animations.ts exists, so waitForAnimations is available. Gating it on E2E_SHOTS fits how web-screen-audit.sh and web-post-bounty-e2e.sh already use that variable.

findings.spec: funding-status.spec.ts: 'the chips count each stance and each wanted role'
findings.what: The directory shows two chip rows with 10 chips (Any, Not raising, Planning a raise, Raising now, Closing the raise, Raise closed, Rolling round; Anyone, Contributors, Backers, Advisors), including zero-count ones. The test asserts that 'closing' and 'advisors' show 0. The empty-state spec says chips that read zero are a problem, but zero chips stay visible whenever the list is not empty.
findings.why: Ten filters on a list that will hold a handful of projects is noise for newcomers. 'Rolling round' is jargon, and weekly rounds are off in the pilot.
findings.suggestion: In raise builds, hide chips whose count is 0 unless they are active, and update the funding-status test to assert that the zero chips are absent instead of reading '0'. Rename 'Rolling round' to 'Open to backers every week' in FUNDING_STANCE_LABELS, and check the card and wizard where the label also appears. Skip merging the rows until raises come back.
findings.verifier: The chips render only when raisesOffered() is true (LaunchesPage.tsx:335), so the pilot never sees them, and 'weekly rounds are off in the pilot' does not apply. In raise builds the noise problem is real: up to 10 chips, with zero-count ones shown, and 'Rolling round' is jargon. Merging the rows and dropping the stance filter is a larger redesign of a surface the MVP hides, so it is not worth doing now. FUNDING_STANCE_LABELS (lib/funding.ts:148) is shared, so a rename also changes card and wizard wording, which is fine but should be checked.

areas.area: Starting a contributor project and the Projects board
areas.summary: This area covers three different things that all say "project": the Start page's contributor-project form (the real MVP path), "Set up community" (a template that fills a community with channels, boards and pages, and still adds AI helpers), and the Projects board (pitches with % stakes, hidden in the contributor-only pilot build). The contributor-project form and its failure handling (locked passkey, server refusals, a missing project said only after a read that worked) are careful and well tested. The weak spots are the word "project" meaning three things, raise-build and agent-era copy and writes that leak into the pilot (the template setup still writes six AI helpers, their seats and a helper limit when the pilot hides helpers), and internal terms like "contributor kit" in user copy. On tests: every mocked spec here runs the raise build, so the pilot's copy is never checked. About a third of the tests (projects.spec.ts) cover a board the MVP hides, including four layout/theme permutations whose screenshots nobody compares.

findings.spec: start-project.spec.ts › a team is picked, set up step by step, and its first channel opens
findings.what: In the contributor-only build, community setup still plans and publishes every helper step: personas (kind 30175), six helper seats plus the founder seat (37010), the default helper limit (37012), automations and a skill. StartProject.tsx only hides the helper section of the preview (line 105, beyondContributorProjects()). use-template-apply.ts calls planApply(entry, existing) with no build filter. The 'What was set up' list then shows 'Helper: The Writer', 'Seat for …' and 'A default limit for helpers' to a pilot founder.
findings.why: DEPRECATION #6 says helpers are hidden where no helper can run. But a pilot owner who presses Set up community still gets helper records on the server, and the done screen lists helpers the build otherwise hides. Those records are left behind on a server with no AI service.
findings.suggestion: Give planApply (or useTemplateApply) a contributor-only option that drops persona, agent_seat, org:budget, automation and skill steps when beyondContributorProjects() is false. Add a unit test in apply.test.mjs proving the pilot plan has no 30175/37012 steps.
findings.verifier: Confirmed. use-template-apply.ts:165 calls planApply(entry, existing) with no build filter. apply.ts plans skill, persona, org root/seat/budget and workflow steps unconditionally. StartProject.tsx only hides things in the UI: the helper/limit lines in Preview (line 108) and the 'Choose where your AI helpers run' and 'See your team' buttons (lines 286 and 297). The 'What was set up' details still render every step result through Progress/describeStep. DEPRECATION #6 hides helpers wherever no helper can run, so writing their records on a pilot server goes against it. The fix (a contributor-only filter on the plan, plus a unit test in run-plan/apply tests) is the right shape. Keep the founder's own org seat only if something in the pilot reads it. Otherwise drop the org steps too.

findings.spec: start-project.spec.ts › a team is picked, set up step by step…
findings.what: The presets are titled 'Creative project' and 'Technical project', with blurbs 'Film, music, audio or any creative work, made with AI helpers.' and 'A web or app product, with a builder, a reviewer and a lead.' The count line is '4 channels · 2 boards · 6 AI helpers · 3 shared pages' (templateCounts, line 70). The empty community says 'Pick a creative or a technical project…' (CommunityShell.tsx:817). None of this creates a project: it adds rooms to a community. In the pilot build the AI helpers, builder, reviewer and lead are all hidden.
findings.why: A newcomer sees 'Creative project' under Set up community and 'Start a contributor project' on Start and will think they did the second. The helper counts and blurbs promise things the pilot does not have.
findings.suggestion: Rename the presets to 'For creative work' / 'For software' (or 'Creative community' / 'Software community'). Use blurbs without helpers in the pilot: 'Rooms and boards for film, music, audio or other creative work.' and 'Rooms and boards for building a web or app product.' Have templateCounts skip helpers when beyondContributorProjects() is false. Empty state: 'Pick what this community is for and it fills with rooms, boards and shared pages.'
findings.verifier: Confirmed in template-copy.ts:34-46. The PRESETS titles 'Creative project' and 'Technical project' and the blurbs 'made with AI helpers' and 'with a builder, a reviewer and a lead' are static. StartProject.tsx Option (lines 214-239) shows them, and templateCounts (line 239) shows '6 AI helpers' in every build, so the pilot sees helper promises the build otherwise hides. The 'More kinds of team' audiences (AI, crypto) leak the same way. 'Project' clashes with the contributor project that Start creates. The suggested renames and the helper-free blurbs and counts in the pilot are reasonable. Also gate templateAudience for the AI and crypto templates, or hide those templates, in the pilot.

findings.spec: start-project.spec.ts › a team is picked, set up step by step…
findings.what: The person picked 'Creative project', but the running screen says 'Setting up AI Media Studio' (line ~352, state.entry.template.name) and the done screen says 'Your community is set up' followed by 'AI Media Studio is set up. There is a welcome message in #writers-room.'
findings.why: They never saw the name 'AI Media Studio', and in the pilot 'AI' names something hidden. The done text also says 'set up' twice.
findings.suggestion: Use templatePreset(id)?.title ?? templateTitle(template) everywhere. Running: 'Setting up your community…'. Done body: 'There is a welcome message in #writers-room.' (drop the repeated sentence).

findings.spec: start-project.spec.ts › members see the restriction before setup… / a refusal after preflight…
findings.what: The button says 'Set up community', but the access line says 'Only this community's owner or an admin can set up its team. Ask one of them to do this.' The refusal says 'Only this community's owner or an admin can set up the team. Ask one of them to finish setup.' (explain.ts:34). The hidden legend is 'Choose a team' and the disclosure is 'More kinds of team'.
findings.why: 'Team' means the helper org chart, which the pilot has none of. A member reads 'team' and 'community' as two different things.
findings.suggestion: Say 'community' throughout: 'Only this community's owner or an admin can set it up. Ask one of them.'; 'Only this community's owner or an admin can finish setting it up. Ask one of them; what already went through is kept.'; legend 'Choose a starting point'; 'More starting points'.

findings.spec: start-project.spec.ts › someone without an account is asked to create one first / a community with no channels offers community setup…
findings.what: The empty-community prompt and its 'Set up community' button show to everyone, including plain members and signed-out visitors. A visitor is told 'Create account … to continue. Community setup needs an owner or admin account.' (StartProject.tsx:455). After signing up as a new account they hit 'You're not on this community's member list yet.'
findings.why: For anyone but the owner this is a dead end: they are walked through creating an account to do something they will not be allowed to do.
findings.suggestion: Show the button only when runsCommunity/offersSetup is true. For everyone else, show 'Nothing here yet. The person who runs this community hasn't set it up.' For signed-out visitors, offer 'Sign in' with 'If you run this community, sign in to set it up.' rather than Create account.
findings.verifier: Confirmed. CommunityShell.tsx already computes runsCommunity and offersSetup (lines 176-189) and uses them for the sidebar entry (line 433). The empty-community prompt at lines 810-830, though, shows 'Set up community' unconditionally. For a signed-out visitor, StartProject shows Create account (lines 451-463), and a new account then lands on the 'not on this community's member list yet' message. Gating the button on offersSetup and showing a plain 'nothing set up yet' line otherwise is right. For signed-out visitors, offering Sign in rather than Create account is the better path for an owner on a fresh browser. The spec tests at start-project.spec.ts:243-275 would need to change with it.

findings.spec: contributor-project.spec.ts › Start offers a contributor project…
findings.what: 'Contributor projects cannot be started on ${label} yet: this app does not know a contract there that makes one.' and 'This app does not know a currency on ${label} for contributors' optional deposits, so it cannot open a work budget there.' (line 94).
findings.why: These explain internals ('a contract that makes one', 'currency for optional deposits') and do not say what to do next. A founder cannot act on either.
findings.suggestion: 'Projects can't be started on ${label} yet. Ask the person who runs this Creaton server to turn them on.' Use the same sentence for the currency case.

findings.spec: contributor-project.spec.ts › a contributor project keeps its funds and the way to leave
findings.what: 'This project's DAO could not be checked against the contributor kit, so its money and the way to leave are not shown here.' 'Contributor kit' also shows on Discover cards ('Set up by the contributor kit' / 'Not set up by the contributor kit', DiscoverCards.tsx:102) and in a Start error (contributor-flow.ts:180).
findings.why: 'Contributor kit' is the contract's internal name, so this copy shows protocol internals.
findings.suggestion: Funds: 'We couldn't confirm this project was set up the standard way, so its money and how to leave aren't shown here.' Discover: 'Set up the standard way' / 'Not set up the standard way'.

findings.spec: contributor-project.spec.ts › anyone suggests work with a % ask…
findings.what: '8 Shares: 5.1% of the project once they are added to the 150 that exist now, so everyone else's part shrinks by that much.' The code comment (work-proposal.ts:170) says each holder keeps (1 − 5.1%) of what they had. A 10% holder goes to about 9.5%, not 4.9%.
findings.why: 'Shrinks by that much' reads as percentage points, which misstates the dilution: the exact thing a newcomer needs to get right before voting.
findings.suggestion: '8 Shares: 5.1% of the project once added to the 150 that exist now. Everyone else keeps 94.9% of what they hold.'

findings.spec: contributor-project.spec.ts › Start offers a contributor project… / anyone suggests work…
findings.what: The label 'Short name' means two things. On Start it is the Shares code ('A short code for the Shares, 2 to 8 letters or numbers, like CREA.', ContributorStartPage.tsx:444). In Suggest work it is the work area's name ('A word or two; the work area's name if it is approved.').
findings.why: The same label for different things on neighbouring screens makes people put the wrong thing in.
findings.suggestion: Start: label 'Shares code'. Suggest work: label 'Work area name'.

findings.spec: launchpad-shouldfix-start.spec.ts › the Start page says who the reviewers are…
findings.what: With two reviewers named, the page says 'Both must agree: … If they split, nothing is decided.' and 'If they split, or one doesn't answer, that piece of work stays stuck until its deadline passes. Name another reviewer.' But validation always refuses fewer than three ('Name at least 3 reviewers…', contributor-project.ts:410). The quorum error says 'a whole number from 1 to N' while the next rule demands at least 2 (lines 428-436). DEPRECATION #9 still describes 'two with Let any one decide'.
findings.why: The founder gets detailed advice about a two-reviewer setup they can never submit, then a different error on Start. The quorum range contradicts itself.
findings.suggestion: Under three reviewers, show one line: 'Name at least 3 reviewers (you have 2).' Change the quorum message to 'a whole number from 2 to ${n}'. Fix the stale note in DEPRECATION/CREATON-EXAMPLE-PROJECT. Update the test to assert the three-reviewer guidance instead of the two-reviewer state.

findings.spec: contributor-project.spec.ts › Start offers a contributor project…
findings.what: The form asks for name, pitch, Shares code, three Share numbers (starting Shares, Shares available for work, most for one work area), reviewers, how many must agree, how you know each reviewer, and per-work-area name, finish check and Shares. The budget must be at least three times the founder's Shares, and that rule only shows after a mistake.
findings.why: The target users have no business experience. Six number decisions on the first screen, with defaults that already work (100,000 / 300,000 / 25,000), is the most likely place they stall.
findings.suggestion: Put the short name, the three Share numbers and 'How many reviewers must agree' under a closed 'Change the numbers' disclosure. Keep name, what it is, reviewers, how you know each reviewer and the first work area visible, and always show the preview. Open the disclosure automatically when founderShareWarning or a field error points inside it, so the live warning is never hidden. Adding 'At least three times your starting Shares.' to the budget hint is optional, because the live warning already covers it.
findings.verifier: The form does put the short name, three Share numbers, reviewers, how many must agree and how you know each reviewer on the first screen (ContributorStartPage.tsx around lines 440-540), and the defaults work, so hiding the numbers is a sound idea. But the 3x rule does not only show after a mistake: founderShareWarning (contributor-project.ts:511, used at ContributorStartPage.tsx:254) is a live warning that appears as soon as you type past the limit, before Start is pressed. It is not shown ahead of time.

findings.spec: contributor-project.spec.ts › Start offers a contributor project…
findings.what: 'What people can work on from the first day. You manage each one: you accept each submission for review, the reviewers judge it, and Shareholders vote on the award.' Elsewhere on the same page it is 'the project votes on an award' (WhatItIs, line ~126) and 'Later budgets are voted like any other decision.'
findings.why: 'Shareholders' brings in corporate/securities vocabulary, and the page uses three phrasings for the same vote.
findings.suggestion: 'What people can work on from day one. You accept each piece of work for review, the reviewers check it, then the project votes on the award.'

findings.spec: projects.spec.ts (all 15 tests)
findings.what: The Projects board (/projects: pitches, % stakes, approve/ask-to-join grants, 'Start it as a contributor project') is hidden in the contributor-only build, because 'a pitch there would hand out Shares outside reviewed work'. Its copy is also far from plain: '8% recorded · 60% declared · 92% of the 100% pool', '1 need you' (BoardPage.tsx:46).
findings.why: It is not in the MVP and contradicts the MVP's core rule (Shares only from reviewed work). Yet 15 mocked tests, about a third of this area's runtime, keep it green, and the 'From a launch' pitch source carries raise-era concepts.
findings.suggestion: Leave the keep-or-retire decision to the owner as an open item in the DEPRECATION 'Waiting on you' table, since #4 chose gating. If suite time matters, move projects.spec.ts out of the 'smoke' testMatch into a separate Playwright project (for example 'later-features') that pilot iteration does not run by default. Separately, rewrite the board's numeric copy ('8% recorded · 60% declared · 92% of the 100% pool', '1 need you') in plain words if it stays.
findings.verifier: DEPRECATION-2026-10-31.md #4 already decided this: the Projects board was put behind the build gate, not removed (beyondContributorProjects in build-gates.ts:62). Retiring it is the owner's call about after the pilot, not a defect. useStartFromPitch/FromBoard and from-pitch.ts feed the Start form, so removing them is more than deleting one route. The fallback is also misdirected: scripts/mvp-gate.sh --later selects real-server journeys, while projects.spec.ts is a mocked Playwright spec in the 'smoke' project (playwright.config.ts:97), which --later does not control. The 'about a third of runtime' figure is not shown anywhere.

findings.spec: projects.spec.ts › pitch fields align and actions stay visible at {1280,390}px in {light,dark} mode
findings.what: Four permutations, each writing two dialog screenshots to the output path that nothing compares. Each also asserts pixel-level row alignment and computed colors (label color === heading color) for a dialog hidden in the MVP. The spec also imports waitForAnimations from desktop/tests/helpers (line 2), coupling the web suite to the desktop app the MVP drops.
findings.why: The screenshots prove nothing. The color-equality check is an implementation detail. Four runs of a hidden feature's layout cost suite time on every run.
findings.suggestion: Point the import at web/tests/helpers/animations (and do the same in the other two web specs). Drop the two unasserted screenshots. Run the dialog layout test at 390px only, but keep the dark theme for that one run, plus the keyboard, scroll and focus-return assertions. Or retire the test along with the board if the owner retires it.
findings.verifier: Part of this holds: the screenshots are written but never compared, and the spec imports waitForAnimations from desktop/tests/helpers. But web/tests/helpers/animations.ts already exists, so nothing needs moving, only the import (three web specs use the desktop path). The test also checks things worth keeping under Review-Proven Rule 8: Space activating the Add a role button, PageDown scrolling, the footer staying put, and Escape returning focus to the opener. The label-color equality was likely added to guard a dark-mode contrast regression, so dropping the theme loop loses that guard.

findings.spec: contributor-project.spec.ts › Start offers a contributor project… (and start-project.spec.ts)
findings.what: Every mocked spec here runs the default build (raisesOffered() is true unless VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1), so they assert the raise-build copy ('Start without a token sale', 'Starts without a token sale', the 'No token sale' chip). The pilot's own copy ('Build with contributors', 'How Shares work', no chip, no helpers in setup, 'rooms' in the empty state) is never asserted in this area. Only the real-server screen audit captures the hosted build.
findings.why: The pilot is the only build people will use, and pilot-only copy or gating regressions (such as the helper leak above) pass this suite unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: First, cover the gates with node unit tests by passing the env: planApply with the contributor-only filter yields no persona, 37012 or helper-seat steps, and templateCounts and the preset copy drop helpers when beyondContributorProjects is false. Then add a few pilot-copy assertions to passkey-contributor.spec.ts, which already runs a contributor-only build ('How Shares work' on /start, no sale steps), and a '/projects is unreachable' check to the hosted social suite. Add a contributor-only mocked Playwright project on E2E_DIST only if that proves insufficient.
findings.verifier: Mostly true: no mocked spec in this area sets VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY, and social-shouldfix-errors.spec.ts says outright that the mocked suite 'runs one ordinary build and cannot switch VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY'. But 'only the screen audit' is wrong. passkey-contributor.spec.ts runs on a VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1 build (scripts/web-passkey-contributor-e2e.sh:79) and visits /start, though it asserts no pilot copy. The hosted social suite also runs that build. The gates take the env as a parameter (beyondContributorProjects(given)), and the repo already pins contributor-only behaviour in unit tests (ideaSaleStepsContract.test.mjs). A second mocked build on another port is the heaviest option.

findings.spec: start-project.spec.ts › a team is picked, set up step by step, and its first channel opens
findings.what: One 90-second test covers the picker copy, two a11y scans, preview text including helper limits ('Each helper can run 200 times, start 20 tasks'), exact event counts for nine kinds, the founder seat payload, opening the channel, and both boards. The retry test repeats most of the same counts.
findings.why: A failure anywhere hides everything after it. The helper-count assertions encode the very behaviour the pilot should not have, so fixing the helper leak would break this test for the wrong reason.
findings.suggestion: Optional, low priority. Split the test into a no-write picker and preview test and a 'what it writes' test (channels, boards, first posts, pages, plus the helper and seat counts for the default build), so a failure early does not hide later checks. Assert that helpers are absent through the unit-level plan test for contributor-only builds rather than in this spec.
findings.verifier: The test does run long (90s timeout) and asserts helper counts (30175 x6, 37010 x7, 37012 x1, the '200 times' preview line). But the claim that fixing the helper leak would break it for the wrong reason does not hold. The fix would be gated on the contributor-only build, and this spec runs the default build, where helpers are legitimately offered, so these assertions stay correct. The retry test also uses the 37010 org-seat refusal as its failure seam. A pilot variant would need a different seam, such as a channel or page write.

findings.spec: launchpad-shouldfix-start.spec.ts › the Start page says who the reviewers are…
findings.what: 'Nobody here has linked an account to their name yet. Ask each reviewer to press "Show your name with this account", then try again.' It does not say where that button is.
findings.why: The founder has to pass the instruction on to three other people, and none of them will know where to look.
findings.suggestion: 'Nobody here has linked their name to an account yet. Ask each reviewer to open their profile menu and press "Show your name with this account", then press Try again.'

areas.area: Contributor journeys on a real local chain (structure, check note, challenge, newcomer, AI helpers)
areas.summary: These two opt-in specs drive the whole contributor loop against a real Anvil chain. A founder starts a project and sets Aim/Now/Not doing. A contributor takes on a piece, with an optional AI interview, and submits work after an optional AI self-check. The founder writes a check note, a manager accepts the work, two reviewers approve, the contributor marks it finished, and the founder opens an award vote with a challenge. A reader then sees who earned what. The passkey spec repeats the core loop with no browser wallet, then adds recovery on a second device, sending money and leaving. As tests they are rigorous and falsifiable, because chain state is checked after almost every UI step. But the main journey is one 500-line test that bundles many off-MVP extras (bounties, forecasts, payouts, remix bonds), runs on a build the pilot never ships, and skips entirely in the mocked suite. That means the newest working-cycle features (Now, take-on, check note, challenge, New here) have no browser coverage in the pilot build. On the product side the loop works, but it asks too much of beginners. It takes about 10 actions from 4 people to earn Shares, including a pointless "Mark it finished" after an 8-day wait. One concept has five names ("words", "Done when", "What finished work looks like", "How it should be judged", "acceptance check"). Several strings leak internal reasoning or jargon ("challenge window", "Set Now", "Its vote is open; publishing the words does not open it again").

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: 'a contributor project is started from the page...' (steps 3, 'Mark it finished' then award)
findings.where: contracts/src/ClaimStake.sol:373 (payout: msg.sender must be contributor) + web/src/features/launchpad/ui/decision-forms.tsx:405-413 (award needs status Paid) + packages/creaton-core/src/launchpad/work.ts:666-681
findings.what: A claim that asked for no money still needs the contributor to come back after the challenge wait (the spec advances 700,000 s, about 8 days) and press "Mark it finished". Only the contributor can press it (contract and UI both check), and until they do, the award form says "No approved work is waiting for an award." Before that, someone also has to press "Finish the review" (settle) after the last approval.
findings.why: For a Shares-only project this button does nothing the person can see, but it blocks their own award. A contributor who doesn't come back after a week (common with beginners) never gets awarded, and the founder can't fix that. The journey to earn Shares is submit, accept, 2 approvals, settle, 8-day wait, finish, propose, vote, start wait, run: about 10 actions by 4 people.
findings.suggestion: Now, with no contract change: put the date in the Approved line ('Approved. On <date> you can mark it finished so the project can vote on your Shares.'), and put 'Mark it finished' in the contributor's Needs you list once the window opens. In the award form, list approved Shares-only claims that are still waiting on the contributor, as 'waiting for <name> to mark it finished', so the founder isn't told 'No approved work is waiting'. As a separate item for the audit backlog: let anyone call payout when amount and stake are both 0, and have the approval that reaches quorum settle the claim.
findings.verifier: The friction is real. AwardForm lists only claims with status Paid. ClaimStake.payout reverts unless msg.sender is the contributor and the challenge window has passed. The status line in work.ts says only 'It can be marked finished once the challenge window ends', with no date. But two parts of the suggestion don't hold up. ClaimStake is in the audit scope, and the award runs through the DAO, which is not the contributor, so 'have the award run the finish step' can't work without a contract change.

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: submitFromWaysToHelp / Start form / pending words
findings.what: One concept has five names. The Start form says "What finished work looks like", Ways to help says "Done when", and the submit form says "How it should be judged", with the placeholder "The work area's acceptance check, in its exact words". The submit form's note says "These are the words Docs was set up with." and "How you checked it against those words", and the pending note says "The words for the work area … are not published yet". The spec also fills work-claim-met with "Checked it against the work area's words".
findings.why: Someone new can't tell that "the words", "Done when" and "How it should be judged" are the same thing. "The words" on its own reads like an internal term. "Check" is also reused for the check note and "Check by", which adds to the confusion.
findings.suggestion: Use "Done when" everywhere. Start form: "Done when" with hint "Reviewers judge every submission against this. It can't be changed later." Submit form label: "Done when (from the work area)"; note: "Copied from Docs. If you change it, the work can't be accepted for review."; met label: "How you checked it's done". Pending note: "Docs's \"Done when\" isn't published yet, so people can't see what finished work looks like."
findings.verifier: I checked every string. The Start form says 'What finished work looks like', Ways to help says 'Done when', and the submit form says 'How it should be judged', with the placeholder 'The work area's acceptance check, in its exact words' and the note 'These are the words X was set up with.' The pending note says 'The words for the work area … are not published yet', and the AI button says 'Check my work against the words with AI'. Using 'Done when' everywhere is plain and consistent. Rename the AI button the same way: 'Check my work against Done when'.

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: 'a contributor project is started from the page, work is claimed the same day, and the award shows on its contributions'
findings.what: One test of about 830 lines with a 10-minute timeout covers start, founder limits, Now, take-on, interview, New here, check note, AI self-check, funds, bounty, forecast, runway, review, challenge, award, contributions, bounty refund and revenue payouts. The script builds it with VITE_DAO_LAUNCH_KITS, bounties, payouts, remix bonds, courts and CREATE: a raise-capable build, not the contributor-only pilot build.
findings.why: A failure in an early, off-MVP step (bounty, forecast) hides every later MVP step and costs a 10-minute rerun. The pilot build (VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1) never runs the working-cycle features this journey exercises. The only pilot-shaped journey, the passkey spec, skips Now, take-on, check note, challenge and New here.
findings.suggestion: Move bounty, forecast, runway, revenue payouts and bounty refund into their own spec. That spec launches its own project, or starts from a saved chain state after the core journey. The core MVP journey (start, Now, take-on, check note, review, challenge, award, contributions) then no longer depends on them. Run that core journey a second time in a VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1 build, with assertions that hold in both builds.
findings.verifier: The test is monolithic, and the script builds with the raise, bounty, payouts, remix, court and CREATE flags. But in Playwright's serial mode, a failure in one test still skips every later test, so splitting into a serial describe only improves reporting. It does not let the MVP steps run after an off-MVP step fails. Building the core journey in contributor-only mode would also hide flows the journey uses.

findings.spec: mocked smoke suite (no spec): check note, take-on, New here, challenge, AI helpers
findings.what: A grep of web/tests/e2e finds check-note-*, take-on-*, new-here-*, decision-challenge-*, work-claim-ai-* and focus-set only in these two opt-in specs. Both are skipped in the mocked suite, so in the run the user asked for, these features show as skipped, not passed.
findings.why: The newest working-cycle features (D165-D168) only get browser coverage when someone runs the slow chain scripts. Copy or UI regressions in the aim/Now/check-note cards go unnoticed in normal CI.
findings.suggestion: Add a mocked spec (mock bridge plus stubbed relay plus routed /llm) for the Overview working cycle: Set Now with the "Check by" rule, take on and let go, the interview with the must-read draft gate, check note with Apply to Now after a failed save, the challenge brief on a vote, and the AI-unavailable (404) path where these buttons are absent and forms still save.
findings.verifier: A grep of web/tests/e2e finds check-note-, take-on-, new-here-, decision-challenge-, work-claim-ai and focus-set only in contributor-journey.spec.ts. The finding says two specs, but it is only one, which makes the gap even wider. That spec is test.skip'd without E2E_ANVIL_URL/E2E_KIT/E2E_CONTRIBUTOR, so the mocked run never exercises these features.

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: second test 'several people earn...' (built on Docs Commons)
findings.what: `docsCommonsPublished = true` is set before the founder-limit checks and before the launch is submitted. If test 1 fails at any later step before the publish, test 2 still waits for a "Docs Commons" option in contributor-built-on and fails there.
findings.why: One failure becomes two: test 2's failure is a red herring that points at remixes, not at what actually broke.
findings.suggestion: Set the flag only after `contributor-done` is visible (after line 288), or better, derive builtOn from `published.some(e => e.kind === 37001 && content includes "Docs Commons")`.
findings.verifier: Line 253 sets docsCommonsPublished = true before the founder-limit checks and before the launch submit and contributor-done (about 288). Test 2 reads it at 1145 and waits 30 s for a 'Docs Commons' option. If test 1 fails in between, test 2 fails on a misleading remix step. The fix is to move the assignment to just after contributor-done is visible.

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: first test, step 4 (challenge before the award)
findings.what: The spec pushes a signed kind-37017 wallet link straight into the stub server's `published` list, with the comment "as the profile's Payment wallet does". It doesn't go through the UI. The challenge then counts only because of this injected record.
findings.why: The real prerequisite, linking the account to the name, is the step a founder is most likely to miss. The composer's own escape is "clear the answers to open the vote without them", and that whole path is skipped in the wallet journey.
findings.suggestion: Drive the link from the page (the Payment wallet card, or the AccountNameLink button the passkey spec already uses), or add a short step that first opens the challenge unlinked and asserts decision-challenge-unlinked, then links in the UI.
findings.verifier: Around line 805 the spec pushes a signed kind-37017 record into the stub's published list, 'as the profile's Payment wallet does', instead of linking through the UI. decision-challenge-unlinked (ChallengeQuestions.tsx:228) is never asserted in any spec. Asserting the unlinked state first and then linking in the UI would cover the step founders are most likely to miss.

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: step 4 challenge; passkey-contributor.spec.ts step 6 award
findings.what: When the account isn't linked, the challenge says: "This account isn't linked to the wallet that opens the vote, so holders would not see your answers. Link it under Payment wallet on your profile, or clear the answers to open the vote without them."
findings.why: This sends the founder to another page, and it suggests deleting their case against the vote to get past a technical prerequisite. That works against the feature's purpose. For a passkey user it also says "wallet", and the fix ("Show your name with this account") is already on the Work tab.
findings.suggestion: Inline the link action in the challenge fieldset: AccountNameLink for passkey accounts, and the payment-wallet link flow for browser wallets. New wording: 'Holders can't see these answers until your name is linked to this account. Link it now, then open the vote.' Keep a smaller second option such as 'Open the vote without the answers'. Don't present deleting the case as the main fix. Change the failure text at :303 to match.
findings.verifier: The quoted string is correct, and it does send the founder off the page. But AccountNameLink only works for a passkey account (it takes PasskeyAccountKeys), so it can't be reused for a browser-wallet founder. Dropping the 'clear the answers' escape also leaves no way back if linking fails (Review-Proven Rule 6).

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: step 3 'work-payout' after pass(700_000)
findings.what: "Approved. It can be marked finished once the challenge window ends." and "Approved. The payment can be taken once the challenge window ends."
findings.why: "Challenge window" is internal vocabulary. It gives no date and doesn't say who has to act.
findings.suggestion: "Approved. On {date} you can mark it finished. Until then, Shareholders can still question it." (money: "…you can take the payment…")

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: submitFromWaysToHelp (work-claim-name 'write-docs')
findings.what: "Up to 32 characters, without accents. Fixed work gets a new title." The specs also type slugs ("write-docs", "translate-es"), so the asserted outcomes read "11 Shares for Translate es in the work area Translate the guide to Spanish" (ContributionsTab.tsx:185).
findings.why: "Fixed work gets a new title" is cryptic, and "without accents" will surprise the Spanish-translation contributor in this very journey. Real users type titles (the placeholder is "e.g. First draft of the guide"), but the tests only prove that slug-to-title conversion produces awkward text.
findings.suggestion: Hint: "Up to 32 letters (no accents). If you resubmit after fixing it, give it a new title." Award line: "25 Shares for “Write docs” (Docs)". In the specs, type realistic titles ("Write the docs", "Spanish translation") so the asserted strings are what users see.

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: check note step ('check-note-next-0' selectOption 'change')
findings.what: The label "Knowing what you know now, would you start it today?" is a yes/no question, but its options are "Keep it / Change it / Drop it".
findings.why: The question and the answers don't match, which makes a founder stop and reread.
findings.suggestion: Label: "What happens to it next?" Hint: "Knowing what you know now, would you start it today?"

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: check note step (asserts check-note-problem 'what changed' right after opening)
findings.what: The check-note form shows a red role="alert" error ("Say what changed for the people the project is for…") the moment it opens, before the founder has typed anything. The take-on form only shows errors after the user tries to save (`tried`).
findings.why: The founder is greeted with an error, and screen readers announce it as an alert. It also behaves differently from the other forms on the same page.
findings.suggestion: Gate the problem text on a `tried` flag like TakeOnWork does (keep Publish disabled, but use a neutral hint until the first press). Update the spec to assert the button state instead of the alert at open.
findings.verifier: CheckNoteCard computes problem from checkNoteProblem(note) with no 'tried' gate, and renders it at :527-533 with role="alert" as soon as the form opens. TakeOnWork gates its problem on `tried` (line 86). Gating it the same way, while keeping Publish disabled, is the consistent fix.

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: take-on, check note and challenge AI drafts
findings.what: The same "you must read the AI's draft" gate is worded three ways. Buttons: "Keep this draft" vs "I've read it: keep this summary". Errors: "Read the draft the AI wrote, then keep it or change it." vs "Read the summary the AI drafted, then accept it or change it." (the button says keep, the error says accept).
findings.why: Inconsistent wording for one rule. "Accept" doesn't match any button on screen.
findings.suggestion: Use one button, "Keep this draft", everywhere, and one message: "The AI wrote this draft. Read it, then keep it or change it."

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: take-on interview (three 'Next' clicks then 'Draft it for me')
findings.what: After the third question, "Next" leads to a screen with nothing but "Draft it for me". There is no Back or Close for the interview. The note says "Your answers are not published", although they are sent to the AI service.
findings.why: The extra screen is a wasted click, and someone who opened the interview by mistake can't leave it. The privacy line is slightly misleading.
findings.suggestion: Make the last question's button 'Draft it for me' and add a 'Back' button. A separate Close isn't needed, since the form's Cancel already exists, though a 'Fill it in myself' link that hides the interview would help. Note: 'Your answers go only to the AI, not to the project. You read and change the draft before saving.'
findings.verifier: The extra screen is real: after the last question, 'Next' leads to a screen with only 'Draft it for me'. But the person is not stuck. The interview sits inside take-on-form, which has its own Cancel (TakeOnWork.tsx:280), and the form fields are right there to fill directly. The privacy note is roughly accurate (nothing is published), but it leaves out that the answers go to the AI.

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: focus-set / Now card
findings.what: The card heading is "Now" and the founder's button is "Set Now". "Now" is used as a proper noun across New here, the check note ("Apply to Now", "are not in Now yet") and the take-on chip.
findings.why: Someone new reads "Set Now" as "set it now". Making a common word into a capitalised product term is the kind of in-house vocabulary the copy standard warns against.
findings.suggestion: Heading: "What we're working on now"; button: "Set priorities". "Apply to Now" becomes "Update the priorities", and "are not in Now yet" becomes "aren't in the priorities yet".

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: take-on form
findings.what: The "By when" hint: "If it passes, the work is open again and nobody is blamed."
findings.why: "If it passes" can be read as "if the work passes review".
findings.suggestion: "If the date goes by, the piece is open to others again. Nobody is blamed."

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: New here (onlooker ticks step 1 only)
findings.what: Step 3 of "New here?" is "Read the next check note…": a passive step that waits on the founder's next note. None of the three steps is "submit your work", which is the step that actually leads to Shares.
findings.why: For people with no business experience, the useful last step is the one that leads to review and Shares. Waiting for a founder's retro is not an action they can take, so the card can sit unfinished for weeks.
findings.suggestion: Keep three steps but make step 3 something the person can do: 'Submit what you took on for review; the next check note says how it went.' Tick it on either a filed claim or a later check note. Add spec steps that tick steps 2 and 3.
findings.verifier: Step 3 was a deliberate choice in CHECK-AND-NEWCOMER-PLAN.md: the card teaches the team's cycle and goes away once a check note follows the person's take-on. Replacing that step drops the design intent. The concern still holds: the step is passive, so the card can sit unfinished for weeks. It is also true that the spec only ticks step 1.

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: second test, pending words (refuseWorkAreaWords)
findings.what: "The words for the work area “guide-es” are not published yet, so people cannot read what finished work in it looks like. Its vote is open; publishing the words does not open it again." It shows the slug (idLabel) rather than the suggestion's title, which D146 uses elsewhere.
findings.why: The second sentence explains the developer's retry logic, not what the user should do. The slug "guide-es" doesn't match "Translate the guide to Spanish", the name shown on the Work tab.
findings.suggestion: "“Translate the guide to Spanish” is missing its “Done when”, so people can't see what finished work looks like. Your vote is fine." Button: "Publish it". Use the area's title, not idLabel(job.id).

findings.spec: passkey-contributor.spec.ts: steps 1, 3, 4, 6 (work-wallet / decisions-wallet / contributor-account-wallet)
findings.what: "You act with your account (passkey; fees are covered on the test network)."
findings.why: "You act with your account" sounds machine-made, and the parenthetical reads like a code comment. This line is on every project tab for every pilot user.
findings.suggestion: "You're signed in with your passkey. Fees are paid for you on this test network."

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts step 5 / second test step 8 (contribution-person-held); passkey step 8 (ragequit)
findings.what: "Holds 25 now (11.1% of all Shares now)." says "now" twice. "This account holds no shares, so there is nothing to leave with." uses lowercase "shares", while "Shares" is capitalised everywhere else.
findings.why: Small things, but they repeat on a page the pilot points everyone to, and the capitalisation is inconsistent with the rest of the app.
findings.suggestion: "Holds 25 today, 11.1% of all Shares." / "This account holds no Shares, so there is nothing to take out."

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: first test, 'contributor-no-raise' heading
findings.what: The spec asserts "Starts without a token sale". The contributor-only (pilot) build shows "How Shares work" instead, so this assertion only holds in a raise-capable build.
findings.why: The journey is tied to the raise build. Running it the way the pilot ships would fail on a heading, not on behaviour. The assertion also checks wording that the pilot deliberately hides.
findings.suggestion: Assert a line both builds share ("New Shares come only from awards"), or branch on the build like ContributorStatusNote does.
findings.verifier: ContributorStartPage.tsx:116 renders 'Starts without a token sale' only when `raises` is true, and 'How Shares work' otherwise. The spec asserts the raise-build heading. Assert a line both builds share, such as 'New Shares come only from awards'.

findings.spec: contributor-journey.spec.ts: submitFromWaysToHelp with aiCheck
findings.what: The AI self-check's `gaps` are never cleared when evidence, met or notMet change, and a slow reply isn't checked against the inputs it was asked about. A contributor who fixes their evidence keeps seeing the old "I could not open the link…" list. A reply that arrives after an edit is shown as if it were about the new text.
findings.why: Stale AI advice next to an edited form misleads the person right before they submit (Review-Proven Rule 2: fence async results).
findings.suggestion: Clear `gaps` when any input changes, and keep a request counter or a snapshot of the inputs so a reply is applied only if the inputs are unchanged. Add a spec step that edits the evidence after the check and asserts work-claim-ai-gaps is gone.
findings.verifier: In WorkCheckAi, `gaps` is set only by check(). It is never cleared when doneWhen, evidence, met or notMet change, and an in-flight reply isn't checked against the inputs it was asked about. Old advice stays next to edited text. Clear gaps when the inputs change, and apply a reply only if the inputs are still the same.

areas.area: Work, review, paid work, decisions and project discussion
areas.summary: This area covers the core contributor loop: submitting work, a manager accepting it for review, reviewers approving or turning it down, "finishing" the review, the waiting period, marking the work finished, and the DAO vote that awards Shares. It also covers the Decisions tab (opening, backing, waiting and running votes), board discussions tied to a decision, and leaving a project. The safety work is careful: turn-down reasons are checked, people are re-asked before giving up Shares, and a busy node gets a plain message. But the loop asks too much of people with no business experience. Shares-only work needs about eight separate presses across three tabs and a 7-day wait. "Finish" means two different things. The same state goes by different names on different screens ("Rejected"/"turned down", "challenge window"/"waiting period", "project"/"work area"). For the team, the biggest risk is that most of this area's specs (work, paid-work, decisions, discussion) skip themselves when no local chain is running. A green mocked run therefore proves nothing about submitting, approving, settling, payout or voting. Only the turn-down path, the busy-node message and the leave dialog are really exercised there.

findings.spec: launchpad-work.spec.ts / launchpad-paid-work.spec.ts / launchpad-decisions.spec.ts / launchpad-discussion.spec.ts (all tests)
findings.what: Four of the seven specs call test.skip unless E2E_ANVIL_URL/E2E_DAO are set, yet they are listed in the mocked 'smoke' project (playwright.config.ts:32,54,55,57). In the mocked run they show as skipped and nothing fails. Across the whole mocked suite, no test that runs submits work, accepts it for review, approves it, settles it, takes the payout, or backs and runs a decision: every spec that clicks work-claim-submit, work-approve, work-bind, work-payout or decision-vote-for is gated on anvil.
findings.why: The owner's question, 'does the mocked suite pass', gets a misleading yes. A regression in the happy path of the product's core loop (FileClaimCard, ReviewActions approve, settle, payout, DecisionCard vote) would only be caught by a run that needs a local chain script.
findings.suggestion: Add a mocked happy-path spec on the stateful /test-rpc stub from launchpad-shouldfix-work. It should submit, accept, approve twice, finish the review, advance the clock and mark it finished. Add a second spec that backs and runs a decision. If the chain-backed specs move to their own 'chain' project, change the --project flag in every scripts/web-*-e2e.sh and journey script at the same time. Otherwise, make the mocked run report its skipped specs by name, so a skip is never read as a pass.
findings.verifier: The gap is real. launchpad-work, paid-work, decisions and discussion all test.skip without E2E_ANVIL_URL, and so do contributor-journey, launchpad-journey and rounds-journey. No spec that runs in the mocked suite clicks work-claim-submit, work-approve, work-payout or decision-vote-for. Two corrections. First, the mocked suite does reach one settle: launchpad-shouldfix-work.spec.ts:555-556 clicks work-settle, but only for a turn-down. Second, these specs sit in 'smoke' on purpose. scripts/web-work-e2e.sh:36 and web-decisions-e2e.sh:42, and the other journey scripts, run them with --project=smoke, and scripts/mvp-gate.sh runs them as the chain-backed gate. Moving them to another project means updating every one of those scripts in the same change.

findings.spec: launchpad-work.spec.ts › a claim goes from filed to taken…; launchpad-shouldfix-work.spec.ts › two reviewers turn work down…
findings.what: After the deciding approval or turn-down, someone still has to come back and press 'Finish the review' or 'Close it as turned down' (a separate settle transaction). Nothing happens until they do: the waiting period does not start (dao-overview.ts:415 says 'Its challenge window starts only once the review is finished.'). For Shares-only work the contributor then waits 7 days, presses 'Mark it finished' (a transaction that moves no money), and someone must open an award vote that goes through review, a hold, 'Start the wait' and 'Make it take effect'.
findings.why: Steps that only exist so someone presses a button are where newcomers stall. A claim whose verdict is clear but that nobody 'finished' sits in limbo with its waiting period not running, and the contributor cannot tell why.
findings.suggestion: When a reviewer's answer reaches the quorum, send attest and settle together through onSendBatch (FileClaimCard already uses it), so the deciding vote also finishes the review. As a fallback, keep the separate button for wallets that cannot batch. Longer term, consider letting the award vote be opened straight from an approved claim without the separate 'Mark it finished' transaction, which needs a contract change to ClaimStake.payout for zero-amount claims.
findings.verifier: The finding holds. ClaimStake.settle (contracts/src/ClaimStake.sol:337-367) has no time condition: it only checks that the approval or objection count has reached quorum and sets releasedAt there, which starts the challenge window. So settle can run right after the deciding attest, in the same batch. WorkTab shows a separate work-settle button, and ReviewActions sends only the attest through onSend. Keeping a fallback button for wallets that cannot batch is right. One caveat: the client's quorum count can be stale. If it is, a batched settle reverts and takes the approval down with it, so on failure send the attest alone. The award-without-payout part needs a contract change, as the finding says.

findings.spec: launchpad-work.spec.ts › a claim goes from filed to taken…
findings.what: 'Finish' means two different actions. The settle button is "Finish the review" and its step reads "Enough reviewers approved it. Anyone can finish it." (packages/creaton-core/src/launchpad/work.ts:607). Seven days later the payout button is "Mark it finished" (WorkTab.tsx:910), with "Approved. The contributor can mark it finished now…" (work.ts:674) and the status chip "Finished".
findings.why: A contributor who already pressed 'finish' once will think it is done and never come back for the second press, so the work is never awardable.
findings.suggestion: Settle: button 'Confirm the approval', step 'Enough reviewers approved it. Anyone can confirm it, and the 7-day wait starts then.' Shares-only payout: button 'Make it ready for a Shares award', step 'Approved and past the wait. The contributor can now make it ready for a Shares award.' Also replace 'challenge window' in the Approved-state text (work.ts:681-682) with 'the 7-day wait'.
findings.verifier: The strings are as quoted: 'Finish the review' and 'Anyone can finish it.' (work.ts:607), then 'Mark it finished' and 'can mark it finished now' (work.ts:674) with a 'Finished' chip. The same verb for two different steps is a real trap. But 'Send it to the vote' is wrong for payout: payout does not open a vote, someone still opens the award decision separately. 'Mark it done' just repeats the same confusion.

findings.spec: launchpad-shouldfix-work.spec.ts › two reviewers turn work down…
findings.what: The status chip shows raw contract states. claimStatusLabel (work.ts:310) only maps Paid to Finished, so people see "Open", "Rejected", "Expired" and "Recovered". The rest of the screen says "Turned down by the reviewers" and "Close it as lapsed". A defeated decision is also labelled "Rejected" (decision-stage.ts:54), so one word covers two different outcomes.
findings.why: The contributor reads 'Rejected' (harsh, and it sounds final) on a chip next to 'Turned down… To try again, fix the work and submit it under a new name'. 'Recovered' means nothing to a newcomer.
findings.suggestion: Map every status in claimStatusLabel: Open→"In review", Approved→"Approved", Rejected→"Turned down", Expired→"Lapsed", Recovered→"Rejected by vote", Frozen→"Frozen". Keep "Voted down" for decisions (decision-stage.ts:54).

findings.spec: launchpad-work.spec.ts › a claim goes from filed to taken…
findings.what: One wait has two names. "Approved. The payment can be taken once the challenge window ends." / "…marked finished once the challenge window ends." (work.ts:680-684), "once the challenge window ends" (dao-overview.ts:175) and "Its challenge window starts only once the review is finished." (dao-overview.ts:415) all call it the challenge window. FileClaimCard.tsx:454 ("after a waiting period"), milestone-timeline.ts:158 and milestone-progress.ts:139 call it the waiting period.
findings.why: Two names for one wait make people think there are two waits. 'Challenge window' is also unexplained jargon.
findings.suggestion: Use "waiting period" everywhere, and give its length when known, e.g. "Approved. It can be marked done after the 7-day waiting period (ends Nov 9)."

findings.spec: launchpad-paid-work.spec.ts › a DAO pays a contributor…; launchpad-decisions.spec.ts › a decision opened elsewhere…
findings.what: The budget vote still says "project" for what the app now calls a work area: "Shares for work: 100 in all, at most 40 per project", "Money for work: … per project" (lines 267, 272, 718, 723). The errors do the same: "Money for work needs a limit per project…", "The limit per project cannot be more than…" (175-187), "The project manager" (338) and "A project needs some Shares, some money, or both." (346). The vote right next to them is titled "Approve the work area …" (744).
findings.why: In a contributor project, 'project' is the whole thing. A voter reading 'at most 40 per project' cannot tell that this is the cap per work area.
findings.suggestion: "Shares for work: 100 in all, at most 40 per work area"; "The work area's manager"; "A work area needs some Shares, some money, or both." Update the two spec assertions to match.

findings.spec: launchpad-work.spec.ts › a claim goes from filed to taken…
findings.what: An empty 'How it should be judged' box gets the same error as an empty 'Where the work is' box: "Say where the work is, and how it should be judged." (lines 220 and 232). The title hint reads "Up to 32 characters, without accents. Fixed work gets a new title." (line 535). The spec asserts only the substring "where the work is", so it cannot tell the two errors apart.
findings.why: Someone who filled in where the work is and is then told to 'say where the work is' will not see what is missing. 'Fixed work gets a new title' is cryptic.
findings.suggestion: Check field: "Pick the work area this is for, so its words fill this in." Hint: "Up to 32 letters, no accents. If you resubmit fixed work, give it a new title." In the spec, assert the check-field error separately.

findings.spec: launchpad-work.spec.ts › a claim goes from filed to taken…
findings.what: The form asks the contributor to supply 'How it should be judged' in "the work area's acceptance check, in its exact words". Once an area is picked, the box is filled in and locked. The only other paths, 'Use different words' and 'Not sure yet' with your own words, produce a submission that "cannot be accepted for review" (the noAreaProblem/wordsProblem refusals). Altogether the form has eight inputs: area, title, where, words, how you checked, not met yet, AI check and payment.
findings.why: The free-text path exists only to fail, and an editable box with a scary warning confuses people. The MVP audience needs a short form: pick the area, give a title, say where the work is and how you checked it.
findings.suggestion: When the chosen area has published words, show them as read-only 'Done when: …' text and remove 'Use different words'. Keep the typed box only when the area's words are not published or the budget has no areas. When areas exist, require one (drop 'Not sure yet' typed words, which noAreaProblem refuses anyway).
findings.verifier: Typing your own words is not only a path to failure. FileClaimCard.tsx:588 covers a work area whose words are not published here, where the contributor has to get them from the manager and type them. It also covers budgets with no work areas, where budgetAreas is empty. Removing free text would make claims impossible in both cases. Where the words are published, though, 'Use different words' (line 608) can only produce a refused submission, because wordsProblem rejects any change.

findings.spec: launchpad-shouldfix-work.spec.ts › two reviewers turn work down…; an unlinked reviewer can still turn work down without a reason
findings.what: Approve is sent on the first press with no confirmation, though it is just as final as a turn-down, while 'Turn it down' opens a form. A turn-down's reason and cause are both optional. A reviewer whose account is not linked can only turn work down with no reason at all. The test 'an unlinked reviewer can still turn work down without a reason' pins that path down as intended behaviour.
findings.why: A contributor who is turned down with no reason learns nothing ('The Work tab shows who, and their reasons if they gave any'). That is the worst first experience for someone new. A mis-click on Approve cannot be undone.
findings.suggestion: Require the 'What was missing?' cause when the reason can be shown (a linked account). Keep the no-reason path only for unlinked accounts and for publish failures. Offer wallet linking inline for non-passkey reviewers, if that flow can be embedded. Skip the extra Approve confirm, or just add a line under the button: 'Approving is final.'
findings.verifier: Part of this holds: the turn-down cause is optional, so a contributor can be turned down with nothing to learn from. But the no-reason path is a deliberate fallback (D145). A reason from an unlinked account would never be shown, and when publishing the reason fails, the reviewer is told to send the verdict without one (ReviewActions.tsx:118-119). Requiring a cause in every case would block a reviewer's verdict on a relay failure or on account linking. An Approve confirm is weak: the send already goes through a wallet or passkey prompt.

findings.spec: launchpad-shouldfix-work.spec.ts › a reviewer whose account is not linked to their name is told…
findings.what: "Link this wallet to your name under Payment wallet on your profile, or turn it down without a reason." The fix is sent to a 'Payment wallet' setting, though the reviewer is not being paid. The error "This account isn't linked to your name, so the contributor would not see your reason. Nothing was sent. Link it first, or leave the reason and what was missing empty to turn it down without one." is long.
findings.why: A reviewer has no reason to look under 'Payment wallet' to fix a review problem, so many will just send a turn-down with no reason.
findings.suggestion: "Your reason won't show until this wallet is linked to your profile. Link it on your profile (Wallet), or send the turn-down without a reason." Better still, put a 'Link it now' button in the form.

findings.spec: launchpad-paid-work.spec.ts › a DAO pays a contributor money…
findings.what: The payment asked for is checked only against the budget-wide mandate.created.perProjectCap, with the error "A single work area can hold at most X of this budget.". It is never checked against the chosen work area's own money left. canAcceptClaim (work.ts:584) requires claim.amount <= record.budget - record.reserved, and WorkTab.tsx:815 shows the manager's 'Accept for review' button only when that holds.
findings.why: Concrete case: a work area approved with 200 USDC, per-area cap 1,000. A contributor asks for 400, the form accepts it, and the deposit is pulled. No manager is ever offered 'Accept for review', and the claim shows 'Waiting for <manager> to accept it for review' until it lapses, with no hint why. The error text also talks about what an area 'can hold' when the problem is the amount being asked for.
findings.suggestion: Check the ask against the chosen area's budget minus reserved, and say: "This work area has X USDC left, so you can ask for at most X." Add that case to the paid-work spec (or a mocked equivalent).
findings.verifier: Confirmed. FileClaimCard.tsx:284-287 checks the ask only against mandate.created.perProjectCap. canAcceptClaim (work.ts:584) requires claim.amount <= record.budget - record.reserved, and the manager's Accept button depends on it. So an ask above the area's remaining money files fine and is never offered for acceptance. The cap message ('can hold at most') also describes the area, not the ask. The area's budget and reserved can be read from the mandate's project records by the chosen area's id.

findings.spec: launchpad-work.spec.ts › a claim goes from filed to taken… (award step)
findings.what: On a finished claim, "Awarding Shares is a decision the DAO votes on. Open it on the Decisions tab" only switches tabs (LaunchDetailPage onOpenDecisions={() => setTab("decisions")}). The person then has to press New decision, choose 'Award Shares for submitted work' and find the claim. The 'challenge' path already opens the composer with the claim chosen (ChallengeIntent).
findings.why: This is the last and most important step, the one that actually gives the contributor something, and it is the least guided.
findings.suggestion: Pass an award intent like ChallengeIntent so the link opens the composer on 'Award Shares' with this claim selected. Label it "Propose the Shares award".
findings.verifier: Confirmed. WorkTab's work-award-open calls onOpenDecisions, which LaunchDetailPage wires to setTab("decisions") at lines 548, 584 and 620. Nothing preselects the award form or the claim. The challenge path already passes a ChallengeIntent to DecisionComposer (LaunchDetailPage.tsx:147, DecisionComposer.tsx:195). The award form in decision-forms.tsx:405-421 already has a 'which' key per awardable claim, so an AwardIntent can seed it.

findings.spec: launchpad-discussion.spec.ts › a discussion started under a decision…
findings.what: Starting a discussion pre-fills the title "Proposal: Set aside a work budget", while everything else in the app calls these 'decisions'. The board disclaimer appears both under the Decision ('Votes on a board show what people think; they are not the DAO's vote.', line 114) and in the post header ('Votes on this board show what people think. They are not the DAO's vote, which happens on the decision itself.', ProposalExtras.tsx:259), even though proposal posts show no vote arrows at all (PostRow.tsx:30). Also "That decision isn't in X's DAO. It may be on the newest page not shown here, or the post may be mistaken." (ProposalExtras.tsx:186).
findings.why: Explaining votes that are not on the screen is over-explaining and invites confusion. 'Newest page not shown here' is unclear.
findings.suggestion: Title: "Decision: Set aside a work budget". Drop the vote disclaimer on proposal posts, which have no arrows, and keep it once on the Decisions card. Missing case: "We couldn't find this decision in X's DAO. The link may be wrong."

findings.spec: launchpad-decisions.spec.ts › a decision opened elsewhere…
findings.what: "Passes when at least {quorum} Shares take part (for, against or neutral) and {pct}% of them back it, for {hold} in a row. It then waits {delay} before it can take effect. Voting closes {deadline}." After approval, the person must press "Start the wait" and later "Make it take effect", with the hint "Approved. It can take effect at … Support must hold until then."
findings.why: Three rules in one sentence is hard to read for people new to voting. 'Support must hold' after it is already 'Approved' reads as a contradiction.
findings.suggestion: Split into a short list: "Needs {quorum} Shares to vote" · "{pct}% must back it, for {hold}" · "Then a {delay} wait before it happens". Queued hint: "Approved. It can happen after {time}, as long as backers don't withdraw."
