findings.spec: launchpad-shouldfix-funds.spec.ts › once an exit lands…; a wallet on another network is refused…
findings.what: The leave flow's wording drifts and leaks internals. The buttons say "Leave and take my share" / "Leave anyway", but success is "Exit confirmed (tx 0x…), and the receipt is recorded.". "shares" is lowercase at lines 342, 362 and 384 but "Shares" elsewhere. The network error is "Your wallet is on chain 1, but this launch is on chain 31337. Switch networks in your wallet and try again." (wallet-effects.ts:98). ragequit-unknown explains that the 'milestone lock is older than the DAO and cannot answer' (line 371).
findings.why: These are raw transaction hashes, chain numbers and contract history in main copy, which the copy standard forbids, plus the raise-era word 'launch'.
findings.suggestion: Success: "You've left. Your Shares were given up and X was sent to your wallet." (put the tx under 'Technical details'). Network: "Your wallet is on Ethereum, but this project is on Base. Switch networks in your wallet and try again." Always write 'Shares'. Unknown: "Leaving isn't possible from this page for this project. Your Shares are unchanged."

findings.spec: launchpad-shouldfix-funds.spec.ts › leaving an empty treasury says it pays nothing…
findings.what: Contributor projects (the MVP) are Shares-only and usually hold no money, so on their Funds tab (ContributorFundsTab.tsx:183) the main action is 'Leave anyway', which destroys every earned Share for nothing. The spec checks the safeguard (a tick box), but the feature itself is a prominent button whose only result in the MVP is losing earned Shares.
findings.why: Newcomers with no business experience may read 'Leave' as 'leave the project' (stop being a member) and burn their contribution record. In the MVP nobody gains anything from this.
findings.suggestion: When the exit pays nothing, collapse the panel behind a disclosure such as 'Give up my Shares' and retitle it so it no longer promises a share. Add one line saying that stepping back only means you stop voting. Keep the full panel when the treasury holds money.
findings.verifier: Do not remove the feature. The panel is shared with raises, and contributor DAOs can hold money: ContributorFundsTab shows FundingCard, WeeklyRoundsCard and PayoutsCard, so an exit can pay. Safeguards already exist when the exit pays nothing: an outline 'Leave anyway' button, an amber warning that the Shares would be destroyed, and a required tick box (RagequitPanel.tsx:558, 804). What remains: the heading still reads 'Leave and take your share' (line 233) when there is nothing to take, and the section is laid out as a main action.

findings.spec: launchpad-shouldfix-funds.spec.ts (all four tests)
findings.what: The spec says it runs on 'a raise's Treasury tab' with an ETH payout, because a build without a contributor kit cannot show the Funds tab. The MVP path, the contributor project's Funds tab where the send goes through the acting (passkey) account, is only covered by the anvil/fork-gated passkey-contributor.spec.ts.
findings.why: The mocked suite guards a raise-era screen that the MVP hides, and leaves the page pilot users will actually see unguarded.
findings.suggestion: Build the mocked e2e bundle with VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_KITS pointing at a stub kit address. Have /test-rpc answer that kit's summon log for the seeded DAO. Then run the 'pays nothing' and 'Shares changed since read' tests on the contributor Funds tab. Keep one raise Treasury test while the panel is shared.
findings.verifier: The gap is real: the Funds tab, the MVP screen, has no mocked coverage. But the suggested fix does not work as written. launchpad-shouldfix-work does not seed a kit summon. ContributorFundsTab only shows the leave panel when useContributorProvenance returns 'kit' (ContributorFundsTab.tsx:90-122), and that needs VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_KITS set at build time. The mocked build does not set it, which is why the spec's header says it cannot show the tab.

findings.spec: launchpad-work.spec.ts › a claim goes from filed to taken, one person at a time…
findings.what: One 240-second test covers form validation, filing, accepting, reviewer gating, the missing-evidence block, two approvals, settling, the waiting period, payout, linking a relay task to the claim (task-delivery, a separate feature), and the bond post/unbond/withdraw cycle. launchpad-decisions.spec.ts:126 also depends on test order ("Runs first: the decision it finds must still be open"), so a CI retry of the second test after the decision has run fails for the wrong reason.
findings.why: When it fails, the failure says little about which feature broke, and any early failure masks everything after it. Order-dependent tests turn retries into noise.
findings.suggestion: For the chain-backed specs, take an anvil snapshot (evm_snapshot) in beforeEach and restore it (evm_revert) in afterEach, or set retries to 0 for them, so each test starts from a known chain state. Then split task-delivery linking and the bond cycle into their own tests that start from the snapshot.
findings.verifier: The problem is real but overstated. Workers are 1 and tests run in file order, so test 1 always runs before test 2. A CI retry (retries: 2) re-runs only the failed test. The real issue is that test 2 changes chain state and cannot be retried on its own, so merging the two tests does not fix retries either. The 240-second work test does mix separate features (task-delivery linking, bond return), and splitting those out is reasonable.

findings.spec: launchpad-shouldfix-ops.spec.ts › a busy chain node (…) is said in plain words…
findings.what: "The chain node is busy. Try again in a minute; if it keeps happening, tell the site's organiser." The spec also asserts that exact sentence and only loosely bounds the request count ("< 60", comment '45 today').
findings.why: 'Chain node' is the kind of technical term the copy standard avoids, and 'organiser' is vague. A bound of 60 against 45 would not catch a doubling of retries.
findings.suggestion: "The network is busy right now. Try again in a minute. If it keeps happening, tell whoever runs this Creaton site." In the spec, tighten the bound to something just above the expected count (e.g. ≤ 48), or assert the number of reads × 3.

areas.area: Raise-era screens: launch kit, milestones, challenges, record, IP and revenue pledge
areas.summary: This area covers a founder launching a raise into its own DAO (the one-button kit launch, choosing who judges milestones), the team's locked Shares and how milestones unlock (a named reviewer panel or holder objections), the public track record, and two statements on a project's page: who holds the IP, and a revenue pledge. Five of the seven specs need a real Anvil chain and skip in the mocked suite. Only the IP and pledge specs exercise anything there, so a green mocked run says nothing about launch, milestones, challenges or the record. The most important product problem is that "Who holds the IP" never shows on a contributor project, because the overview hides it, even though contributor projects are the MVP and IP is the question contributors most need answered. The copy is careful and honest, but it swaps "tokens" and "Shares" for the same thing, and leaks slugs and accounting or crypto terms ("net receipts", "SHA-256", "milestone-2"). The chain specs are thorough, but they are a few very large tests with some weak assertions, and two raise-only modes for judging milestones double what this area has to maintain and explain.

findings.spec: launchpad-ip-record.spec.ts (all tests)
findings.what: IpRecordCard (and RevenuePledgeCard) only render inside OverviewTab, which is passed to DaoOverview as `children`. DaoOverview drops children for contributor projects (`{contributor ? null : <details>...{children}}`), and contributor records are published with stage "graduated" (start/lib/contributor-project.ts:730), so they always take the DaoOverview path. A contributor project, which is the whole MVP, never shows "Who holds the IP". On a raise project after graduation, both cards sit inside the collapsed "About the raise this project came from".
findings.why: In a contributor project, "who owns what I build here" is the first question a contributor without legal experience has. D38 built this record for that reason, but in the pilot no one can see or edit it. The spec only seeds stage "live" raise records, so it can't catch this.
findings.suggestion: Render IpRecordCard directly in DaoOverview for contributor projects, near the Contributions or Ways to help summary, and outside the raise details for graduated raises. Make the copy fit a project with no raise: the "entity-on-raise" standing ("when the raise completes") must not appear for a contributor project, and "holding its token" should say "holding its Shares". Add a mocked spec that seeds a contributor record (stage graduated, contributor kit) and asserts ip-card is visible.
findings.verifier: Holds up. IpRecordCard and RevenuePledgeCard are rendered only in OverviewTab.tsx:290-293. LaunchDetailPage.tsx:516 sends `workDao && stage === "graduated"` to DaoOverview, which drops children for contributor projects (DaoOverview.tsx:652). contributor-project.ts:730 publishes stage "graduated", so a contributor project never shows the IP record. The spec's one graduated case has no DAO, so it goes through OverviewTab and can't catch this. ip-record.ts:213/247 do say "holding its token" and "when the raise completes". TOKENOMICS-REVIEWER-BRIEF.md lists the IP record under the contributor-stage track record, so this is intended for the MVP. The suggestion is sound. Show only IpRecordCard for contributors; the revenue pledge stays raise-era.

findings.spec: launchpad-dao-launch / challenge / milestone / record / journey .spec.ts (test.skip guards)
findings.what: Five of the seven specs in this area are skipped unless E2E_ANVIL_URL and other chain variables are set, which only the scripts/web-*-e2e.sh wrappers do. In the mocked smoke run they report as skipped, not failed, and no mocked test covers the copy or gating on these screens (DaoLaunchPanel, ChallengeMilestones, MilestoneRow, RecordTab).
findings.why: The team reads a green mocked suite as "raise screens OK" when nothing on them ran. A copy or gating regression, such as the reviewer-panel validation messages or the no-wallet disabled state, goes unnoticed until someone runs `mvp-gate --later`.
findings.suggestion: Move the five chain-gated files out of 'smoke' into their own 'chain' Playwright project that only the scripts/web-*-e2e.sh wrappers and `mvp-gate --later` run. Then a green mocked run says nothing about raise screens. Don't add mocked raise-screen specs until raises are back in scope.

findings.spec: launchpad-challenge.spec.ts: a milestone is turned down by the holders...
findings.what: The holder-objection Milestones screen says "tokens" for the team's Shares throughout: "The team votes with all of its tokens from the start", "{n} tokens still locked.", "Holders can still vote to spend the treasury or to issue more tokens" (line 177), "About {n} tokens will be held back (… of the team's locked tokens)" (line 269). The panel Milestones tab, DaoLaunchPanel and the record use "Shares" for the same thing. RecordTab.tsx:292 heads a Shares section "The team's tokens", and ip-record.ts:213/220/257 say "holding its token".

RecordTab heading: "The team's Shares". ip-record: "Until it does, holding its Shares gives no claim on the code, name or other work."

findings.spec: launchpad-challenge.spec.ts: a milestone is turned down by the holders...
findings.what: The rules read like a contract: "The objection stands only if more is against the milestone than for it and at least {x}% of what could vote is against it. With less interest than that, the milestone stands." Line 157 adds: "So the tokens still ahead stay locked, and are burned, while an earlier milestone can be objected to. Once the last one has unlocked, what stands behind it is the bond."
findings.why: "Stands" is used in two opposite senses in one sentence, and "what could vote" is internal phrasing. A holder deciding whether to object can't tell what will happen.
findings.suggestion: "The milestone is turned down if more holders vote against it than for it, and at least {x}% of all votes that could be cast are against it. Otherwise it unlocks." Replace the last paragraph with: "Milestones go one at a time. The next can only be submitted after the last one's late-objection period ends, so the Shares still locked can be burned if an earlier milestone is successfully challenged. After the last milestone, only the team's bond is at stake."

findings.spec: launchpad-milestone.spec.ts: the founder sees what is locked...
findings.what: A milestone claim is named "milestone-2" (or "milestone-2-2" on a retry), and that slug is what reviewers see in the claim list. The test finds the claim with `filter({ hasText: "milestone-2" })`.
findings.why: Reviewers and backers read a slug instead of what was promised, which is the milestone's own words ("mainnet live"). Everywhere else claims carry human names ("First draft of the guide").
findings.suggestion: Show the milestone's words as the claim's visible title, for example "Milestone 2: mainnet live", and keep the slug only as the id. If the 32-character name limit forces a short name, render the tranche label beside it in the Work list.

findings.spec: launchpad-milestone.spec.ts: the founder sees what is locked...
findings.what: Submitting a milestone takes three wallet prompts (file the claim, state which milestone, send it to reviewers) and a publish, and nothing warns the person beforehand. If they stop partway, the resume line reads like a work log: "Your last submission is not finished. Still to do: state which milestone it is for, then send it to the reviewers." The dead-end branch (line 327) says only "Your last submission cannot be continued."
findings.why: A person without crypto experience sees three confirmations for one button and is likely to cancel the second, which is exactly the case the test drives. The dead-end text gives no next step, which breaks the rule that errors say what to do next.
findings.suggestion: Small copy fix only. Dead end: show left.problem, then "Press Start over to submit it again; your evidence is below to copy." Before the first prompt, add one line: "Your wallet will ask you to confirm up to 3 times." Skip batching transactions unless the panel mode survives the pre-audit decision.
findings.verifier: The resume copy is accurate (MilestoneRow.tsx:326 joins STEP_WORDS). The dead-end branch (line 327) also throws away `left.problem` from remainingSteps (milestone-submission.ts:27). It is not a full dead end, though: the evidence and a 'Start over' button render right below it (lines 329-357). The finding missed that. Panel-mode submission is raise-era and may be removed (see finding 11), so heavy rework or batching isn't worth it now.

findings.spec: launchpad-revenue-pledge.spec.ts: the founder adds a pledge...
findings.what: Once a pledge is saved, the founder can't take it back. The editor has no Remove button, and clearing the percent is refused with "Say what percent of net receipts you pledge."
findings.why: A founder who adds a pledge by mistake, or whose plans change, can only lower it to 1%. The public page then keeps showing a promise they never meant to make, or no longer make.
findings.suggestion: Add a "Withdraw the pledge" action that publishes the record without revenuePledge. Optionally keep a public line such as "The team withdrew its pledge on {date}" so withdrawing is visible rather than silent. Add a test step for it.
findings.verifier: pledgeFromDraft refuses an empty percent (revenue-pledge.ts:106). The editor only saves `revenuePledge: made.pledge` and has no remove path (RevenuePledgeCard.tsx:46-60), so a pledge can't be withdrawn. D82 frames the pledge as an unenforced statement, so letting the team withdraw it, with a visible public line, is consistent. Low priority: the card is raise-era and today sits only inside the raise details.

findings.spec: launchpad-revenue-pledge.spec.ts (all tests)
findings.what: "Percent of net receipts" (label), "Blank: for as long as it earns" (placeholder on a free-text date field), and the sentence "The team pledges 20% of the project's net receipts to the treasury, every quarter, … It is not written into a signed document on record. The contracts do not enforce it." The heading is "What the project earns". The "Until" input is free text that needs "2030-12-31", and the date shows to visitors unformatted ("until 2030-12-31").
findings.why: "Net receipts" is accounting jargon for the people this product is for. A free-text ISO date invites the error path. "The contracts do not enforce it" is protocol-flavoured.
findings.suggestion: Label: "Share of what the project earns (after costs), in %". Use an `<input type="date">` labelled "Until (optional)" with the hint "Leave empty to keep paying for as long as the project earns." Sentence: "The team promises to pay 20% of what the project earns, after costs, into the treasury every quarter, until 31 Dec 2030. This is a promise, not a signed agreement, and nothing makes the team keep it." Heading: "Revenue promise".

findings.spec: launchpad-ip-record.spec.ts: choosing the file fingerprints it in the browser
findings.what: The field labels are "Fingerprint (SHA-256)", "Choose the file to fingerprint it" and "Link (https)". The refusal reads "The assignment needs a title, an https link and a fingerprint of 64 characters, or leave all three empty." (ip-record.ts:330). The card shows "Fingerprint abababab…ababab" while the pledge card shows "fingerprint abababababab…", so the same thing is shortened two ways (RevenuePledgeCard.tsx:189 vs IpRecordCard.tsx:53).
findings.why: SHA-256 and "64 characters" are internals. The file picker fills the fingerprint for people, so they should never need to know its length. The two shortened forms make the same document look different on two cards.
findings.suggestion: Labels: "Link to the document" and "Pick the signed file (it stays on your computer; we only record a fingerprint so changes can be spotted)". Hide the raw fingerprint input behind "Paste a fingerprint instead". Error: "Add a title, a link starting with https://, and pick the file for the {name}, or leave all three empty." Use one shortFingerprint helper for both cards.

findings.spec: launchpad-dao-launch.spec.ts: the founder launches a project into its own DAO with one button
findings.what: The summary reads "Kept by the DAO: 0 Shares (they never vote)" and "Backers can leave with: X% of what is left in the treasury before the first milestone, and Y% once every milestone has unlocked (your team's Shares count only as they unlock)". The panel continuity note (LaunchPanelFields.tsx:123) adds "the only thing the DAO can then do with them is give them up and burn them". Reviewers are entered as "One wallet address per line."
findings.why: The parentheticals pack mechanism into a summary the founder skims before one irreversible transaction. "Give them up and burn them" is awkward, and typing raw addresses contradicts the rest of the app, where reviewers are picked by name.
findings.suggestion: "Kept by the DAO: 0 Shares. The DAO's own Shares never vote." / "If backers leave: before the first milestone, X% of the treasury; after all milestones, Y%." Continuity note: "…no milestone can be approved, and the locked Shares can only be burned." Reviewers hint: "Pick people by name, or paste one wallet address per line."

findings.spec: launchpad-record.spec.ts: someone with no wallet can read what was set aside, paid and turned down
findings.what: The treasury figure is labelled `sale.kind === "custom" ? "USDC" : sale.symbol`. saleCurrencyFor (packages/creaton-core/src/launchpad/sale-currency.ts:89) classifies any token that isn't the chain's known USDC as "custom", with decimals fixed at 6. The same hard-coded "USDC" appears in DaoTreasuryTab.tsx:61, DaoOverview.tsx:234, DecisionsTab.tsx:127/217, decision-title.ts:61, SalePriceCard.tsx:22 and social/ui/PostContent.tsx:90.
findings.why: A project whose currency is any other ERC-20 has its treasury, budgets and payouts shown as "USDC", and for an 18-decimal token every amount is off by 10^12. That is a wrong money figure on the page meant to build trust.
findings.suggestion: Add one helper, currencyLabel(sale), in sale-currency.ts and make every caller pass localUsdcAddress(), so a local USDC is classified 'usdc'. Show a record whose currency is neither ETH nor the known USDC as 'unknown currency' with no amounts, or refuse it when reading records. Don't add symbol()/decimals() reads from the chain.
findings.verifier: The app only ever creates USDC or ETH records: currencyChoices offers only those, and use-contributor-start.ts:104 uses usdcAddress. 'custom' comes up mainly when a caller doesn't pass localUsdc (PostContent.tsx:86, SalePriceCard.tsx:21) on a local chain, where the fallback to 'USDC' is actually right. A wrong label for a real other ERC-20 needs a record published by hand, so it is latent, not a live 10^12 error. The eight copied ternaries are real duplication.

findings.spec: launchpad-challenge.spec.ts and launchpad-dao-launch.spec.ts
findings.what: A raise can unlock the team's milestones two ways: a named reviewer panel (LaunchPanelFields, MilestonesTab, MilestoneRow and the three-prompt submit) or holder objections (ChallengeMilestones, the bond, the deposit, the vote and the late clawback). Each has its own launch fields, Milestones screen, rules text, PowersCard wording and an end-to-end journey.
findings.why: Neither ships in the MVP, but both have to be kept working, kept consistent (the token/Shares split above is one symptom) and explained to backers. Two modes for one decision is exactly the choice a founder without business experience can't judge. The challenge path is already the default.
findings.suggestion: Don't delete now. Record a pre-audit decision to drop the panel launch path, removing DaoLaunchKit.launch's panel branch and MilestoneLock from the audit scope. Then remove the app pieces (LaunchPanelFields/LaunchReviewFields, the panel branch of MilestonesTab/MilestoneRow, milestone-submission.ts, launchpad-milestone.spec.ts) in the same change. Until then, leave the panel option unchanged behind the raise flags.
findings.verifier: D56 already decided that holder objections are the default and the panel is kept 'beside it until the journeys pass'. So the direction matches past intent. But the panel is in the audit scope: DaoLaunchKit.launch, MilestoneLock, and the panel named in the TreasuryMandate factory (AUDIT-SCOPE.md lines 29, 70, 72, 129, 158). Removing only the app side would leave contract paths the app can't serve. The screens are raise-era, outside the MVP and behind flags, so deleting code now gains little.

findings.spec: launchpad-milestone.spec.ts: the founder sees what is locked, unlocks the first milestone with one click, and a stranger sees nothing of it
findings.what: One 230-line test covers the locked-Shares card, the unlock, the stranger view, the public track record, the portfolio holdings, the storage-full refusal, an interrupted wallet, resume after reload and the backer's Milestones view. The challenge spec (launchpad-challenge.spec.ts:270) is one 520-line test in the same way.
findings.why: When it fails, the title names none of the nine behaviours, and every later step is untested on that run. A flaky portfolio read hides a resume regression. Each run also costs minutes of chain time.
findings.suggestion: Wrap each behaviour in a named test.step() (unlock, stranger view, track record, portfolio, storage-full refusal, interrupted wallet, resume, backer view). The report then names what failed, without restructuring the chain fixture. Low priority, since these are raise-era chain journeys.
findings.verifier: Accurate: milestone and challenge are each a single test (lines 225 and 270). But each step builds on chain state from the step before. Splitting them means test.describe.serial with a shared page or context, and later tests still skip once an earlier one fails, so splitting buys little. The record spec already covers the record page.

findings.spec: launchpad-record.spec.ts and launchpad-milestone.spec.ts
findings.what: `expect(record-figure-waiting).toContainText("0")` passes for "1,000", "200" or "10". Likewise launchpad-milestone.spec.ts:301 has `record-figure-work` toContainText("1"), which passes for any value containing a 1.
findings.why: These assertions can't fail when the money figure is wrong, and wrong money figures are what this page exists to show correctly.
findings.suggestion: Assert the exact value: `toHaveText(/^Waiting to be paid.*\b0(\.00)?\b/)`, or target a value-only test id (record-figure-waiting-value) with `toHaveText("0")`.
findings.verifier: launchpad-record.spec.ts:109 is toContainText("0") and launchpad-milestone.spec.ts:301 is toContainText("1"). Both pass for many wrong values. "200" at line 108 also matches "1,200". Use exact matches on a value-only element or an anchored regex.

findings.spec: launchpad-dao-launch.spec.ts: with no wallet in the browser the launch is off, and nothing is sent
findings.what: The comment says "the button is off and the page says why", but the test only checks that the button is disabled and the block height didn't change. It never asserts the explanation (dao-launch-wallet or the gate note).
findings.why: Rule 6 in CLAUDE.md: a disabled button with no reason strands the founder. The text that tells them to connect a wallet is the part they need, and it isn't checked.
findings.suggestion: Assert that dao-launch-gate is visible and contains the no-wallet gate message exactly as the gate logic produces it. Import it or match on /wallet/i. Don't hard-code new wording.
findings.verifier: Real gap: the test at launchpad-dao-launch.spec.ts:654 only asserts that the button is disabled. DaoLaunchPanel renders the reason through GateNote with testId 'dao-launch-gate' (line 286) and a WalletStrip with prefix 'dao-launch' (line 285). The suggested wording "Connect a wallet to launch" is made up and may not match the gate's message.

findings.spec: launchpad-ip-record.spec.ts: each standing says only what the documents on record support
findings.what: The loop reopens the same page five times and "cleans up" with `page.unroute("**/*").catch(() => undefined)`. mock-relay registers `**/info`, `**/communities` and a routeWebSocket, so unroute("**/*") removes nothing. Handlers and init scripts pile up and each iteration relies on the newest one winning. The loop also stops at the first failing standing.
findings.why: The cleanup line is dead code that suggests isolation the test doesn't have. Five sequential reloads also make it the slowest test in the file.
findings.suggestion: Cut the browser loop down to one representative standing on a fresh page and delete the unroute line. The node unit tests already cover the five wordings.
findings.verifier: Accurate: mock-relay registers '**/info', '**/communities' and a routeWebSocket (mock-relay.ts:234-248). unroute('**/*') matches none of them, so the cleanup line does nothing, and handlers pile up. But ip-record.test.mjs already covers every standing (line 98) and checks that no weaker standing says holders own anything (lines 160-190). The finding's 'better still' is already done.

findings.spec: launchpad-revenue-pledge.spec.ts / launchpad-ip-record.spec.ts
findings.what: Nothing covers a failed save. When the server refuses the record, both editors show `error.message` raw in pledge-problem or ip-problem. No test checks that the draft survives, or that the message says what to do next. The IP spec also seeds tokenPlan mode "mint", which D150 made read-only, yet lets the founder edit.
findings.why: A raw server string ("error: server is busy") breaks the rule that errors say what happened and what to do next, and it is the likeliest failure on a hosted pilot.
findings.suggestion: Map publish failures to plain sentences once, in the shared publish in use-launches.ts or a copy module: "Couldn't save. Your changes are still here; try again in a moment." Keep the specific refusals the relay can name. Add one mocked spec that uses mock-relay's `refuse` for the launch record and asserts the sentence and that the editor keeps its contents. Seed tokenPlan mode 'dao' in the IP spec.
findings.verifier: Real: both editors show error.message raw (IpRecordCard.tsx:171-175, RevenuePledgeCard.tsx:59-63). The publish path throws 'signing failed' or the relay's raw message, or 'Server rejected the event' (use-launches.ts:323-328). No spec covers a refused save, though mock-relay supports `refuse`. The mint-mode seed is a legacy shape, since D150 opens old minted launches read-only, so seeding 'dao' is right. But the error mapping belongs in one place, not in each card.

areas.summary: This area covers two optional money features. Weekly rounds sit on a contributor project's Funds tab: members who want out sell Shares to people who want in at one weekly price, and funding rounds sell new units, or Loot, for the project. Post bounties ("Money behind this post") put money behind a Home post, and that money pays whichever work most of it backs, with forecasts and an optional court attached. The pilot image turns both off, so neither is in the MVP. Both specs need a real chain and skip in the mocked suite, so they show up there as skips and the mocked run tests none of these screens. Most of the copy is careful and plain. The real defects are two wrong messages: a bid that is too low in a funding round says "a Share" and "what leaving pays", and one refund message says the court "did not uphold" work that it did uphold. There is also a gating gap: a contributor-only build still offers a sale of new units. The terms "back", "Loot", "new units", "floor" and "middle forecast" are used inconsistently or are jargon. The two journeys prove the happy path, but two of their key claims cannot fail as written, and the rounds journey has grown into a funding-and-exit test.

findings.spec: rounds-journey.spec.ts: a member who wants out is matched with two who want in (step 8, funding round bid)
findings.what: The funding-round bid form reuses bidPlan, which always says Shares and leaving. In a funding sale with a least price of 1.65, a bid at 1.5 shows "Bid at least 1.65 USDC a Share: what leaving pays." A bad amount shows a parse error that starts "How many Shares". In a funding round the floor is the sale's least price, the thing bought is a new unit (Loot), and leaving has nothing to do with it.
findings.why: A newcomer buying into a project is told the wrong reason for the wrong item at the moment they decide whether to put money in.
findings.suggestion: Pass `funding` into bidPlan. For a funding round use: "Bid at least 1.65 USDC a unit: the sale's lowest price." and the parse label "How many units". Holders' rounds keep "Bid at least X a Share: what leaving pays." Add a rounds-copy.test case for the funding wording.
findings.verifier: bidPlan (rounds-copy.ts:135-162) takes no funding flag. It always parses with the label "How many Shares" and always says "Bid at least X a Share: what leaving pays." RoundOrderForms.tsx:143 calls it the same way whether `funding` is set or not. Elsewhere the funding copy talks about "new units" and a "least price" (funding-copy.ts:52, rounds-copy.ts:94), so this form contradicts the rest of the funding card. Passing `funding` into bidPlan and adding a rounds-copy.test case is the right fix.

findings.spec: post-bounty-journey.spec.ts: work nobody backed is appealed... (court path)
findings.what: When refunds open after the court upheld the work but nobody pressed Pay within the grace period (appeal.state === "upheld" and postBountyStage returns "refunds"), the card says "The court did not uphold the work in time. Everyone can take their money back." The court did uphold it.
findings.why: The worker is told they lost the case when they actually won it and the money simply went unclaimed. That is false and will cause disputes.
findings.suggestion: Split the two states. For "refused": "The court ruled against the work. Everyone can take their money back." For "upheld": "The court ruled for {name}'s work, but nobody paid it by {date}. Everyone can take their money back." In the "upheld" stage line, also tell the worker to press Pay themselves: "…Anyone can pay it now, including you, until {date}; after that the money goes back."
findings.verifier: postRefundsOpen (openBounty.ts:393) opens refunds for appeal.state === "upheld" once ruledAt + PAY_GRACE has passed. postBountyStage then returns "refunds", and post-bounty-copy.ts:39-41 shows "The court did not uphold the work in time" for both refused and upheld. That is false for upheld. Split the line as suggested. The upheld date is bounty.appeal.ruledAt + PAY_GRACE, since the refunds stage carries no date.

findings.spec: rounds-journey.spec.ts steps 6-9 (funding terms, funding round)
findings.what: The "funding" decision kind and the "Funding the project" card (sell new Loot to outside buyers) are gated only on whether the build names the weekly-rounds contract. They are not gated on raisesOffered(). The "trading" kind just above is hidden in a contributor-only build with the comment "a contributor-only build offers no sale of any kind".
findings.why: Selling new units to buyers is a raise. Today it stays out of the pilot only because the image leaves out VITE_WEEKLY_ROUNDS. Anyone who turns weekly rounds on for a contributor-only run would also expose a fundraising sale, which the MVP scope rules out.
findings.suggestion: Add `if (id === "funding" && !raisesOffered()) return false;` and return null from FundingCard when !raisesOffered(). Holders' weekly rounds can stay available behind their own flag. Removing it costs nothing in the pilot, and raise builds are unchanged.
findings.verifier: DecisionComposer.tsx:220-229 hides "trading" when !raisesOffered(), with the comment "a contributor-only build offers no sale of any kind". "funding" checks only weeklyRounds(), contributor and fundingTerms. FundingCard renders whenever useFunding returns rounds, and ContributorFundsTab:190 shows it with no build check. Selling new units to outside buyers for USDC is a raise, and the MVP scope rules raises out. DEPRECATION says only that weekly rounds stay off in the pilot image, so today the exclusion depends on an image setting. Adding the raisesOffered() gate in both places is cheap and changes nothing for raise builds.

findings.spec: post-bounty-journey.spec.ts: money behind a post ... a dip stops it in time
findings.what: The test claims "A dip stops it": Cara un-backs and re-backs on day 3, then 9 days pass and the bounty is payable. Without the reset it would be payable at day 9 from the first backing, and with the reset at day 12. Both are before day 12, so the assertion passes whether or not the dip restarted the clock.
findings.why: This is the bounty's main safety rule, that the backing must hold for nine days in a row. As written, removing the reset logic would not fail any test.
findings.suggestion: After the re-back, pass 7 days and assert the status still reads "is paid on" and post-bounty-pay is absent. That is day 10, which would already be payable without the reset. Then pass 2 more days and assert "Anyone can pay it now."
findings.verifier: At spec lines 283-300, Cara un-backs and re-backs on day 3, then pass(9 days) brings the clock to day 12. A clock that never reset would have been payable from day 9, so "Anyone can pay it now." passes either way. The only check on the dip is that the status briefly reads "Takes money and work until", which says nothing about payableAt. The suggested check, 7 days after the re-back (still "is paid on", no post-bounty-pay) and then 2 more days, would fail if the reset were removed.

findings.spec: post-bounty-journey.spec.ts: work nobody backed is appealed, a juror drawn by stake upholds it
findings.what: `expect(latest(ben).getByTestId("post-bounty-refund")).toHaveCount(0)` runs on Ben's page as it was loaded before `pass(31 * 86_400)`. Only Dev's page was refreshed, so Ben's card still shows the pre-deadline state and could never show a refund button.
findings.why: It looks like it proves refunds stay closed during the appeal window, but it cannot fail.
findings.suggestion: Call `await refresh(ben)` before the assertion, and also assert Ben's status contains "can appeal to the court until".
findings.verifier: Ben's page is never reloaded after pass(31 days). usePostBounties caches chainTime inside the query result, with staleTime 10s and refetchOnWindowFocus: false (use-post-bounties.ts:30-45), so Ben's card still computes its stage from the time before the deadline and can never show post-bounty-refund. Add refresh(ben) before the assertion, and also assert that Ben sees "can appeal to the court until".

findings.spec: rounds-journey.spec.ts and post-bounty-journey.spec.ts (both)
findings.what: Both specs sit in the mocked "smoke" project, but each calls test.skip unless chain env vars such as E2E_ANVIL_URL are set. In the mocked suite they always show as skipped. No mocked spec renders WeeklyRoundsCard, the round order forms or PostBountyCard.

findings.suggestion: Add web-rounds-e2e and web-post-bounty-e2e to mvp-gate.sh's LATER list, so some gate runs them. Then cover the copy bugs at the unit level: a post-bounty-copy test for the refunds line with appeal.state "upheld", and a rounds-copy test for bidPlan in a funding round. Do not add a new Playwright project only for these two. If the chain-only specs should leave smoke, move all thirteen together in a separate change.
findings.verifier: The problem is real. Both specs test.skip without chain env, and in mocked runs they show as skipped. Neither web-rounds-e2e.sh nor web-post-bounty-e2e.sh is in mvp-gate.sh's PILOT or LATER list, so no gate runs them. The suggested fix does not fit, though. Thirteen specs in the smoke project use this same E2E_ANVIL_URL skip pattern, and both scripts call `--project=smoke`. Creating a separate project for just these two is inconsistent and means changing both scripts. Unit tests for the copy also already exist (rounds-copy.test.mjs, post-bounty-copy.test.mjs, openBounty.test.mjs).

findings.spec: rounds-journey.spec.ts: a member who wants out is matched...
findings.what: One 600-second test called weekly rounds also covers funding terms, a funding sale and round, a ragequit with a 2% exit fee and flagging a foreign token (D136), in steps 6-11. A failure in the token-flag step marks the rounds feature red, and nothing past the first failure runs.
