Move steps 6-11, plus the exit-fee leaving check, into a funding-rounds spec that reuses the same setup helper, run only by a raise/--later gate. This fits finding 2, which keeps funding out of contributor-only builds.
findings.verifier: The problem is real: steps 6-11 (funding terms, sale, funding round, exit with fee, foreign-token flag) sit inside one 600s rounds test. But the suggestion to end after step 5 and keep step 12 does not work as written. Step 12's leaving assertions ("after the 2% exit fee", and dao-leaving-now on Overview) depend on the funding terms published in step 6. Step 10 also uses the newcomer's Shares from step 5.

findings.spec: rounds-journey.spec.ts
findings.what: No test covers "Take my Shares back", "Take them back and leave", "Take my bid back", "Collect, and leave with the Shares", or a void round ("Nobody settled it in time…" followed by Collect). These are how a user changes their mind or recovers when nobody settles the round.
findings.why: These are the ways back (rule 6 in CLAUDE.md). If one breaks, a seller's Shares or a buyer's money stay held with no visible way to get them out.
findings.suggestion: Skip the unit test for the void status line, which already exists. Add one cancel-bid (or cancel-sell) click to step 4 before submitting the final orders. Also add a void-round path, for example in the second round: place an offer and a bid, let 3 + 2 days pass with no settle, then check that Collect returns both. If chain time is too costly, put this in a mocked spec of WeeklyRoundsCard's buttons per phase.
findings.verifier: Mostly real. The journey never clicks rounds-cancel-sell, rounds-cancel-bid or rounds-collect-leave, and never collects after a void round; in step 12's void-free "Nothing traded" round nobody had orders. One part is already covered: the void status line has a unit test (rounds-copy.test.mjs:35, "takes back"), and the history row for a void round is tested too. Collect after a settled round is exercised in steps 5 and 9.

findings.spec: post-bounty-journey.spec.ts: Dev submits work / Ben backs it
findings.what: "0% of the money that counts backs this". "The money that counts" is an internal idea (money not taken back) that no one is told about.
findings.why: A newcomer cannot tell what "counts" means or why their money might not count.
findings.suggestion: "{n}% of the money put in backs this". If the difference from the total matters, say it in the existing "How the money decides" note: "Money someone has taken back no longer counts."

findings.spec: post-bounty-journey.spec.ts (status lines asserted throughout)
findings.what: "Takes money and work until {date}. The work most of the money backs for nine days is paid.", "Most of the money backs X's work. If it stays that way, it is paid on {date}. No new money until then." and "Agreed. X is paid on {date} unless the backing drops." The two waiting states read almost the same, and "No new money until then" is said in only one of them, with no reason given.
findings.why: People see one status flip to another ("Most of the money backs", then "Agreed.") with no visible event, which is confusing. The open line reads like a rule, not a status.
findings.suggestion: Open: "Open for money and work until {date}. Work that keeps most of the money behind it for nine days gets paid." Agreeing: "Most of the money backs {name}'s work. If that holds, they're paid on {date}. No one can add money for the first three days." Holding: "Most of the money still backs {name}'s work. They're paid on {date} unless backing drops below half."

findings.spec: post-bounty-journey.spec.ts: Ben backs it / Cara backs it
findings.what: "Back this" and "Move my backing here" mean pointing your bounty money at a piece of work. Elsewhere "back" means funding a launch ("Back this launch", DiscoverCards.tsx:331) and supporting a decision ("Backing 200" on decision cards). That is three meanings for one word.
findings.why: Someone who learned "back" as "vote for a decision" or "put money in" will think pressing it here adds more money.
findings.suggestion: Use "Choose this work" / "Choose this work instead" / "Undo my choice" here, with the status line "Most of the money chose {name}'s work". Alternatively keep "back" for decisions only, and tie the raise-only "Back this launch" to "Fund".

findings.spec: rounds-journey.spec.ts steps 6-9
findings.what: The same thing has three names: "Set a funding limit of 100 new Loot" (decision title), "Buyers get Loot, with no vote" (chip), and "40 new units at 1.65 USDC each", "Bid for new units" and "Funding limit (new units)" (round and form). "Loot" is DAO-framework jargon.
findings.why: A buyer cannot tell that the "new units" they bid for are the "Loot" in the terms. "Loot" also sounds like a game.
findings.suggestion: Choose one plain name, for example "non-voting shares": "Buyers get non-voting shares", "Set a funding limit of 100 non-voting shares", "40 non-voting shares at 1.65 USDC each". Keep "Loot" only inside a Technical details disclosure.

findings.spec: rounds-journey.spec.ts step 3
findings.what: "Floor at opening: 1 USDC a Share" is a trading term, and the card states it next to the "Leaving now pays about 1 USDC a Share." line.
findings.why: Two numbers that usually match, one of them in jargon, make readers wonder which price applies.
findings.suggestion: "Lowest price this round: 1 USDC a Share (what leaving paid when it opened)"

findings.spec: rounds-journey.spec.ts step 5 (each buyer bid 30, got 25)
findings.what: "How a round works" says "the highest at which bids still take everything offered". It never says that when more is wanted than offered, buyers at the round's price split what is offered. In the journey each buyer bid for 30 and got 25 with no explanation.
findings.why: Getting less than you bid for, with no warning, looks like a bug or a loss.
findings.suggestion: Add: "If people want more than is offered at that price, it is shared out in proportion to each bid, and the rest of your money comes back." To the bid plan line add: "You may get fewer than you asked for."

findings.spec: rounds-journey.spec.ts steps 2-3
findings.what: After the vote passes, someone must wait 30 days and press "Switch on weekly rounds". After that, someone must press "Open this week's round" every week and "Settle the round" within two days, or everything is returned. None of these steps is assigned to anyone or surfaced outside the Funds tab.
findings.why: These steps have no owner, and people without business experience won't know to come back. Rounds would quietly never happen, or a matched trade would be lost because nobody settled it.
findings.suggestion: Defer until weekly rounds are switched on for a real group. When that happens, first add "A round is ready to settle (by {date})" to WaitingOnYou for holders of that DAO, which is the costly miss because a matched trade is lost. A combined "Start the first round" button can send the two transactions in sequence, the same way approve-then-bid works today.
findings.verifier: The problem is real. Switch-on (shares.activateExitExchange) and open (rounds.openRound) are separate buttons, and WaitingOnYou.tsx and HomeYours have no rounds items, so nobody is prompted to open or settle a round. But weekly rounds are off in the pilot image (DEPRECATION #38), so this is not MVP work. Also, "one button" would still mean two transactions on two contracts.

findings.spec: post-bounty-journey.spec.ts (both tests)
findings.what: "Money behind this post" adds a second, money-weighted bounty system on Home posts, separate from the work-area bounties that reviewers approve (bounty-copy.ts). It brings forecasts, profile forecast scores and a staked jury court (CREATE token) with it. The pilot image already leaves it out (PILOT-RUNBOOK lists bounties, the court and forecasts as optional), but the specs and the card ship in the smoke project.
findings.why: Two ways to get paid for work, decided by different people (reviewers vs. whoever put in the most money), plus a court and a scoring system, make the product harder to understand for the MVP's audience. A single funder holding more than half the money decides alone, which also invites misuse on an open social feed.
findings.suggestion: Keep the address gate, consistent with how the court is gated. Tie it to raisesOffered() only if the owner decides post bounties belong to raise builds. Add web-post-bounty-e2e to mvp-gate's LATER list, and put the question ("do people need paid asks outside a project's work areas, decided by money rather than reviewers?") on the after-pilot review list rather than removing code now.
findings.verifier: The finding overstates what removal would take out. ForecastPanel is also used by WorkAreaBounties, and the court is used by work-area flows and RemixBondPanel, so forecasts and the court stay either way. Gating on raisesOffered() would also be wrong, because money on a post is not a raise. The court is deliberately gated by its contract address (build-gates.ts courtOffered), and DEPRECATION handled it that way. The pilot image already leaves out the bounty contract, so the card is already off there. What remains is real: the specs are not in any gate, and whether to keep a second money-weighted payment path is an open product question.

findings.spec: post-bounty-journey.spec.ts (Cara's profile forecast score)
findings.what: "Forecasts: 96 out of 100 over 1 settled bounty. Always saying 50% would score 75." and "Middle forecast: 60% · 2 people". The 75 baseline is a scoring-rule detail, and "middle forecast" is a median.
findings.why: Readers will not know why 50% scores 75 or what a "middle" forecast is. The line reads like a stats lecture on someone's profile.
findings.suggestion: Profile: "Forecast accuracy: 96 out of 100 (1 bounty). Guessing 50% every time scores 75." Panel: "Typical guess: 60% (2 people)". The outcome line becomes "It got done. The typical guess was 60%."

findings.spec: rounds-journey.spec.ts step 4 (offer and bid submit)
findings.what: The rounds forms show "Allowing…" as their busy label and give no warning that the wallet will ask twice. The post-bounty form explains it: "Your wallet asks twice: once to allow the amount, once to put it in."
findings.why: A first-time user sees an unexpected second wallet prompt, labelled "Allowing…", and may reject it, which leaves the offer or bid unsent.
findings.suggestion: Add under each form: "Your wallet asks twice the first time: once to let the round hold your Shares (or money), once to place the offer." Change the busy label to "Approving in your wallet (1 of 2)…".

areas.area: AI helpers, org chart, task planning and the DAO OS screens
areas.summary: This area covers several things: the project progress feed on Home and on project pages, the community Tasks board (Next up, backing, the plan, claiming a finished task, the "Delivery & payment" links), the AI helpers view and the tab helper, the Org chart and its setup wizard, and the Workflow runs dialog. The pilot build already hides AI helpers, Org and the idea-page ops surfaces. It still shows the community Tasks board, though, along with its "Reward (points)", "Claim as contribution" and "Onchain claim" pieces, and these compete with the project Work tab and Shares. Reviewers have no screen in the web app to accept a points claim, so that path dead-ends in the pilot. The copy on these screens is the most jargon-heavy in the app: "Onchain claim", hex claim and budget ids, chain-id numbers, "allowance not verified here", raw JSON scopes, and the same word ("seat", "Work") used with different meanings. Most specs are real and falsifiable, and the progress-feed and org-setup specs are good. A few prove little: a no-op assertion, a fixed 2-second sleep, a pause test that never checks when it paused, and an org-chart test whose title and assertions date from before the setup wizard existed.

findings.spec: task-planning.spec.ts: "a task's plan survives a row that omits it, and the finisher claims it once"
findings.what: The community Tasks board (shown in the pilot via work-toggle, CommunityShell.tsx:484-498) lets a finisher "Claim as contribution" for "Reward (points)", and the toast says "A reviewer accepts it before the points count." Nothing in web/src writes reviewStatus "accepted". Only the CLI does (crates/buzz-cli/src/commands/agent_wiki.rs:898). So in the pilot a claim stays pending forever. The pilot also has a second, real contribution path (project Work tab, Shares by vote).
findings.why: Pilot users are new to this. They would meet two ways of claiming work, two rewards (points and Shares) and a review that can never happen in the app. That breaks trust in the one loop the MVP is about.
findings.suggestion: In the contributor-only build, hide the Reward field, the points note and "Claim as contribution" on the Tasks board, and keep Tasks as plain to-dos (owner, due date, Next up). Alternatively, link a task to the project's Work area so Shares stay the only reward. Raise builds keep the panel. Cost: the Your-work Points card already only shows to people with points (DEPRECATION #7), so nothing else depends on it in the pilot.
findings.verifier: In the web app the only writers of 37013 records (task-planning.ts:274, task-source.ts:170) set reviewStatus "pending". Nothing in web/src or packages/creaton-core sets "accepted"; only buzz-cli agent_wiki.rs:898 does. The Tasks toggle (CommunityShell.tsx:484-498) is not gated, and WorkBoard.tsx:633 renders TaskPlanningPanel in every build. So a pilot claim stays pending forever, next to the real Shares path. DEPRECATION-2026-10-31 only hid the Points card for people without points (#7) and asked for one meaning of "points" (#15). It did not decide to keep task claims in the pilot.

findings.spec: task-planning.spec.ts: "a task's plan survives a row that omits it..."
findings.what: "Points are credited when the finished task is accepted as a contribution, and add to the contributor's share of the project. Accepting a contribution does not send USDC. Arrange payment separately or use the DAO's Work tab for a funded claim." This contradicts Portfolio (PortfolioPage.tsx:220: "They are not Shares in any project."), names USDC, and uses "funded claim".
findings.why: It tells people that points give them a share of the project, which the Portfolio page denies. That is a factual inconsistency about what people earn.
findings.suggestion: If the field stays (raise builds): "Points show on your profile once a reviewer accepts the task. They are not Shares and are not money. To earn Shares, take the work on the project's Work tab."
findings.verifier: The quoted text is exact (TaskPlanningPanel.tsx:142-147). It says points "add to the contributor's share of the project", while PortfolioPage.tsx:220 says "They are not Shares in any project." It also names USDC and "funded claim". The suggested rewrite fixes the contradiction.

findings.spec: dao-os.spec.ts: "task links persist through status changes..." and "a refused task-link save preserves the draft..."
findings.what: The pilot's Tasks board shows: heading "Delivery & payment"; "Link the project, its output and an existing funding claim. Finishing or approving this task never sends money. A reference does not establish that a claim was filed for this task or approved by the project."; label "Onchain claim"; options like "Approved · claim 0x12ab34cd… · budget 0x9f8e7d6c…"; "Select this project's network (11155111) to read its claims."; "Read from the chain: …".
findings.why: Hex ids, a chain-id number and "onchain claim" are the protocol internals the copy standard bans. "Select this project's network" gives a pilot user no action they can take.
findings.suggestion: Heading "Where this work went". Intro: "Link the project and the finished work. Saving this never pays anyone." Rename "Output or evidence link" to "Link to the finished work". Rename "Onchain claim" to "Matching piece of work on the project" and label options by the claim's title or work area and contributor name, not ids. Drop the network line in the pilot (one chain), or say "Can't read this project's work right now. Try again." Rename the save button to "Save links" and the success message to "Saved. Nobody was paid."
findings.verifier: The strings are verbatim: "Delivery & payment", the intro, "Onchain claim", options built from `claim ${id.slice(0,10)}… · budget ${mandate.slice(0,10)}…`, `Select this project's network (${chainId})`, and "Read from the chain:". The chain check compares the app's own RPC endpoint (getRpcEndpoint) with the project's chainId, so a pilot user has nothing to select. The suggested "can't read this project's work here" wording is right.

findings.spec: browser-agent.spec.ts: "the tab agent works a task it was assigned and reports the outcome"
findings.what: When the AI call or the "done" status publish fails after the agent has already set the task to in_progress, the catch only posts "⚠️ Task failed: …". The task row stays "in_progress" under the agent's name, and rememberTaskRow (line 412) stops the same row being retried. This catch also drops task.parentEventId, so the failure lands top-level instead of in the task's thread, unlike line 438.
findings.why: Scenario: the AI service times out. The board shows the helper "In progress" forever, nobody is told it needs reassigning, and Next up hides it because it counts as started. This breaks review rule 1: a caught failure must leave a retry record or propagate.
findings.suggestion: In that catch, publish the task back to "open" (or a "blocked" status with the reason), unassign or keep the assignee as the team decides, post the failure in the same thread (pass task.parentEventId), and add a spec where the gateway returns 500 that asserts the final 44011 status is not in_progress.
findings.verifier: browser-agent.ts:476-482 is exactly as described. After in_progress is published, a failure in askLlm or in the done publish only posts a message. It does not pass task.parentEventId, unlike line 438. The task row is never moved off in_progress, and rememberTaskRow blocks a retry of that event. publishTaskUpdate accepts any status string, so publishing "open" or a blocked status is a small change. The bug sits behind the AI-helpers gate, so it does not reach the pilot, but it is real in other builds.

findings.spec: browser-agent.spec.ts: "a refused status row is reported instead of claimed as done"
findings.what: The helper posts the raw relay error into the room: "⚠️ Task failed: restricted: not a channel member". The spec locks in this raw text (/Task failed: restricted/). Elsewhere the app runs errors through failureWords(), which strips the "restricted:" code.
findings.why: Everyone in the room sees a protocol prefix and gets no next step.
findings.suggestion: Use failureWords(error).text and say what to do, e.g. "I couldn't start \"{title}\": {plain reason}. Add me to this room, or give the task to someone else." Change the spec to assert the plain sentence and that "restricted:" is absent.

findings.spec: org-chart.spec.ts: "org chart renders role tree with occupant chips when nodes exist"
findings.what: The header "{n} teams · {m} seats" counts every 37010 node as a "team" (roles like "CTO" or "Researcher" included) and counts unique occupants as "seats". A role with nobody in it adds no seat, and one person in two roles counts once. The spec asserts "2 teams · 3 seats" for one role plus one team holding three people. HelpersPanel.tsx:170-171 uses "seat" for the role slot itself ("An open seat is waiting for a helper").
findings.why: The numbers are wrong as words: after setup a person sees "2 teams" for one team and one role. "Seat" means a person on one screen and a slot on the next.
findings.suggestion: Header: "{teams} teams · {roles} roles · {people} people", or drop the counts. Pick one meaning: "seat" = a slot, which may be open. On node cards use "{n} people". Update the spec to assert the corrected counts.
findings.verifier: OrgView.tsx:266-269 counts every node (team, role or agent_seat, per SEAT_KIND_LABEL) as a "team", and :274 uses seatCount = the number of unique occupants. The node card (:181) labels its occupant count "seats", while HelpersPanel uses "seat" for a slot. Both the wording and the counts are inconsistent. The view is not in the pilot (helpers gate).

findings.spec: polling-bounds.spec.ts: "the workflow runs list pauses its own refreshing..."
findings.what: Every build, the pilot included, puts "Workflow runs" in the Notifications menu. The web app has no way to create a workflow (features/workflows only has WorkflowRunsPanel); workflows are YAML set up from the CLI.
findings.why: For a pilot user it is an always-empty, unexplained entry above their real notifications in the menu they open most.
findings.suggestion: Don't gate by build. Show "Workflow runs" only when the community has at least one workflow definition (30620) or a recent run, the same way ApprovalsPanel hides itself when empty. Keep the polling-bounds spec by seeding one workflow definition in its mock relay.
findings.verifier: The claim that the web app cannot create workflows is false. Applying a template in StartProject (packages/creaton-core/src/templates/apply.ts:475-487) publishes kind 30620 workflow definitions; the catalog has nightly-standup and scene-review, and template apply is not gated by contributor-only. So a pilot community set up from a template can have runs. The entry is still always shown even when there are none (NotificationBell.tsx:108-121), unlike ApprovalsPanel, which returns null when empty.

findings.spec: dao-os.spec.ts: "task links persist..." / "outside tasks, forged edits..." (People & agents tab)
findings.what: Strings: "A seat or task assignment does not grant wallet authority. Budget controls distinguish recorded limits from enforced limits. Usage in AI helpers covers this browser's helper, not all project agents."; "Founder-recorded budget & approval limits"; "Onchain binding recorded; allowance not verified here"; "No applicable limit found in the latest budget records. This does not establish unlimited authority."; "These announcements do not prove permission."; and a <pre> holding JSON.stringify of the role scope.
findings.why: This reads like an audit log, not a team page: legal hedging, internal terms (binding, allowance, authority) and raw JSON. Even in raise builds, a founder without business experience cannot act on any of it.
findings.suggestion: One short line: "Helpers can only do what their limits allow. Limits marked 'checked' are enforced; others are a note." Rename the budget heading to "Limits". Replace the onchain line with "Spending cap set on the treasury". Replace the empty-limit line with "No limits set for this helper." Replace the JSON <pre> with plain lines ("Can see work below this role · Can't assign work").

findings.spec: dao-os.spec.ts: "Home connects project reports..." / "outside tasks, forged edits..."
findings.what: The same board has four names: the sidebar says "Tasks" (CommunityShell.tsx:497); here it is "the workspace's Work tab", "Open workspace Work board" and "Open the workspace for the rest", while the project page also has its own "Work" tab, which is something else. Buttons "Milestone evidence & unlocks" and "Money & spending authority" use internal terms.
findings.why: DEPRECATION #15 promised one meaning for "Work". A newcomer clicking "Work board" expects the project's Work tab and lands on a community task list.
findings.suggestion: Call the community board "Tasks" everywhere: "No tasks yet. Tasks the team adds in the community's Tasks list show up here." / "Open Tasks" / "Showing the first five. Open Tasks for the rest." Rename the buttons "Milestones" and "Money".

findings.spec: dao-os.spec.ts: "Home connects project reports, reading history, discussion and the four main destinations"
findings.what: (a) Links read "Artifact 1 · example.com". (b) Each team card says "Team update" in its header and again as a "From the team" chip. (c) Empty state: "No reports in this view yet. Follow a project or share what shipped, an artifact and what comes next." (d) "The shared report was not found in the latest loaded updates. This does not mean it was deleted." (e) The copy failure says "Open the project's Updates tab to share it.", which gives no way to get the link.
findings.why: "Artifact" is builder jargon. The duplicate label is noise on every card. The copy-failure message sends people somewhere that does not solve the problem.
findings.suggestion: (a) "Link 1 · example.com", or just the hostname. (b) Keep the chip only for "Not approved yet" and drop "From the team". (c) "No updates yet. Follow a project to see its news here." (d) "We couldn't find that update in the latest ones. Press Show more to look further back." (and rename "More progress" to "Show more"). (e) "Couldn't copy. Here is the link:" followed by a selectable read-only field holding the URL. Update the spec's "Artifact 1" locator.

findings.spec: task-planning.spec.ts: "a task already credited (by the worker or the CLI) cannot be claimed twice"
findings.what: Whether a task is claimed lives only in local useState. On reload, or for a task the worker or CLI already credited, the panel still offers "Claim as contribution". Only after clicking does the person get the error toast "This task has already been claimed." The spec asserts this click-then-fail behaviour.
findings.why: Offering an action that is known to fail is a dead end, and it hides the real state (claimed, waiting for review).
findings.suggestion: Read the 37013 record for item.doneRowId when the panel opens (use-task-planning already queries it on claim). If one exists, show "Claimed by {name}, waiting for review" instead of the button. Change the spec to assert the button is absent and the status line is shown.
findings.verifier: `claimed` is only local useState (TaskPlanningPanel.tsx:83), and `claimable` (:90-93) ignores any existing 37013 record. After a reload, or for a task the CLI credited, the button is offered and only fails on click. This applies wherever the claim stays (raise builds, if finding 0 lands).

findings.spec: org-setup.spec.ts: "when the server refuses, the person is told what to do and can try again"
findings.what: Any viewer (even one signed out, as in org-chart.spec's second test) is offered the four-step "Name your organization" wizard. Only on the last step does it say "Only this community's owner or an admin can start its organization. If that is not you, the server will say so", and then the server refuses.
findings.why: A member fills in four steps and then is refused. That makes them feel they broke something.
findings.suggestion: Reuse useCommunitySetupAccess() in OrgView. Hide the wizard and show "This community hasn't set up its organization yet. Its owner or an admin can do that." only when access is "denied" or "anonymous". Keep the wizard for "allowed", and also for "unknown" or "error", with the owner sentence moved to the first step. Update org-chart.spec's signed-out test to expect the not-set-up line.
findings.verifier: The problem is real. OrgView shows OrgSetup whenever the chart is empty (showSetup, OrgView.tsx:322-334), and the owner/admin sentence appears only on the review step (OrgSetup.tsx:322-327). But an access check already exists: useCommunitySetupAccess() in features/templates/use-template-apply.ts reads the NIP-43 membership list and returns allowed/denied/unknown/error/anonymous. CommunityShell already uses it for the setup entry. Hiding the wizard on "unknown" or "error" would also hide the only way to set up the org (review rule 6).

findings.spec: browser-agent.spec.ts: "the tab agent announces itself to the relay when started"
findings.what: `const announced = await expect.poll(...).toBe(true); expect(announced).toBeUndefined();`. The second assertion only checks that expect.poll resolves to undefined, which it always does.
findings.why: It is dead weight that reads like a check. The test proves only that some 44010 with d=pubkey exists, not its content (name, tools).
findings.suggestion: Drop the second assertion and assert the announced content instead (name, runtype "browser", heartbeat present).
findings.verifier: browser-agent.spec.ts:103-115 assigns the result of `await expect.poll(...).toBe(true)` and then asserts it is undefined, which always holds. The test checks only that a 44010 with d=pubkey exists, not what it says.

findings.spec: helpers.spec.ts: "a project's helper runs in the tab under its own name..."
findings.what: The negative check (the "@buzz-tab" mention is not answered) is a fixed `waitForTimeout(2_000)` followed by `expect(prompts).toHaveLength(1)`.
findings.why: It adds 2 seconds to every run and can pass falsely if the handler answers after 2 seconds. That is the flaky-negative pattern.
findings.suggestion: Deliver the "@buzz-tab" mention first and a "@The Writer" mention after it. Wait for the second answer, then assert prompts has length 1 and the first was never answered (ordered delivery makes it falsifiable without sleeping).
findings.verifier: helpers.spec.ts:198-206 uses waitForTimeout(2_000) followed by toHaveLength(1): a fixed sleep for a negative check. The ordered-delivery idea is sound if the agent handles mentions one at a time. If it handles them concurrently, also check that no prompt text contains "are you there" after the second answer arrives.

findings.spec: polling-bounds.spec.ts: "the workflow runs list pauses its own refreshing after fifteen minutes, and Refresh resumes it"
findings.what: The loop accepts a pause at any minute from 1 to 30 and swallows clock errors with `.catch(() => {})`. It never checks that requests stop after the pause. "Refresh resumes it" is proved only by the text "Recent runs", not by polling starting again.
findings.why: A regression that pauses at minute 1, or keeps polling while showing the paused label, would still pass.
findings.suggestion: Count run-list requests (page.route on the query). Assert no pause at 14 minutes and a pause by 16. Assert no new requests over the next 5 minutes. After Refresh, assert a request happens within one interval.
findings.verifier: polling-bounds.spec.ts:54-62 loops for up to 30 minutes, swallows clock errors, accepts a pause at any minute, and never checks that requests stop or start again. After Refresh it only asserts the text "Recent runs", which the panel shows anyway. So a pause at minute 1, or polling that continues behind the label, would still pass.

findings.spec: org-chart.spec.ts: "org view falls back to the roster when no nodes exist"
findings.what: The title and comments predate the setup wizard: with no nodes the page now shows OrgSetup above the roster, which the test ignores. `expect(page.getByText("Loading org chart…")).toBeHidden()` cannot fail on the fallback path. The file also hand-rolls its own WebSocket mock pinned to `127.0.0.1:4173` instead of createMockRelay, so it ignores E2E_PORT.
findings.why: It locks in a stale empty state, asserts nothing about what a new community sees first, and breaks when the suite runs on another port.
findings.suggestion: Switch to createMockRelay. Rename the test to "an empty org offers setup, and lists any helpers". Assert org-setup is visible (or hidden for a non-owner, if that change lands) and drop the trivially-hidden loading assertion.
findings.verifier: org-chart.spec.ts:108 routes WebSockets only for /127\.0\.0\.1:4173/, so it ignores E2E_PORT, which playwright.config.ts reads. The empty-chart test (:156-171) ignores the OrgSetup now shown above the roster, and its "Loading org chart…" toBeHidden check is trivially true on that path. Note that the org view is not in the pilot build.

findings.spec: dao-os.spec.ts: "the project-first experience fits a phone and preserves readable actions"
findings.what: It writes three full-page screenshots to /private/tmp on every run that nothing compares. It also drives an idea page whose "Building together" overview only shows in raise builds (ideaShowsTeamSurfaces).
findings.why: The screenshots slow the suite and leave files behind, and the test does not cover the build the pilot ships.
findings.suggestion: Keep the overflow assertions and drop the screenshots (or gate them behind an env flag). Add the same no-horizontal-scroll check for a contributor project page, which is what the pilot opens.
findings.verifier: dao-os.spec.ts writes three screenshots to /private/tmp (lines ~501, 508, 538 in the 475-545 range) that nothing compares, and macOS-only paths fail on Linux CI. The idea-page overview depends on ideaShowsTeamSurfaces(raises), which is false in the pilot. Keeping the scrollWidth checks and adding one on a contributor project page is the right change.

findings.spec: task-planning.spec.ts / dao-os.spec.ts (Tasks board in the pilot build)
findings.what: No spec drives the Tasks board as the pilot build shows it (VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1). Nothing checks which parts of the task detail (TaskEditors, TaskDeliveryPanel, TaskPlanningPanel) a pilot user sees, or that a contributor project with a DAO does not show hex claim ids or a network number.
findings.why: The specs in this area run in a raise-capable build. Their most user-visible pilot surface (Tasks) could leak raise-era and onchain copy without any test failing.
findings.suggestion: Add the check to the screen audit's mvp run (tests/e2e-real/screen-audit.spec.ts with WEB_FEATURES=mvp, which builds with VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1). Open a task linked to a contributor project with a DAO, assert no "0x" text and no "network (" text, and assert whatever reward and claim decision lands from findings 0-2. Alternatively, build a pilot dist and point a dedicated mocked spec at it via E2E_DIST/E2E_PORT.
findings.verifier: The gap is real: WorkBoard renders TaskEditors, TaskDeliveryPanel and TaskPlanningPanel in every build, and no mocked spec covers the pilot build. But the mocked suite (web/tests/e2e) runs against a single build. VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY is compile-time, and E2E_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY is read only by tests/e2e-real/screen-audit.spec.ts, which scripts/web-screen-audit.sh exports for its mvp build. A mocked spec cannot simply flip a runtime switch.

areas.summary: This area covers what a pilot user meets in a community: rooms and live chat between two people, edits, reactions, replies, deletions, mentions and the bell, the wiki, the Tasks board, reconnecting after a dropped connection, and whether the main screens fit a phone and pass axe in light and dark. The multi-user and failure-state tests are the strongest part of the suite. They check real regressions (blind wiki writes, an empty channel shown after a failed read, reconnect backoff, the AUTH race, the p-gate), and most would fail if their guard were removed. Coverage is aimed at the wrong build, though. Every responsive and axe spec runs on the raise build, and about a third of the responsive and axe tests cover screens the contributor-only pilot hides (fleet, org, repos, launchpad create and detail, "No chain data"). The "pilot" axe spec even checks a token-unlock milestone card from the raise era. Meanwhile the pilot's own pages (a contributor project's overview and work areas, the contributor Start wizard, a board) get no phone or axe check. On the product side, the chat screens still talk like a protocol ("history query", "the client keeps retrying", "image/gif", "channels" next to "rooms"), and I found three real accessibility bugs: the mention list does not work from the keyboard, the sign-out confirm is not a dialog, and the bell hides its unread count from screen readers.

findings.spec: multi-user.spec.ts: the composer suggests people seen in the channel, not just agents
findings.what: The mention suggestions can only be picked with a pointer. The textarea's onKeyDown sends on Enter even while the suggestion list is open, nothing handles ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Tab/Escape, and the list (Composer.tsx:226-240) has no listbox/option roles and no aria-expanded or aria-activedescendant on the input.
findings.why: A keyboard or screen-reader user types "@Ali", presses Enter to pick Alice, and the message goes out as plain "@Ali" with no p tag, so Alice is never notified. CLAUDE.md rule 8 (every input modality is a first-class seam) names exactly this kind of defect. The spec only clicks the option, so this path is never exercised.
findings.suggestion: While mentionQuery !== null and there are candidates: ArrowUp/Down move a highlighted index, and Enter/Tab pick it with pickMention instead of sending. Escape closes the list. Give the list role=listbox with option children and aria-selected, and give the textarea aria-expanded/aria-controls/aria-activedescendant. Add a test that types "@Ali", presses ArrowDown and Enter, then sends, and asserts that the published event carries Alice's p tag and that Alice's bell rings in a second context.
findings.verifier: Composer.tsx:258-263: onKeyDown sends on Enter (no Shift) with no check of mentionQuery, so typing "@Ali" and pressing Enter sends plain text. pickMention is the only thing that pushes into mentionPubkeys, and it is reachable only from the option buttons' onClick. There are no ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Tab/Escape handlers and no listbox/option/aria-expanded/aria-activedescendant. One nuance: the option buttons come before the textarea in DOM order, so Shift+Tab does reach them. That path is undiscoverable, and the list is not announced, so the defect stands. The suggested fix and test are right.

findings.spec: responsive-surfaces.spec.ts: profile menu fits once an identity exists
findings.what: The "Sign out of this browser?" confirmation is a bare Overlay div. It has no role="dialog", no aria-modal, no aria-labelledby, no focus move into it, no focus trap and no Escape handler. Other hand-rolled dialogs, such as PageDialog and the invite page's Mac choice, already do this properly.
findings.why: This confirm is the most destructive one in the app: signing out without the recovery key loses the account. A screen-reader user is not told a dialog opened, focus stays on the menu behind it, and Tab walks into the page underneath. axe misses it because nothing in it is technically invalid.
findings.suggestion: Use the shared AlertDialog (Radix), as the bell's Workflow runs dialog does, or add role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby pointing at the h3, move focus to Cancel on open, and close on Escape. Extend the spec to press Escape and assert the dialog closes, and to assert getByRole('alertdialog', { name: 'Sign out of this browser?' }).
findings.verifier: ProfileMenu.tsx:782 renders a plain <Overlay>. shared/ui/portal.tsx shows Overlay is only a portalled div, with no role, aria-modal, labelling, focus move, trap or Escape. The only Escape handler in the file (line 228) belongs to the menu. PageDialog uses useFocusTrap, role=dialog and aria-modal, so the contrast holds. Moving to the shared AlertDialog, as NotificationBell does for Workflow runs, is the right fix.

findings.spec: multi-user.spec.ts: a mention from another user raises the notification bell
findings.what: The bell button has aria-label="Notifications". That label replaces its visible text, including the unread badge, so a screen reader announces "Notifications" whether there are 0 or 12 unread. The button also has no aria-expanded for the panel it toggles.
findings.why: For a screen-reader user, the unread count is the whole point of the bell. The spec checks the badge text visually with toContainText("1"), which passes while the accessible name stays wrong.
findings.suggestion: Remove the aria-label so the name comes from the visible text, or set aria-label={unread > 0 ? `Notifications, ${unread} unread` : "Notifications"}, and add aria-expanded={open}. Have the test assert getByRole('button', { name: /Notifications, 1 unread/ }).
findings.verifier: NotificationBell.tsx:92 sets aria-label="Notifications" on a button whose visible content includes the unread badge, so the count never reaches its accessible name. There is no aria-expanded for the panel. Prefer the explicit label (`Notifications, N unread`) over just removing aria-label: without it the name becomes "Notifications 1", which is ambiguous.

findings.spec: a11y-pilot.spec.ts: a project's Overview with its milestones, and the Milestones tab, are accessible
findings.what: The "pilot" axe spec seeds a raise-era sale record (floorPrice, tickSpacing, tokenPlan mode dao, unlocks.milestones) and scans MilestoneSummaryCard ("The team's tokens unlock with 2 milestones… holders can object… posts a bond"). That card belongs to the raise flow, not the pilot. No phone or axe spec opens a contributor project (ContributorKit record): its Overview, work areas, Needs you, the Contributions tab, or the /start/contributor wizard. a11y-phone visits /launchpad and /projects, but those are hidden in the pilot build.
findings.why: The pilot is contributor-only (VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1), so the screens pilot testers actually use have no accessibility or phone-layout gate, while the gate spends its time on screens they never see.
findings.suggestion: Replace a11y-pilot's milestone fixture with the ContributorKit fixture from contributor-project.spec.ts. Scan the contributor Overview, a work area with Ways to help, and the Needs you list in both schemes. Leave the start/contributions scans where they already are. In a11y-phone, swap /launchpad and /projects for a contributor project page and /start/contributor, or move the raise pages to a later-only list.
findings.verifier: Part of the claim is false. contributor-project.spec.ts already runs axe on the contributor start page (line 281), the Contributions tab (367) and suggested work (447), and launchpad-shouldfix-work.spec.ts scans the work tab and the turn-down form. So contributor screens do have a desktop light-scheme axe gate. What is true: a11y-pilot seeds a raise-era sale record and scans MilestoneSummaryCard, which only shows on raise-era Overviews. a11y-phone visits /launchpad and /projects, both hidden in the pilot build. No dark-scheme or phone scan covers a contributor project, work areas or Needs you.

findings.spec: responsive-surfaces.spec.ts / a11y.spec.ts / a11y-phone.spec.ts (whole files)
findings.what: All responsive and axe specs run only in the smoke project, against the default build, which offers raises and AI helpers. Nothing runs them against the contributor-only build the pilot ships. About a third of these tests target surfaces the pilot hides: "fleet view fits", "org view fits", "launchpad directory fits", "launchpad create dialog fits", "launchpad detail fits", "an unavailable chain read reports no amount", "repository browser fits", and in a11y.spec "the repository browser", "the launchpad", "the org view" and "the agents view".
findings.why: The gate's time and signal go to screens the pilot never shows. Layout and axe regressions that only appear in the contributor-only layout (different nav, hidden helpers, different Discover header) are never caught.
findings.suggestion: Add a playwright project that serves a VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1 build (E2E_DIST already exists) and runs a11y-phone, a11y-pilot and the pilot subset of responsive-surfaces. Move the raise-only and helper-only tests into the --later set, as mvp-gate.sh already does for the raise journeys.
findings.verifier: playwright.config.ts has a single smoke project that serves the default dist, which offers raises (raisesOffered, read via beyondContributorProjects). The only scripts that build with VITE_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY=1 are web-social-e2e.sh (real-relay social specs only), web-passkey-contributor-e2e.sh and web-screen-audit.sh (screenshots, no axe or overflow check). None of them runs the responsive or axe specs. The listed tests (fleet, org, launchpad directory, create and detail, repos, agents) target surfaces that build-gates.ts hides in the pilot. E2E_DIST and E2E_CONTRIBUTOR_ONLY already exist as hooks, so the suggested contributor-only project is cheap to add.

findings.spec: multi-user.spec.ts: a relay that drops the history query reports a failure, not an empty channel; a client recovers after its connection drops
findings.what: Several room error strings sound like the protocol rather than plain speech: "The server did not answer the history query for #general, so this channel is not known to be empty." (873), "Showing live messages only. The server didn't answer the history request for this channel." (858), and the live chip's tooltip "Live updates from the server have stopped; the client keeps retrying." (723).
findings.why: "History query", "not known to be empty" and "the client" are engineering terms. A newcomer cannot tell what happened or what to do, and the copy standard requires errors to say what happened and what to do next.
findings.suggestion: 873: "We couldn't load the messages in #general. Check your connection and try again." 858: "Older messages didn't load. New ones will still appear. Reload the page to try again." 723: "New messages aren't arriving right now. We'll keep trying to reconnect."

findings.spec: multi-user.spec.ts: a wiki page query the relay drops is reported, not shown as no pages; an archived community explains why its channels do not load
findings.what: Wiki: "The server did not answer the wiki page query, so there is no known list of pages." (415) and "Showing saved pages. The server didn't answer." (396). Community: "<host> did not answer the channel query." (CommunityHomePage.tsx:51) and "This community is archived, so its channels are no longer served." (CommunityHomePage.tsx:222).
findings.why: These have the same machine-sounding "query" and "served" phrasing. They also show a raw hostname as the subject of the sentence.
findings.suggestion: 415: "We couldn't load the pages. Try again in a moment." 396: "These pages may be out of date. We couldn't reach the server." 51: "We couldn't reach this community. Try again in a moment." 222: "This community has been archived. Its rooms can no longer be opened."

findings.spec: multi-user.spec.ts: an archived community explains why its channels do not load
findings.what: An archived community still renders QueryError with the title "Couldn't load this community", a Try again button and the sign-in recovery block, even though the page already knows the reads fail on purpose.
findings.why: Retrying can never work, and "Couldn't load" plus a retry reads as a temporary fault. People will keep pressing it or report a bug.
findings.suggestion: When entry?.archived is set, render a plain notice titled "This community is archived", with no retry and no SignRecovery, and keep only the "All communities" link. Extend the test to assert there is no Try again button.
findings.verifier: CommunityHomePage.tsx:213-229 swaps in the archived description but still renders CommunityLoadState. That shows QueryError titled "Couldn't load this community", plus onRetry and the SignRecovery block. For an archived community the reads fail by design, so the retry and sign-in recovery cannot help. The multi-user test only asserts the archived text. A dedicated notice without retry is the right fix.

findings.spec: responsive.spec.ts / multi-user.spec.ts (sidebar, timeline, work board, search)
findings.what: The same thing has two names. The sidebar is labelled "Channels", with "Load more channels" and "Couldn't load more channels" (ChannelSidebar.tsx:252, 278, 302), "No messages yet in general.", and "No channel" / aria-label "Channel" on the task form (WorkBoard.tsx:425-428). Elsewhere the same screens say "Edit room", "Share this room", "Link to this room copied" and "fills with rooms and shared pages". The sidebar entry is "Wiki" while the empty state calls them "shared pages", and the search box says "Search messages…" (CommunityShell.tsx:424) although it also finds wiki pages.
findings.why: Within one session a newcomer sees "channel", "room", "wiki" and "shared pages" and has to guess whether they are different things.
findings.suggestion: Use "room" everywhere: "Rooms", "Load more rooms", "Couldn't load more rooms", "No room", "No messages yet in #general". Pick one name for the pages ("Pages" is plainer than "Wiki") and use it in the sidebar, the empty state and search hits (search-hits.ts:77 "wiki page" becomes "page"). Change the placeholder to "Search messages and pages…".

findings.spec: multi-user.spec.ts: an attachment over the limit is refused without an upload attempt
findings.what: "This file is 11 MB, over the 10 MB limit for image/gif." The message shows a raw MIME type to the user.
findings.why: "image/gif" and "video/mp4" are internals, and the sentence does not say what to do next.
findings.suggestion: Map the type to a word (GIF, picture, video, file) and add an action: "This GIF is 11 MB. GIFs can be up to 10 MB, so try a smaller one." If no type is known: "This file is 120 MB. Files can be up to 100 MB."

findings.spec: multi-user.spec.ts: an edit and a reaction reach the other client live
findings.what: An edited message (kind 40003 overlay) replaces the text in place with no "edited" marker. The row shows only the original timestamp. The test confirms the reader sees "Edited wording" and never "Original wording", so the change is silent.
findings.why: Rooms are where people agree on work and paste decisions (DecisionEmbeds renders in the message body). A silent edit can change what someone appeared to agree to, and other readers cannot tell.
findings.suggestion: When overlayContent is set, show a small "(edited)" after the time, with the edit time in its title. Have the test assert the marker appears on the reader's row.
findings.verifier: ChannelTimeline.tsx has no "edited" marker: overlayContent silently replaces the content (line 225), and overlays.edits is passed in as content only. The "(edited)" marker should go in. One note: the edits map holds only the text, so showing the edit time in a title means carrying the 40003 event's created_at through as well. Without that, use a plain "(edited)" first.

findings.spec: a11y-pilot.spec.ts: Home's checklist is accessible for a helper and for a founder
findings.what: A checklist step's done state is shown only visually: an aria-hidden check icon and a line-through. Every unfinished step's action is a link or button named just "Go".
findings.why: A screen-reader user hears three steps with no done or not-done state and three identical "Go" controls, so the checklist is unusable without sight. axe does not flag either problem at the serious or critical level, which is why the spec passes.
findings.suggestion: Add visually hidden text such as {step.done ? "Done: " : "To do: "} before the label, and give each Go aria-label={`Go: ${step.label}`}, or make the label itself the link. Assert getByRole('link', { name: 'Go: Look at a project' }) in the spec.
findings.verifier: HomeHero.tsx:238-280: the check circle is aria-hidden, done state is only a line-through class, and every unfinished step's control is named "Go" (both the Button and the Link variants). There is no sr-only state and no aria-label. The fix is as suggested. Making the step label itself the link is the simpler option.

findings.spec: a11y-pilot.spec.ts: Home's checklist is accessible for a helper and for a founder
findings.what: Step label "Add your name and a picture" with the hint "The picture is optional." The hint contradicts the label.
findings.why: The label asks for a picture and the hint then says it is not needed. The step is also ticked by a name alone (signals.named).
findings.suggestion: Label: "Add your name". Hint: "A picture helps people recognise you, but it's optional."

findings.spec: responsive-surfaces.spec.ts: notifications panel fits
findings.what: The notifications panel always shows a "Workflow runs" entry, which opens a "Workflow runs" dialog ("Recent runs, what each step did, and anything waiting for your approval"), plus ApprovalsPanel. Both are automation/agent features, and neither is gated by the contributor-only build that hides AI helpers.
findings.why: In the pilot, nobody has workflows. The first item in a newcomer's bell is a term they cannot place, and it pushes the actual mentions down.
findings.suggestion: Keep ApprovalsPanel as is. Render the Workflow runs entry only when beyondContributorProjects() is true (the same gate behind `helpers` and fleet-toggle in channels/ui/CommunityShell.tsx), or only once the community has at least one run. Update the responsive "notifications panel fits" spec to assert the entry is absent in a contributor-only build.
findings.verifier: Mostly right, with one correction. ApprovalsPanel already returns null when it has nothing to show (ApprovalsPanel.tsx:31), so it costs nothing in the pilot. Only the "Workflow runs" button (NotificationBell.tsx:108-120) always shows. No web screen creates workflows (only WorkflowRunsPanel, ApprovalsPanel and the bell mention them), so pilot users can never have runs. DEPRECATION-2026-10-31 says nothing about keeping it.

findings.spec: multi-user.spec.ts: a task created by one client appears on the other's board
findings.what: The community Tasks board's "Assignee" select lists only AI helpers (useAgentRoster): "Anyone" plus agents. People cannot be picked. In the contributor-only build no helpers exist, so the select only ever shows "Anyone". The header reads "3 items · 2 tasks · 1 issue", and the board mixes in git "Issues" (an All types / Tasks / Issues filter), although repositories are hidden in the pilot.
findings.why: This is a dead control and developer vocabulary on a board meant for non-technical teams. It also overlaps with projects' own work areas and Needs you, which DEPRECATION #15 meant to give one meaning for "work".
findings.suggestion: Fill Assignee from room members and recent authors (the same source as useMentionCandidates), or hide it when the list is empty. In the contributor-only build, hide the Issues type filter and replace the counts with "3 tasks". Consider whether this community board should link to the project's work areas instead of being a second task system.
findings.verifier: WorkBoard.tsx:437-447: Assignee options are only "Anyone" plus useAgentRoster agents, so in the contributor-only build (no helpers) it is a dead control. The type pills (All types/Tasks/Issues, line 402-410) and the item/task/issue counts (line ~361) are always shown. The Tasks toggle in CommunityShell is not gated by helpers, so pilot users see this board. Filling Assignee from people (useMentionCandidates) or hiding it when empty, and hiding Issues in the pilot, are reasonable fixes. Whether to fold the board into work areas is a product question for the owner.

findings.spec: responsive-surfaces.spec.ts: wiki pages can be created, renamed and deleted
findings.what: Page names are forced into slugs. Typing "Release Notes" shows "Saved as release-notes", the placeholder is "release-notes", the page list shows the slug, and the toast says "Moved shared-page to Recently deleted" (use-wiki-removal.tsx:106).
findings.why: Lower-case hyphenated names are a developer convention. People without technical backgrounds expect the title they typed to be the title they see.
findings.suggestion: Keep the typed title for display (in a title tag or the first heading) and use the slug only for the address. Change the placeholder to "Release notes" and drop the "Saved as …" hint, or say "Link: …/release-notes". The toast becomes "Moved \"Release notes\" to Recently deleted".
findings.verifier: PageDialog.tsx: the placeholder is "release-notes" and the hint reads `Saved as ${slug}`. KnowledgeIndex.tsx:42 lists page.slug, and use-wiki-removal.tsx:99/106 toasts `Discarded ${page.slug}` / `Moved ${page.slug} to Recently deleted`. The wiki toggle is not gated in the pilot. Keeping a display title, with the slug only as the address, means adding a title tag to the page event. That is a small schema change, and still the right direction.

findings.spec: responsive-surfaces.spec.ts: an unavailable chain read reports no amount
findings.what: "No chain data", with the tooltip "No chain data: <reason>." and "Live chain values."
findings.why: "Chain" is crypto jargon. Even on raise pages, a buyer wants to know whether the amount is known.
findings.suggestion: Label: "Amount unavailable". Tooltip: "We couldn't check the amount raised just now. Try again later." Use "Up to date" instead of "Live chain values."

findings.spec: multi-user.spec.ts: a reply appears threaded for the other client; a wiki page has an address that survives a reload
findings.what: The reply test proves threading by checking that the className includes "ml-8". The wiki address test (line 1081) proves selection with the class /bg-black\/10/. KnowledgeIndex already sets aria-current on the active page, and replies have no accessible marker at all.
findings.why: Both assertions break on a style change and pass if the class stays but threading breaks. They also mirror the a11y gap: a screen reader cannot tell a reply from a root message.
findings.suggestion: Wiki: expect(...).toHaveAttribute('aria-current', 'true'). Replies: render the thread as a nested list or give the reply row an accessible label such as "Reply to <name>", then assert that. Show the same name in the composer, replacing "Replying to a message" (Composer.tsx:205) with "Replying to Alice".
findings.verifier: multi-user.spec.ts:410-414 checks className includes "ml-8". Its comment says it proves "the root as its parent", but no published tag is checked. The wiki test at line ~1093 matches /bg-black\/10/. KnowledgeIndex.tsx:30 already sets aria-current="true" on the active page, so that assertion is a one-line swap. Reply rows (ChannelTimeline.tsx:218/251) carry only the ml-8 class, and the composer says "Replying to a message". The suggestion holds. For replies, also assert the published event's parent e tag.

findings.spec: responsive-surfaces.spec.ts: notifications panel fits / fleet view fits / work board fits / org view fits / launchpad create dialog fits
findings.what: These tests click a toggle and immediately call expectNoOverflow without waiting for the surface to appear. If the view fails to render, shows a skeleton, or the click misses, the page is narrower than ever and the test passes. The file also re-implements mockRelay (twice: lines 94 and 397), its own overflow helper (duplicating helpers/layout.ts expectNoSidewaysScroll), and a desktop-width CRUD test ("wiki pages can be created, renamed and deleted", line 476) that has nothing to do with responsiveness.
findings.why: Overflow checks that cannot fail when the screen is missing prove little, and the duplicated fixtures drift from mock-relay.ts.
findings.suggestion: Before measuring, assert that a landmark of each surface is visible (the panel's "Nothing new." or an item, the Tasks heading, the dialog title). Use createMockRelay and expectNoSidewaysScroll from helpers/layout.ts, and move the wiki CRUD test into a wiki spec. Also drop the dead api.github.com mock in "invite landing fits" (line 521): DESKTOP_APP is off by default, so there is no release lookup.
findings.verifier: responsive-surfaces.spec.ts:261-295: notifications, fleet, work and org each click a toggle, then call expectNoOverflow right away with no visibility check, so a missing surface passes. The launchpad create test (382-389) has the same pattern. The file defines its own mockRelay (line 98) plus inline route and routeWebSocket fixtures in the wiki test (~397-420), and its own overflow/expectNoOverflow helpers. The wiki CRUD test (476) runs at 1280px and is not about layout. The api.github.com route in the invite test is dead: InvitePage only uses the buzz-download release lookup when DESKTOP_APP is set.

findings.spec: a11y-phone.spec.ts: the top-level screens are accessible and fit on a phone
findings.what: One test loops over 10 pages with a fixed 600 ms sleep each and a 180 s timeout. The first failing page stops the loop, so later pages go unchecked, and the pages run one after another instead of in parallel.
findings.why: A single regression hides any others behind it, and the test is slow and order-dependent.
findings.suggestion: Generate one test per page and scheme (for (const [name, path] of PAGES) test(...)) and replace waitForTimeout(600) with waiting for the page's heading. Failures then report every broken screen and run in parallel.
findings.verifier: a11y-phone.spec.ts loops over 10 PAGES inside one test per scheme, with test.setTimeout(180_000) and waitForTimeout(600) per page. The first failing expect stops the loop, so later pages are never checked. One test per page and scheme, each waiting for a page landmark, is strictly better. Note: workers is 1 in the config, so the parallel-run gain is small. Better failure reporting is the main win.

findings.spec: multi-user.spec.ts: a mention from another user raises the notification bell; a locked passkey identity does not mint a second key
findings.what: The mention test opens a second "author" context that never does anything; the mention is injected with relay.deliver, so it is not cross-user at all. The passkey test ends with expect(getByRole('alert').first()).toBeVisible(), which any alert on the page satisfies, and uses a fixed waitForTimeout(4_000). The suite also has fixed waits of 12 s (backoff) and 6 s (wiki auto-save).
findings.why: The mention test's name promises an end-to-end path that the test does not exercise. The passkey assertion would pass on an unrelated error. The fixed waits add about 22 s per run.

Keep one relay.deliver case only if a non-UI author is needed, and rename it to match. Passkey test: first wait for the specific locked-passkey refusal and its Unlock control, then read localStorage to check no nsec was minted. That replaces the 4s sleep with a real sync point. Wiki auto-save: wait for the saved state, or the published event in the relay, instead of 6s. Try page.clock for the 12s backoff only if it works with the mock relay's reconnect timers. Otherwise leave it.
findings.verifier: Real. The mention test's author context does nothing; the mention comes from relay.deliver with pubkey "c"*64. The passkey test ends on getByRole("alert").first(), which any alert satisfies. Fixed waits of 12s (line 496), 6s (753) and 4s (896) exist. Two parts of the suggestion need care. The 4s wait guards a negative claim (no nsec gets minted), so it should not simply be deleted. And page.clock with the WebSocket reconnect pump in the mock relay is untested and could make the backoff test fragile.
